discovery.summary: Analyze an Animation Sequence's motion from its own frames: how far and fast the root travels and turns, when each foot is planted and how fast a planted foot still moves, how closely the last frame meets the first, and the bones with the sharpest rotation spikes.
whenToUse: Footstep notifies must go where the feet land (feet[].contacts are the planted intervals in seconds).
A walk or run must match the character's movement speed: an in-place clip's plantedSpeed is the ground speed it implies; a root-motion clip's should be near 0.
A clip must be checked for a clean loop or for pops before it is used.
whenNotToUse: Only the length, notifies or curves are needed (use get_animation_info).
A character playing in a running game must be measured (use control_actor get_transform motion).

assetPath.description: Animation Sequence asset path, e.g. /Game/Anims/A_Run (a montage or blend space is refused: analyze the sequences it plays).

feet.description: Foot bones to check (default every bone whose name holds foot but not ik, e.g. foot_l and foot_r).

contactHeight.description: cm above a foot's lowest point that still counts as planted (default 5).

maxSamples.description: Frames sampled, spread evenly with the first and last always in (default 300, at most 2000; a shorter clip samples every frame).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

rootMotion.description: The root bone's path in component space (in-place clips stay at 0).

enabled.description: Whether the sequence has root motion enabled.

displacement.description: From the first to the last frame, [x, y, z] in cm.

loop.description: Last frame against the first, every bone but the root in its parent's space: near 0 is a clean loop.

worstBone.description: The bone with the largest rotation.

contacts.description: Planted intervals as [start, end] in seconds (at most 32).

plantedRatio.description: Share of sampled frames the foot is planted (0-1).

plantedSpeed.description: Average horizontal speed of the planted foot in cm/s: the ground speed an in-place clip implies, or foot slide on a root-motion clip.

pops.description: The three bones whose rotation spikes fastest: a pop shows as one far above the rest.

examples.title: Analyze an Animation Sequence's motion from its own frames: how far and fast the root travels and turns, when each foot is planted and how fast a planted foot still moves, how closely the last frame meets the first, and the bones with the sharpest rotation spikes.

output.message: A_Run: 0.70 s, 22 frames; the root travels 0.0 cm (0.0 cm/s); 2 foot bone(s); loop seam 0.05 cm, 0.4 deg.

discovery.summary: Delete animation assets by path (artifacts), each closed in any editor and garbage collected first. Paths that do not exist are listed under missing; when none of them existed the call still succeeds, saying nothing needed removing. No undo and no reference check: an asset others still use leaves them pointing at nothing.
whenToUse: Assets made for a test or a discarded attempt (a temporary Anim Blueprint, a trial montage) must go.
whenNotToUse: The work should be kept.
Other assets may still use them: check their referencers first (asset.inspect_asset with lookup=dependencies and referencers=true).

discovery.summary: Change an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph, chosen by edit. add_layered_blend_per_bone adds a Layered Blend Per Bone node that layers each blend pose over the bones its branch filters name (a bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND) and names the node for wiring. set_value sets a node setting (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment) or the animation an asset player plays, by node name or nodeId, and reads it back; NODE_NOT_FOUND lists the nodes and AMBIGUOUS_NODE the matches. Both save unless save is false.
whenToUse: edit=add_layered_blend_per_bone: Part of the body must play another animation than the rest, such as attacking or aiming while walking.
edit=set_value: A graph node property must change.
edit=set_value: A Sequence Player or Blend Space Player must play a different animation.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_layered_blend_per_bone: A whole-body blend between poses (add_blend_node).
edit=set_value: Use add_blend_node.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

layerSetup.description: One entry per blend pose, in pin order: [{ branchFilters: [{ boneName, blendDepth }] }]. A filter takes boneName and every bone under it from that blend pose over the base pose: blendDepth 0 (default) at full weight at once, N ramps the weight up over N bones down the chain (the named bone gets 1/N), and a negative depth on a bone under an earlier filter takes that branch back out (-1 removes it). Every bone must be on the Animation Blueprint's skeleton (BONE_NOT_FOUND).

boneName.description: Shorthand for one layer filtering this bone and its children; ignored when layerSetup is sent.

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

nodeName.description: The node: its object name (AnimGraphNode_SequencePlayer_0), its GUID (the nodeId create_node, add_state and inspect_graph report), or a custom name set in its NodeComment or its title when one node has it. Looks in the AnimGraph and in the state machines and states under it; a name that matches nothing answers NODE_NOT_FOUND listing every node (nodes), and one that matches several AMBIGUOUS_NODE listing them (candidates).

nodeId.description: The node GUID; an alternative to nodeName.

propertyName.description: The property: a member of the node's settings struct (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, Sequence) or of the graph node (NodeComment), with dots for a nested one (Node.PlayRate). On an asset player the asset property (Sequence, BlendSpace) is written through the node's own setter and read back, and fails when the node did not take it; any other property is written by reflection and its stored value read back.

value.description: The value: a number, boolean or string, an {x,y,z} or {r,g,b,a} object for a struct, or for an asset property the asset path (/Game/Anims/A_Idle).

edit.description: Which configure anim graph node variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeName.description: Object name of the node made.

nodeId.description: GUID of the node made: the nodeId graph edits take.

layerCount.description: Blend poses with branch filters set.

saved.description: Boolean parameter.

propertyName.description: Echoes propertyName.

value.description: The value now stored, read back from the node: the asset path for an asset property.

examples.title: Change an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph, chosen by edit. add_layered_blend_per_bone adds a Layered Blend Per Bone node that layers each blend pose over the bones its branch filters name (a bone not on the skeleton is BONE_NOT_FOUND) and names the node for wiring. set_value sets a node setting (Alpha, PlayRate, bLoopAnimation, NodeComment) or the animation an asset player plays, by node name or nodeId, and reads it back; NODE_NOT_FOUND lists the nodes and AMBIGUOUS_NODE the matches. discovery.summary: Sockets on a skeleton (skeletonPath; a skeletal mesh path uses its skeleton), chosen by socketOp; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create (add) puts socketName on attachBoneName, which both require, at relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale (default zero, zero and one); a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND and a taken name SOCKET_EXISTS. configure (modify) changes an existing socket: attachBoneName moves it, and relativeLocation, relativeRotation and relativeScale replace only the parts given; a missing socket is SOCKET_NOT_FOUND and a call naming nothing to change is refused.
whenToUse: socketOp=configure|modify: Socket offset must change.
socketOp=add|create: An attach point is needed.
whenNotToUse: socketOp=add|create: Use an existing socket.

relativeLocation.description: Socket location relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

relativeRotation.description: Socket rotation relative to its attach bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].

relativeScale.description: Socket scale relative to its attach bone as [x, y, z].

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

socketOp.description: Which configure socket variant to run; omit for 'configure'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Make a placed skeletal-mesh actor drive as a wheeled vehicle (Chaos Vehicles): adds an MCP_VehicleMovement4W movement component when it has none, then sets the wheels (replacing them), engine, transmission, mass and drag. Each value is set by name, so one an engine version lacks is skipped without a word; only that actor changes, and nothing is saved until its level is.
whenToUse: A car or truck actor (a skeletal mesh with wheel bones) must be set up to drive.
whenNotToUse: A skeletal mesh only has to simulate physics, not drive (use setup_physics_simulation).
Every copy of a vehicle Blueprint should drive: add the vehicle movement component in the Blueprint (manage_blueprint edit_scs).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

vehicleType.description: Vehicle movement to set up; only a wheeled vehicle is supported (default WheeledVehicle4W).

wheels.description: Wheel setups, replacing the existing ones: [{ boneName, offset {x,y,z}, radius, width, friction }].

engine.description: Engine settings: maxRPM, maxTorque, gears (forward gear count).

transmission.description: Transmission settings: finalDrive and forward gearRatios.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Create an animation asset: a sequence, montage, blend space (1D/2D), aim offset, pose asset from a sequence, or procedural animation.
whenToUse: kind=asset|blend_space: An animation asset or graph must be authored.
kind=sequence: A keyframed clip is needed.
kind=montage: A playable montage is needed.
kind=blend_space_1d: A single-axis blend is needed.
kind=blend_space_2d: A two-axis blend is needed.
kind=aim_offset: Aim blending by look direction is needed.
kind=pose_library: Named poses (facial shapes, hand poses, correctives) must be blended by name in an Animation Blueprint.
kind=procedural: A runtime-authored animation is needed.
whenNotToUse: kind=aim_offset: Use a blend space.
kind=pose_library: A playable clip is needed; use kind sequence or montage.
kind=procedural: Use a static sequence.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

path.description: Canonical /Game output path for the created asset.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

animationPath.description: Sequence the montage plays; its skeleton is used when skeletonPath is omitted.

slotName.description: Name of the montage slot (default DefaultSlot).

sourceAnimationPath.description: AnimSequence whose key frames become the poses; its skeleton is used.

poseNames.description: Distinct names for the poses in frame order; frames without a name keep the engine default name.

additive.description: Make the poses additive against pose 0, as facial and corrective poses are (default false).

boneTracks.description: Bone tracks to key: [{ boneName, frames: [{ frame, rotationDelta?: {pitch,yaw,roll}, rotation?: {pitch,yaw,roll}|{x,y,z,w}, location?: {x,y,z}, scale?: {x,y,z} }] }]. frame runs 0 to numFrames inclusive. Only the poses that matter need keys: frames between two keys of a channel are blended (rotation slerped), frames before its first key or after its last hold that key. Channels left out keep the reference pose of that bone, so a rotation-only track poses without collapsing the skeleton. Prefer rotationDelta, which bends the bone relative to its rest orientation; plain rotation replaces the local rotation outright and needs the rest orientation to already be known. Calling it again with the name of an existing clip re-keys that clip from empty (its additive settings are kept).

kind.description: Which create animation asset variant to run; omit for 'asset'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

poseNames.description: Pose names read back from the asset.

saved.description: Whether the pose asset was saved.

skeletonSaved.description: UE 5.0 to 5.2: whether the skeleton, which holds the pose curve names there, was saved.

discovery.summary: Create or tune a physical material: friction, bounce (restitution), density and how two touching surfaces combine them. A mesh takes it through control_actor edit_component property PhysMaterialOverride (edit_scs set_property on a class template).
whenToUse: An object must bounce, slide or grip differently: a bouncy ball (restitution 0.9, restitutionCombineMode Max), an ice floor (friction 0.05, frictionCombineMode Min).
A physical material must be adjusted: the same name and path tune it in place.
whenNotToUse: A character slides or grips the ground: use manage_character set_movement_property (ground friction, braking).

name.description: Asset name, e.g. PM_Bouncy.

path.description: Folder for the asset (default /Game/Physics).

friction.description: Kinetic friction, 0 (ice) to 1 and above (rubber); the engine default is 0.7.

staticFriction.description: Friction at rest, before a body starts to slide.

density.description: Density in g/cm3, which sets mass from volume (water is 1).

frictionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their friction: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

restitutionCombineMode.description: How this surface and the one it touches combine their bounce: Min lets the slipperier (or deader) one win, Max the grippier (or bouncier) one; Average when not set.

physicalMaterialPath.description: Object path of the physical material.

created.description: True when this call made it; false when it tuned one already there.

discovery.summary: Edit an Animation Blueprint graph: blend, cached-pose and slot nodes, state machines, states, transitions and transition rules, blend trees. Any other AnimGraph node (Two Bone IK, Modify Bone, Blend Space Player) is created by class with manage_blueprint edit_graph create_node.
whenToUse: edit=add_blend_node: Graph needs a blend node.
edit=add_cached_pose: Pose reuse optimization needed.
edit=add_slot_node: Montages (attacks, reloads, emotes) must play on a character whose Animation Blueprint has no Slot node for their slot.
edit=create_state_machine: State-driven animation is needed.
edit=add_state_machine: A state machine must be embedded.
edit=add_state: A new animation state is needed.
edit=add_transition: States must connect.
edit=set_transition_rules: Transition condition must change.
edit=set_transition_rules: A state machine must actually be able to leave a state: author the condition here after add_transition.
edit=delete_transition: A transition was authored between the wrong two states.
edit=delete_transition: A transition is dead weight and its rule graph should go with it.
edit=create_blend_tree: Several animations must be switchable through one blend node in an AnimBlueprint.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_cached_pose: Inline pose suffices.
edit=add_slot_node: The montage asset itself is made (create_montage).
edit=create_state_machine: A single graph suffices.
edit=delete_transition: The state itself must go, not just the transition.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

slotName.description: Slot name.

groupName.description: Slot group a new slot joins on the skeleton (default DefaultGroup). Montages in one group interrupt each other; a slot already on the skeleton keeps its group.

transitions.description: Transitions to create between the listed states, as [{ sourceState, targetState }].

stateMachineName.description: Target state machine name inside the Animation Blueprint.

animations.description: Animation asset paths to play in this state; one Sequence Player is created per entry and the first drives the state Result pose. Without it the state is created empty and the character holds its reference pose.

crossfadeDuration.description: Transition blend duration in seconds. blendTime is accepted as an alias.

priorityOrder.description: Evaluation order when several transitions out of one state can fire on the same frame; the lowest wins.

automaticRule.description: Fire the transition when the source state's sequence player reaches the end of its animation instead of testing a condition. Left alone when omitted.

bidirectional.description: Whether the transition also applies from toState back to fromState. Left alone when omitted.

conditionVariable.description: Animation Blueprint variable the transition rule tests, e.g. Speed or bFalling. Without it the rule graph is left unconnected, which reads as false forever and the state machine never leaves its entry state.

conditionComparison.description: How conditionVariable is tested: greater (default), less, greater_equal, less_equal for a numeric variable; true or false for a bool.

conditionValue.description: Right-hand value for a numeric conditionComparison (default 0). Ignored for true/false.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

treeName.description: Comment/name for the blend node (alias of name).

connectToOutput.description: Wire the blend node into the AnimGraph output pose (default true).

edit.description: Which edit anim graph variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: The slot name the node plays.

groupName.description: The slot group the slot is in on the skeleton.

nodeName.description: Object name of the node made.

nodeId.description: GUID of the node made: the nodeId graph edits take.

saved.description: Whether the Animation Blueprint reached disk.

skeletonSaved.description: Whether the skeleton, given a new slot group, reached disk.

animationsApplied.description: One entry per created Sequence Player. Only the first can be connected to the state Result pose.

animationsFailed.description: Requested animation paths that could not be loaded.

condition.description: The rule that was written into the transition graph. Absent means no conditionVariable was given, so the transition stays false and the state is never left.

deleted.description: True when the transition and its rule graph were removed.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

location.description: Bone location relative to its parent; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

rotation.description: Bone rotation relative to its parent as [pitch, yaw, roll]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

scale.description: Bone scale as [x, y, z]; left out, the bone keeps its own at this frame.

value.description: Property value (any type).

createIfMissing.description: Create the curve when the sequence does not have it (default true).

notifyClass.description: AnimNotify (or AnimNotifyState) class name; prefixed with AnimNotify_/AnimNotifyState_ automatically when missing.

time.description: Trigger time in seconds, used when frame is omitted.

trackIndex.description: Notify track index within the animation sequence.

startFrame.description: First frame of the notify state range.

endFrame.description: Last frame of the notify state range.

additiveAnimType.description: NoAdditive (default) plays the clip as a full pose. LocalSpaceAdditive keeps only its difference from the base pose and adds that on top of whatever plays under it (a Sequencer section on another row, Apply Additive in an Animation Blueprint). MeshSpaceAdditive adds rotations in mesh space, for aim offsets; Sequencer cannot play it.

basePoseType.description: What the additive difference is taken from (default RefPose): RefPose = the skeleton reference pose, AnimScaled = basePoseAnimation frame by frame, AnimFrame = one frame (basePoseFrame) of basePoseAnimation.

basePoseFrame.description: Frame used as the additive base pose.

basePoseAnimation.description: Animation sequence to take the additive base pose from.

forceRootLock.description: Whether root motion is force-locked to the reference pose.

length.description: New length in seconds, used when numFrames is omitted.

frameRate.description: Frames per second; the sequence keeps its current rate when omitted.

edit.description: Which edit animation variant to run.

discovery.summary: Create a physics asset or edit it, chosen by edit; each change is saved unless save is false (saved). create builds bodies and joints from skeletalMeshPath as the editor's Create Physics Asset does, at outputPath (or name in path; default <mesh>_PhysicsAsset beside the mesh): geomType Capsule (default), Box, Sphere, TaperedCapsule (cloth only), SingleConvexHull or MultiConvexHull, any other name refused; bones shorter than minBoneSize get no body unless bodyForAll; createConstraints joins the bodies; assignToMesh (default false) makes the mesh use it; a build that makes no body is refused (BODY_GENERATION_FAILED). add_body gives boneName a Capsule (default), Sphere or Box shape sized by radius and length or width, depth and height, placed by center and rotation; a bone that already has a body gets the shape added to it (created false), and a bone the skeleton lacks is BONE_NOT_FOUND. configure_body (modify_body) sets mass (kg, above 0, as the body's mass override), linearDamping, angularDamping, collisionEnabled and simulatePhysics (true simulates with the ragdoll, false is Kinematic and follows the animation), and refuses a call that sets none of them. add_constraint joins bodyA and bodyB with a joint Limited to 45 degrees on every axis (both bodies must exist, BODY_NOT_FOUND; a second joint on the pair is CONSTRAINT_EXISTS); set_constraint changes the pair's joint or makes one; configure_constraint_limits sets swing1, swing2 and twist angles and motions from limits. assign makes skeletalMeshPath (or meshPath) use physicsAssetPath and saves the mesh.

length.description: Capsule length between the end caps (default 20).

rotation.description: Box or capsule rotation relative to the bone as [pitch, yaw, roll].

discovery.summary: Edit a skeleton (skeletonPath), chosen by edit. add_bone adds boneName under parentBoneName (needed once the skeleton has bones; a taken name is BONE_EXISTS) at location, rotation and scale relative to the parent. set_bone_parent moves boneName under parentBoneName (UE 5.3 and later): its own descendants are refused, and the parent it already has changes nothing (changed false). discovery.summary: Remove part of a skeleton or physics asset, chosen by element. bone removes boneName from the skeleton (UE 5.3 and later): with removeChildren its whole branch goes, otherwise its children move up to its parent, and the root bone is refused. socket removes socketName from the skeleton (a socket defined on a mesh is not found here). physics_body removes the body of boneName from physicsAssetPath together with every constraint that uses it. A missing bone, socket or body is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: element=bone: A bone must be removed.
element=socket: An attach point must be taken off a skeleton.
element=physics_body: A bone should no longer simulate.
whenNotToUse: element=bone: Keep the bone.
element=socket: The socket transform should change; use configure_socket.
element=physics_body: The body only needs different parameters (use configure_physics_body).

removeChildren.description: Whether child bones are removed with the target bone.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

element.description: Which remove skeleton element variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

remainingSockets.description: Number of sockets left on the asset after the call.

remainingBodies.description: Number of physics bodies left on the asset after the call.

A missing bone, socket or body is refused. Saved unless save is false (saved).

kind=rig: IK retargeting source needed.
kind=retargeter: Retarget between two skeletons.

kind=rig: Use create_control_rig.
kind=retargeter: Single skeleton.
kind=chain_mapping: The retargeter does not exist yet (kind retargeter).

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

skeletalMeshPath.description: Skeletal mesh the IK Rig is built on; its skeleton is used.

sourceChain.description: Source IK Rig chain that drives it; empty or None clears the mapping.

kind.description: Which setup ik variant to run; omit for 'setup'.

mapping.description: Every target chain with the source chain now driving it (None when unmapped).

whenToUse: A placed prop such as a crate or a barrel must fall, tumble or be pushable.
A skeletal mesh must simulate physics.
whenNotToUse: A vehicle is being set up (use configure_vehicle).
Every copy of a Blueprint must simulate: set bSimulatePhysics on its mesh component (manage_blueprint edit_scs).

actorName.description: A placed actor: a prop simulates on its root when that is a physics body, else on its first static mesh; a skeletal mesh actor gets a Physics Asset for its mesh.

physicsAssetName.description: Name of the generated Physics Asset.

assignToMesh.description: Whether the generated Physics Asset is assigned to the mesh.

bodyCount.description: Physics bodies made for the skeletal mesh.

discovery.summary: Make a skeletal actor go limp in the running game (Play or Simulate), chosen by ragdoll. setup switches every physics body of its skeletal mesh to simulate, assigning physicsAssetPath first when given; activate turns that on or off (activate, default true). A mesh with no physics asset is refused (NO_PHYSICS_ASSET), and ragdollActive reads back whether it now simulates. A Character keeps its capsule and movement running, so stop those as well for a body that falls.
whenToUse: ragdoll=setup: A skeletal actor must enter ragdoll simulation at runtime (editor build).
ragdoll=activate: Ragdoll must be switched on/off at runtime (editor build).
whenNotToUse: ragdoll=setup: Author the PhysicsAsset (use create_physics_asset).

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

physicsAssetPath.description: Physics asset to assign before simulating; the mesh default is used when omitted.

ragdoll.description: Which setup ragdoll variant to run; omit for 'setup'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

A mesh with no physics asset is refused (NO_PHYSICS_ASSET), and ragdollActive reads back whether it now simulates. A Character keeps its capsule and movement running, so stop those as well for a body that falls.

whenNotToUse: Use create_ik_retargeter to build the retargeter asset without baking.

assets.description: Canonical /Game animation asset paths to retarget.

targetMesh.description: SkeletalMesh to retarget onto. Defaults the same way as sourceMesh.

discovery.summary: Skin a static mesh to a skeleton so it deforms with the animation, producing a SkeletalMesh.
whenToUse: Clothing, armour or a prop must move with the body instead of holding its shape.
A garment downloaded as a static mesh needs to be worn.
whenNotToUse: The mesh is already a SkeletalMesh on the right skeleton.

staticMeshPath.description: StaticMesh to skin, e.g. a coat downloaded as a rigid mesh.

skeletalMeshPath.description: SkeletalMesh whose geometry to re-skin, for a dressed character whose own rig will not retarget. Its materials carry over. Use instead of staticMeshPath.

outputPath.description: Canonical /Game path for the SkeletalMesh this writes.

sourceSkeletalMesh.description: An already-skinned mesh on the same skeleton to copy weights from, such as the body the garment is worn over. Beats computing weights fresh wherever the garment hugs the body. Falls back to smooth binding when omitted.

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

weights.description: Which binding ran: 'transferred' from sourceSkeletalMesh, or 'smooth'.

discovery.summary: Delete every asset under folderPath (subfolders included; the folders stay) or the listed assetPaths, then resolve old redirectors there. An asset something outside the delete still uses is kept and listed in referenced with what uses it; deleted lists the paths actually gone.
whenToUse: Every asset under a folder, or a long list of assets, must be deleted in one call.
Old redirectors in the folders the assets are deleted from must be resolved in the same call (on by default).
whenNotToUse: An asset others still use must go anyway, breaking what uses it (use asset.delete with force).
The folder itself must be removed as well as its assets (use asset.delete with the folder path).

folderPath.description: Folder whose assets are deleted, subfolders included; the folders themselves stay. Used when assetPaths is absent; only assets the registry has already indexed are found.

assetPaths.description: Assets to delete (/Game paths); one that does not exist is skipped.

fixupRedirectors.description: Default true. After a delete that removed something, resolve the redirectors that already exist in the folders the assets were deleted from, subfolders included: their referencers are re-pointed and re-saved, then the redirectors nothing points at any more are removed. Deleting creates no redirectors, so this only cleans older ones.

success.description: False when nothing was deleted: every asset is used by others (ASSETS_REFERENCED), none of the paths exists (NO_VALID_ASSETS), or something loaded still holds them (BULK_DELETE_FAILED).

deleted.description: The paths actually gone after the delete (an empty folder replies an empty list).

requested.description: Assets found to delete, the kept ones included.

remaining.description: Paths the engine left on disk although they were not referenced.

referenced.description: Assets kept because others use them, each {path, referencedBy: the packages that use it}.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Delete two obsolete assets and clean redirectors

discovery.summary: Create a Content Browser folder at path (under /Game or another allowed root); one that exists already answers success with alreadyExisted true. An empty folder may be gone after an editor restart until an asset is saved in it.
whenToUse: A new empty folder is wanted in the content browser, for example to organise assets before moving them in.
A folder must be ensured at a path without knowing whether it exists; alreadyExisted in the reply says which it was.
whenNotToUse: An existing folder must change name or location (use asset.rename or asset.move).
The folder exists and its contents must be seen (use asset.list).

path.description: Folder path, e.g. /Game/Art/Props; a path outside the allowed roots is refused (INVALID_PATH).

discovery.summary: Create a Texture Render Target 2D asset for a scene capture or a Blueprint to draw into: width and height (default 1024, at most 8192), format (default RGBA8), saved unless save is false (saved says whether it was written). A render target already at that path is kept as it is and answered with alreadyExists and its own size; another asset there is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
whenToUse: A scene capture, or a Blueprint that draws to a texture, needs a render target asset to render into.
A render target of a chosen size and pixel format must exist at a /Game path; one already there is reported, not replaced.
whenNotToUse: A capture actor must be pointed at a target or re-captured (use build_environment.configure_scene_capture).
A texture with generated pixels such as a gradient or noise is wanted (use texture.create_texture).

name.description: Render target name.

renderTargetPath.description: Full asset path, e.g. /Game/RenderTargets/RT_Capture; replaces name and packagePath.

format.description: Render target format (default RGBA8): an ETextureRenderTargetFormat name such as R8, RG8, RGBA8, RGBA8_SRGB, R16f, RGBA16f, RGBA32f or RGB10A2, with or without RTF_; FloatRGBA and A2B10G10R10 are accepted too. Another name is refused.

save.description: Save after creation. Defaults to true.

discovery.summary: Delete one or more assets, or whole folders. A folder of thousands of assets can take minutes and reports how far it has got as it goes; when the call answers before the delete is done (task.state running), the delete carries on, so check the folder with asset.list instead of deleting again.
whenToUse: One or several assets, or a whole folder, must be removed from the project for good.
An asset should go only if nothing else uses it; a still-referenced asset is kept and reported.
whenNotToUse: A placed actor must leave the open level, not its asset (use inspect.delete_object).
The assets under a folder must go while the folder stays, with old redirectors there resolved in the same call (use asset.bulk_delete).

path.description: Single asset path (alternative to paths).

force.description: Delete an asset even when assets outside this delete still reference it (their references break). Default false: such an asset is kept and listed in referencedPaths. Folders are always deleted whole.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Delete one or more assets, or whole folders. A folder of thousands of assets can take minutes and reports how far it has got as it goes; when the call answers before the delete is done (task.state running), the delete carries on, so check the folder with asset.list instead of deleting again.

discovery.summary: Copy an asset, or a whole folder with its sub-folders, and save the copies. destinationPath is a folder (the copy keeps the source name, or takes newName), a full asset path, or a bare name beside the source; newName alone copies beside the source. A taken destination is refused (DESTINATION_EXISTS) and a missing source answers ASSET_NOT_FOUND; a folder copy skips assets whose destination is taken (duplicatedCount under assetCount). Each asset is copied on its own: what referred to the original, placed actors and the other copies included, still does. A copied Blueprint gets its Math Expressions rebound and a copied Niagara system is compiled, so both work at once.
whenToUse: An asset needs a copy to edit safely while the original stays unchanged.
A whole folder must be copied with its sub-folders and every asset in it.
whenNotToUse: The asset keeps its identity but changes name or folder (use asset.rename or asset.move).
A variant of a material with different parameter values is wanted, without copying its graph (use material.create_material_instance).

sourcePath.description: The asset to copy (a /Game package or object path), or a folder: every asset under it is copied, sub-folders kept.

destinationPath.description: Where the copy goes: a folder (one that exists, or ending in /) where it keeps the source name or takes newName, a full asset path, or a bare name, which lands beside the source.

newName.description: Name for the copy: in the destinationPath folder, or beside the source when destinationPath is left out.

saved.description: One asset: whether the copy was saved (an unsaved copy is gone after the editor restarts).

assetCount.description: Folder: the assets found under it, as far as the asset registry has indexed them.

duplicatedCount.description: Folder: how many were copied; fewer than assetCount means some destinations were taken.

savedCount.description: Folder: how many copies were saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Copy an asset, or a whole folder with its sub-folders, and save the copies. destinationPath is a folder (the copy keeps the source name, or takes newName), a full asset path, or a bare name beside the source; newName alone copies beside the source. A taken destination is refused (DESTINATION_EXISTS) and a missing source answers ASSET_NOT_FOUND; a folder copy skips assets whose destination is taken (duplicatedCount under assetCount). Each asset is copied on its own: what referred to the original, placed actors and the other copies included, still does. A copied Blueprint gets its Math Expressions rebound and a copied Niagara system is compiled, so both work at once.

discovery.summary: Add a parameter expression to a material or material function, or reset every parameter override on a material instance. To override a parameter value on an instance, use set_material_parameter.
whenToUse: edit=add_parameter: A new scalar, vector, texture or static-switch parameter must be introduced on a material or material function.
edit=reset_parameters: A material instance must return to its parent's values by dropping every parameter override.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_parameter: An existing parameter needs a new value on a material instance (use material.set_material_parameter).
edit=add_parameter: Another kind of node must be added to the material graph (use material.add_material_node).
edit=reset_parameters: Only some overrides need new values (use material.set_material_parameter).
edit=reset_parameters: A fresh instance of the parent is wanted instead (use material.create_material_instance).

value.description: Parameter value.

edit.description: Which edit material instance variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Add a parameter expression to a material or material function, or reset every parameter override on a material instance. To override a parameter value on an instance, use set_material_parameter.

discovery.summary: Export a static or skeletal mesh asset (or an animation sequence, on its preview mesh) to a file through the editor's own exporters: glb (default: one self-contained glTF binary), gltf (JSON with its buffers and textures beside it), fbx or obj. It is written under Saved/Exports unless outputPath says otherwise; the reply gives the path, the size, the files written beside it and any exporter warnings.
whenToUse: A mesh must leave the editor as a file: for Blender or another DCC tool, a web viewer, a mesh checker or a 3D printer.
An animation must be looked at or checked outside Unreal (export the sequence as glb).
whenNotToUse: A file must come into the project (use asset.import).
Only the mesh's soundness must be checked (use inspect.check_mesh, which needs no file).

assetPath.description: Asset to export, e.g. /Game/Meshes/SM_Rock or /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube. A skeletal mesh is written with its skeleton; an animation sequence is written on its skeleton's preview mesh.

format.description: File format; default glb, or the extension outputPath ends in. glb and gltf are scaled to meters with materials converted to glTF PBR; fbx and obj keep centimeters.

outputPath.description: Where to write, inside the project, project-relative or absolute: a file (Saved/Exports/Rocks/SM_Rock.glb) or a folder, which gets <asset name>.<format>. A file already there is replaced.

path.description: Absolute path of the file written.

otherFiles.description: Files the export wrote beside it, each {name, bytes}: a gltf's .bin buffers and textures, obj's UV and collision variants.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Export a mesh as glTF binary

discovery.summary: Import a file inside the project folder (sourcePath, relative to the project or absolute under it; a path outside is SECURITY_VIOLATION, a missing file SOURCE_NOT_FOUND) as an asset at destinationPath: a folder keeps the file name, an object path names it. An asset already there is replaced only with overwrite (DESTINATION_OCCUPIED otherwise): a plain file replaces it in place, keeping what points at it, while an FBX with skeleton or animation options deletes it first (REPLACE_FAILED while something still uses it). skeletonPath imports an FBX animation take onto that skeleton, or with importMesh binds the imported skeletal mesh to it. The reply names assetPath (the mesh when the file holds one), alsoImported (its takes, materials and textures) and saved (default true).
whenToUse: A source file inside the project folder (FBX, OBJ, PNG, WAV) must become an asset at a /Game path.
An FBX animation take must be imported onto an existing skeleton without importing the mesh again.

A character FBX must become a skeletal mesh bound to an existing skeleton (skeletonPath with importMesh), so it plays that skeleton's animations; createPhysicsAsset, physicsAssetPath and importMorphTargets shape the rest.
whenNotToUse: The content is a Fab listing or a downloaded Megascans pack (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing or megascans).
Ready-made assets from an engine template, plugin or downloaded pack must be copied in as they are (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).

sourcePath.description: File to import, inside the project folder: relative to it (Saved/Imports/Crate.fbx) or absolute under it; any other path is refused.

destinationPath.description: The folder the asset goes in, e.g. /Game/Imports (it keeps the source file's name), or an object path such as /Game/Chars/SK_Hero.SK_Hero to name it.

overwrite.description: Replace an asset already at the destination; without it the import is refused with DESTINATION_OCCUPIED. A plain file replaces it in place; an FBX with skeleton or animation options deletes it first, so the old asset is not reimported with its own stored settings.

save.description: Save the imported asset. Defaults to true; pass false to keep it in memory only.

importAnimations.description: Import animation takes from an FBX. Off by default, which imports mesh only.

skeletonPath.description: Existing skeleton, e.g. /Game/Chars/SK_Hero_Skeleton. Alone it imports the FBX's animation take ALONE against it (implies importAnimations); with importMesh it binds the imported skeletal mesh to it instead, so the mesh shares that skeleton's animations.

importMesh.description: With skeletonPath: import the skeletal mesh onto that skeleton (its takes too when importAnimations) instead of the take alone.

createPhysicsAsset.description: Skeletal mesh: make a physics asset for it (default true); false makes none.

physicsAssetPath.description: Skeletal mesh: an existing physics asset to use instead of making one.

importMorphTargets.description: Skeletal mesh: import its morph targets (blend shapes).

assetPath.description: The imported asset, renamed to the destination name: a mesh when the file holds one.

saved.description: Whether it was saved.

alsoImported.description: Other assets the import made (its takes, materials, textures), at most 50.

skeleton.description: Skeletal mesh: the skeleton it is bound to.

physicsAsset.description: Skeletal mesh: its physics asset (empty when none).

bones.description: Skeletal mesh: bones in its reference skeleton.

morphTargets.description: Skeletal mesh: morph targets it carries.

details.description: Operation details.

Import a character onto an existing skeleton

discovery.summary: Bring a marketplace asset into the project: add a Fab listing (it returns at once with an operationId; poll query_marketplace lookup=fab_import_status), cancel a Fab import that is queued or downloading, download a Fab asset, or import a Megascans asset.
whenToUse: marketplace=fab_listing: A Fab listing id is known and its content must be added to the project through the signed-in Fab tab.
marketplace=fab_cancel: A Fab import that is queued, or a unreal-engine pack that is downloading, must be stopped: a wrong listing, or one taking too long.
marketplace=fab_download: A signed Fab download URL is in hand and the pack must be fetched to disk; it lands in the Fab cache, not in /Game.
marketplace=megascans: A Megascans pack already downloaded by Bridge must be imported with its master materials and presets applied.
whenNotToUse: marketplace=fab_listing: The listing must first be found or judged (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=fab_listing: An import is already running and only its progress is wanted (use asset.query_marketplace with lookup=fab_import_status).
marketplace=fab_listing: The pack is already downloaded on disk and only needs copying in (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).
marketplace=fab_cancel: Only the progress of the import is wanted (use asset.query_marketplace with lookup=fab_import_status).
marketplace=fab_cancel: Assets an import already created must be removed (use asset.delete).
marketplace=fab_download: Only a listing id is known, with no signed URL (use marketplace=fab_listing, which adds the listing directly).
marketplace=fab_download: Downloads already on disk must be listed, not fetched again (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=megascans: The Megascans library index must be browsed first (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=megascans: The pack files should just be copied in as they are (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid, as it appears in a fab.com/listings/<uid> URL. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max, because it is used to build an API path.

destinationPath.description: A /Game folder to move what the import created to, for example /Game/Props/Barriers. The layout beneath the import's own folder (StaticMeshes, Materials, Textures) is kept under it. Omit to leave the import where Fab put it. The shared master materials in /Game/Fab/Materials, MaterialFunctions and Textures never move, and a unreal-engine pack is left where Fab put it.

assetName.description: The name for the import's one mesh: SM_<assetName>, or SK_ for a skeletal mesh, with its material instance and textures following (MI_<assetName>, T_<assetName>_<suffix>); a surface with no mesh is named by its one material instance. Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, 64 at most, for example ConcreteBarrier. Without destinationPath the assets are renamed where they are. Not applied when the import holds no single mesh or material instance to name; relocationNote says so.

quality.description: Quality tier of the file to fetch, for a listing that publishes one file per tier, as Megascans does: raw (the unprocessed scan, hundreds of MB), high, mid or low. Omit to take the best game-ready tier: high, else mid, low, raw. A tier the listing does not publish is refused with QUALITY_NOT_AVAILABLE, naming the tiers it does. Ignored for a listing that publishes no tiers and for a unreal-engine pack. The reply's quality, fileName and downloadBytes say which file was chosen.

combineMeshes.description: Only for source mesh formats (fbx, obj, gltf, glb, usdz) that Fab imports itself; ignored for Megascans and unreal-engine packs. Omit to leave Fab's behaviour alone: every mesh of a file is merged into ONE static mesh. false imports each mesh as its own asset: the adapter switches off Interchange's mesh combining on the pipelines Fab generated for this import, and the status read's combineMeshesApplied says whether that landed in time (COMBINE_UNSUPPORTED refuses the call when this engine gives no way to). true accepts the single merged mesh explicitly, which a scene-sized file (one mesh file of 50 MB or more) requires.

operationId.description: Operation id from the add reply (or the status read's queue). Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max.

assetId.description: Fab asset id, used as the cache key.

downloadUrl.description: Signed https download URL issued by Fab. Short-lived: a stale URL fails with DOWNLOAD_FAILED.

destinationDirectory.description: Where the pack lands. Defaults to the Fab library cache directory, which list_fab_downloads and the fabLibrary source root both read.

downloadType.description: Transfer mode: "http" or "buildpatch". BuildPatchServices is for Marketplace-era packs; pointing it at a plain URL stalls rather than failing, so it must be opted into.

payload.description: A complete Bridge export envelope: { exportPayload: [ { assetId, assetType, exportMode, exportType, folderName, name, assetPaths[] } ] }. Use this to pass through exactly what Bridge would have sent.

assetPaths.description: Absolute paths of the downloaded pack files. Used with folderName to synthesize a single-entry envelope when payload is omitted.

folderName.description: Destination folder name under /Game/Megascans. Required when synthesizing from assetPaths.

assetType.description: Bridge asset type: 3d, 3dplant, atlas or surface.

exportMode.description: Bridge export mode: normal, normal_drag or progressive.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to folderName.

marketplace.description: Which import marketplace asset variant to run.

success.description: True when Fab accepted the download. It does not mean content exists: poll fab_import_status for that.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

accepted.description: True when Fab accepted the workflow. Not the same as content existing.

operationId.description: The background import. Pass it to asset.query_marketplace lookup=fab_import_status. On QUEUE_FULL it names the import at the head of the queue instead, and on ADD_ALREADY_RUNNING the open import of this listing.

alreadyRunning.description: True when this listing was already queued or being imported and this call returned that same operation instead of starting another.

phase.description: queued when another import is running, else downloading right after Fab accepts. For alreadyRunning, the phase the operation was in.

queuePosition.description: 1-based place in the queue while phase is queued; absent otherwise.

title.description: The listing title, once Fab has been asked about it (absent while queued).

formatCode.description: Format Fab was asked to import: unreal-engine, gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz.

quality.description: Quality tier of the chosen file (raw, high, mid or low) when the listing publishes tiers, as Megascans does: the one asked for in quality, else the best game-ready one. Absent otherwise.

fileName.description: The file Fab downloads. Source formats only: a unreal-engine pack has a version name, not a file.

downloadBytes.description: Size of that file in bytes. Absent when Fab publishes none (a unreal-engine pack): absent means unknown, never zero.

versionName.description: Listing version selected for this engine.

engineExactMatch.description: False when no build of the pack declares the running engine; engineMatch says which build was taken instead.

engineMatch.description: exact, older or newer: the pack build taken against the running engine. older is the newest build for an earlier engine, newer the oldest build for a later one. Absent for a source format, or when no version declares an engine.

engineVersion.description: The engine version that build declares, for example UE_5.4.

combinesMeshes.description: True when Fab's importer merges every mesh of a file into ONE static mesh for this listing: a source mesh format that is not Megascans. False for Megascans and unreal-engine packs.

note.description: What to do next: poll the status read, do not add again.

cancelled.description: True when the cancel was accepted.

servedFromCache.description: True when the pack was already cached and no transfer occurred.

entryCount.description: Export-payload entries dispatched to the importer.

discovery.summary: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, a directory report, or a diff: its unsaved changes against the saved file, or a compare with another asset.
whenToUse: lookup=metadata: What was recorded on an asset must be read back: its registry tags and the package metadata that asset.set_metadata writes, tags included (a tag set with kind=tags shows under metadata as "true").
lookup=dependencies: Before deleting or replacing an asset, the packages, Blueprints and levels that use it must be listed.
lookup=dependencies: The packages an asset itself uses must be listed (direct ones only).
lookup=graph: The reference graph of an asset must be walked several levels deep in one call (depth is capped at 8).
lookup=validate: An asset must be confirmed to exist and load before other calls rely on it (no content, reference or data checks are run).
lookup=report: Every asset under a directory, with name, path and class, must be listed in one reply, optionally saved as a JSON file in the project.
lookup=diff: What changed in an asset since it was last saved must be known before saving or discarding it.
lookup=diff: Two versions of an asset must be compared, such as a backup copy and the current one.
whenNotToUse: lookup=metadata: The asset's own values are wanted, such as a texture size or material parameters (use texture.get_texture_info or material.get_material_info).
lookup=dependencies: The node graph inside a material or Blueprint is wanted, not package links (use asset.query_asset with lookup=graph).
lookup=graph: Only the direct packages an asset uses, or the packages that use it, are needed (use lookup=dependencies, which is cheaper).
lookup=graph: A material's package references are wanted; a plain material answers here with its expression nodes (use lookup=dependencies).
lookup=validate: Every asset in a folder must be checked for load errors (use system_control.validate_assets).
lookup=report: A paged view of one folder is enough (use asset.list); the report returns the whole tree unpaged.
lookup=diff: The asset's current values are wanted (use blueprint.get_blueprint or inspect.get_property).
lookup=diff: A level or another kind of asset must be compared; only Blueprints, DataTables and data assets are.

referencers.description: List the packages that USE this asset (Blueprints that spawn it, levels that place it) instead of the ones it uses; check this before deleting or replacing an asset.

againstPath.description: Another asset of the same kind to compare with, such as a duplicate kept as a backup. Omitted, the asset is compared with its own saved file, so the reply lists its unsaved edits.

lookup.description: Which inspect asset variant to run.

tags.description: Asset Registry tags (key-value). A tag written by set_tags appears here only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry.

metadata.description: Package metadata (key-value): what set_metadata wrote, and each set_tags tag as its name with the value "true".

details.description: Operation details.

graph.description: Adjacency map of asset path -> array of dependency paths.

maxDepth.description: Traversal depth actually used after clamping.

truncated.description: True when the walk hit the depth or node ceiling and the graph is partial.

against.description: What the asset was compared with: "saved file", or the againstPath asset.

propertyChanges.description: Saved properties that differ, at most 50: object (asset, defaults for a Blueprint's class defaults, component <name>, or row <name>), property, change (changed, added or removed) and now and saved (the other side) as text, each cut at 200 characters.

componentChanges.description: Blueprint components added, removed, or moved to another class or parent, at most 50: component, change, now and saved; a component's changed values are under propertyChanges.

graphChanges.description: Blueprint graph changes, at most 50, node moves left out: graph, change (graph added, graph removed, node added, node removed, or changed), node and nodeId when a node is named (nodeId is the live graph's node where it has one), and detail, the engine's own description.

rowChanges.description: DataTable rows added or removed, at most 50: row and change; a changed row's values are under propertyChanges.

discovery.summary: List the assets and subfolders in a folder (path), the registered content sources, or the instances of a material.
whenToUse: kind=assets: what a folder holds must be seen (subfolders included unless recursive is false).
kind=content_sources: which template, feature pack, plugin or Fab folders exist to copy content from.
kind=material_instances: which material instances use a parent material.
whenNotToUse: An asset must be found by name, class or tag anywhere in the project (use query_asset).

path.description: Canonical /Game path to list.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.
Zero-based offset into the full result set.

pagination.description: Nested pagination envelope. Top-level limit/offset take precedence when both are supplied.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous list response. Forward verbatim to resume.

recursive.description: Include the assets of every subfolder (default true); false lists only this folder's own assets, its subfolders still named under folders.

includeTags.description: When true, include asset tags in the listing response.

includeMetadata.description: When true, include the file size and modification date of each asset.

filter.description: Substring filter. Listing assets: a case-insensitive match on the asset name, and on the own name of each folder listed. Listing content sources: a case-sensitive match on the source id and, for plugins, the category.

sourceRoot.description: Restrict the listing to one root. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. Omit to list every root.

includePackageCounts.description: Include packageCount per source. Costs a recursive file scan per returned entry, so leave off for a broad sweep and turn on once the candidate list is short.

kind.description: Which list variant to run; omit for 'assets'.

offset.description: Applied zero-based offset.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

sources.description: Discovered sources. Each entry carries sourceRoot, sourceId, kind (template | featurePack | megascansPack | plugin | contentFolder), hasContentFolder, migratable, and packageCount when requested.

rootDirectories.description: Absolute directory each root token resolved to, so an operator can confirm where the Bridge library was found.

missingRoots.description: Root tokens whose directory does not exist on this machine.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.
whenToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: A naming convention must be enforced across a folder or a list, such as swapping a prefix or adding a suffix to every asset.
maintenance=bulk_rename: Several unrelated assets must each get a specific new name in one call (the renames list).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors left in a folder by earlier moves or renames must be resolved: referencers are repointed and the redirectors deleted.
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: Blueprints in a folder or a list need every node refreshed, then compiled and saved, for example after a class was renamed.
maintenance=migrate: Loose .uasset content from an engine template, plugin or downloaded Fab or Megascans pack must be copied into the project.
maintenance=migrate: A migration must be previewed with a dry run before any file is copied.
whenNotToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: One asset or one folder gets a new name (use asset.rename).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors should only be listed before anything changes (use asset.query_asset with lookup=search and classNames ObjectRedirector).
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: One Blueprint only needs compiling (use blueprint.compile).
maintenance=migrate: A source file (FBX, PNG, WAV) must become an asset (use asset.import).
maintenance=migrate: The available sources are still unknown (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).

pattern.description: Search pattern (used when searchText is absent).

replacement.description: Replacement text (used when replaceText is absent).

checkoutFiles.description: Check out files in source control.

renames.description: Explicit renames, each asset to its own new name in its own folder, all in this one call: [{sourcePath, newName}]. An entry whose asset is missing, or whose newName is taken, is skipped and named under skipped. Replaces the pattern fields.

path.description: Alternative directory path.

sourceRoot.description: Content source root token. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. A filesystem path is never accepted here — the token is resolved plugin-side, so no directory outside these roots is reachable. megascansLibrary probes both the shell Documents folder and the profile Documents folder (OneDrive redirects the first) and honours MCP_MEGASCANS_LIBRARY_DIR; fabLibrary reads the Fab plugin's own UFabSettings.CacheDirectoryPath and honours MCP_FAB_LIBRARY_DIR. The Fab plugin owns its own sign-in and downloading — these roots only read what it already placed on disk.

sourceId.description: Relative id under sourceRoot, exactly as returned by list_content_sources (for example "TP_VehicleAdvBP"). Must be relative: no "..", no leading "/", no drive prefix. Omit to migrate the root itself.

subPath.description: Optional folder under the source content directory, to migrate one subtree instead of the whole pack.

destinationPath.description: Root the copied tree lands under. Leave at "/Game" to preserve the source layout and keep internal references valid; any deeper path relocates the tree and flags referenceIntegrity as "at-risk".

overwrite.description: Overwrite packages that already exist at the destination. Default false, which skips them and reports skippedCount.

dryRun.description: Report what would be copied without writing anything. Returns the same counts and packagePaths sample.

maxPackages.description: Refuse the migration when the source holds more files than this, so a mistyped source cannot copy tens of gigabytes. Narrow with subPath or raise deliberately.

maintenance.description: Which maintain content variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

sourceDirectory.description: Absolute directory the packages were read from.

copiedCount.description: Files copied (or that would be copied under dryRun).

skippedCount.description: Files already present at the destination and left alone because overwrite was false.

failedCount.description: Files that could not be copied.

totalFiles.description: Package files discovered in the source.

referenceIntegrity.description: "preserved" when the source layout was reproduced under /Game, "at-risk" when destinationPath relocated it.

packagePaths.description: Up to 40 destination package paths, for verifying the migration landed where expected.

failedFiles.description: Up to 20 source-relative paths that failed to copy.

warnings.description: Advisory messages, including the reference-integrity warning for a relocated destination.

examples.title: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.

discovery.summary: Move an asset to a new path, or a whole folder: every asset under it moves (sub-folders kept) and references, redirectors and project settings follow.
whenToUse: An asset must go to another folder; references and project settings (default map, game mode) that point at it follow.
A whole content folder must relocate with its sub-folders; its redirectors are resolved and the emptied source folder is removed.
whenNotToUse: Only the name changes and the asset stays in its folder (use asset.rename).
The asset must be copied and the original left in place (use asset.duplicate).

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: everything under it moves into destinationPath, keeping sub-folders, and the emptied folder is removed.

newName.description: Rename in place instead: the asset keeps its folder and takes this name (used when destinationPath is omitted).

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Move an asset to a new path, or a whole folder: every asset under it moves (sub-folders kept) and references, redirectors and project settings follow.

discovery.summary: Turn Nanite on for a static mesh asset, or several in one call (assetPaths), and set the share of its triangles Nanite keeps; each mesh is rebuilt and saved, and the reply reads naniteEnabled and trianglePercent back from it.
whenToUse: A static mesh needs Nanite enabled, or the percentage of triangles Nanite keeps changed.
Several meshes need Nanite: assetPaths does them all under one consent.
whenNotToUse: A dynamic mesh must be baked into a new Nanite static mesh asset (use manage_geometry.convert_to_nanite).
Plain LOD levels are wanted for a mesh that will not use Nanite (use asset.process_asset with process=lods).
The mesh has a translucent material slot (glass): Nanite draws only opaque and masked materials, so the call leaves such a mesh as it is (NANITE_UNSUPPORTED_MATERIAL).

assetPaths.description: Several static meshes, each turned on, rebuilt and saved in this one call (a whole imported pack, or every heavy mesh get_stats statsKind=frame lists); one mesh that fails does not stop the others.

trianglePercent.description: Percent of the source triangles Nanite keeps, 0-100 (default 100).

naniteEnabled.description: Nanite is on, read back from the mesh.

trianglePercent.description: Percent of its triangles Nanite keeps, read back from the mesh.

saved.description: It was saved.

materialsFlagged.description: Materials of the mesh, and those its placed copies in the open level override its slots with (from UE 5.8, material instances too), that lacked the Nanite usage flag: it is set and they are saved, since the editor sets a missing one only when it next draws the mesh, never saves it, and a packaged game draws that surface without it. Absent when none lacked it.

meshes.description: With assetPaths: one row per mesh, {assetPath, naniteEnabled, trianglePercent, materialsFlagged} for one rebuilt and saved, or {assetPath, error} for one that is not a static mesh, holds a translucent material, is outside the allowed paths or could not be saved; any error fails the call (NANITE_PARTIAL) with the other meshes done.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rebuild Nanite data after a mesh edit
