discovery.summary: Process an asset, chosen by process. thumbnail renders its preview at width by height (default 512, 1 to 4096) and stores it in the asset, which is left unsaved (thumbnailCached; engine content keeps its own), writing it as a PNG as well when outputPath names a project-relative file. lods gives static meshes lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each half the triangles of the one before), replacing LODs past the count and hand-tuned settings, then rebuilds and saves each. mesh_materials sets the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or name, so every placement shows them; an engine mesh changes for this session only and is never saved (saveSkippedReason). mesh_collision sets the collision of a static mesh asset (a fitted box, sphere or capsule, its render triangles, or none), rebuilds every placed copy and saves it. lods and mesh_collision refuse engine meshes (ENGINE_CONTENT): duplicate one into /Game first.
whenToUse: process=thumbnail: An asset needs a preview image, optionally written as a PNG file inside the project.
process=lods: One or several static meshes need LOD levels generated so distant copies render cheaper.
process=mesh_materials: An imported mesh came in with every slot on the default grid material and each slot needs its own material, once for every placement of the mesh.
process=mesh_materials: Several slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset get their materials in one call, by index or by slot name.
process=mesh_materials: Every mesh of an imported pack needs the same slot-name to material map (base, Material_0 ...): assetPaths with the slot names.
process=mesh_collision: An imported or Fab mesh has no simple collision, so pawns fall through it or walk through it.
process=mesh_collision: A decorative mesh (grass, flowers, small debris) must stop blocking the player.
process=mesh_collision: A terrain-like or concave mesh must collide exactly with its own triangles (complex).
whenNotToUse: process=thumbnail: The image should show the editor viewport or a level camera view (use control_editor.screenshot).
process=lods: LOD reduction settings or screen sizes must be tuned by hand (use manage_geometry.configure_mesh_lods).
process=lods: The mesh should use Nanite instead of discrete LODs (use asset.nanite_rebuild_mesh).
process=mesh_materials: Only one placed actor must look different from its mesh (use control_actor.set_material, which overrides a component and leaves the asset alone).
process=mesh_materials: It is not known yet which slot holds which part of the mesh (inspect.inspect_object with objectKind=mesh lists every slot with the triangle count and bounds of its geometry).
process=mesh_collision: A dynamic mesh actor needs collision generated (use manage_geometry.configure_mesh_collision).
process=mesh_collision: Only one placed copy should stop colliding (use control_actor.set_actor_collision).
process=mesh_collision: It must be checked whether a placed mesh blocks at all (use inspect.raycast_world).

outputPath.description: Project-relative PNG file to write, e.g. Saved/Thumbnails/SM_Crate.png.

assetPaths.description: Several asset paths to process in one call: lods generates LODs for each; mesh_materials sets the same materials entries on each mesh by slot name, passing over a slot a mesh lacks (an entry no mesh has fails the call), as a whole imported pack needs.

lodCount.description: Number of LOD levels to generate (1-50, default 4).

slot.description: The slot to set: its 0-based index (9) or its slot name ("hull"), as inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists them under materialSlots.

materialPath.description: Material or material instance asset path, e.g. /Game/Materials/M_Hull. It must load: a path that does not is refused, never swapped for a default material.

materials.description: The slots to set, one entry per slot: [{slot, materialPath}]. slot is a 0-based index or a slot name (inspect_object objectKind=mesh lists both under materialSlots). Every entry is checked first. One that is refused (index out of range, unknown slot name, a material that does not load) is named under refused and fails the call, while the valid entries are applied together in a single rebuild of the mesh.

save.description: Save the mesh after the change. Defaults to true.

collisionType.description: box, sphere or capsule: one shape fitted to the mesh bounds (a capsule stands upright along Z) replaces its simple collision. complex: the render triangles are the collision, exact for terrain-like or concave meshes but costlier. none: no collision, so pawns and traces pass through.

process.description: Which process asset variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

meshes.description: With assetPaths: one row per mesh, {assetPath, changed (slots this call changed on it), error (it is not a mesh, or does not load), saved (false only when it could not be saved)}.

materialSlots.description: Every slot of the mesh after the call, each {slotIndex, slotName, material (the asset path the slot holds, empty for none), changed (true when this call changed it)}.

applied.description: Entries that were valid and applied.

changed.description: Slots whose material this call changed; an entry that names the material a slot already holds changes nothing.

refused.description: Entries that were refused, each {index (its position in materials), slot (as given), materialPath, code, reason}: a slot index out of range, an unknown slot name, a material that does not load. A refused entry changes nothing, the call fails (MATERIAL_SLOTS_PARTIAL, or MATERIAL_SLOTS_REFUSED when no entry was valid) and the valid entries stay applied.

saved.description: Whether the mesh was saved.

saveSkippedReason.description: Why nothing was saved: save was false, or the mesh is engine content, which is never written.

collisionType.description: The collision the mesh has now.

shapeCount.description: Simple collision shapes the mesh holds after the call (0 for complex and none).

componentsRefreshed.description: Placed copies of the mesh in open worlds whose collision was rebuilt to match.

examples.title: Process an asset, chosen by process. thumbnail renders its preview at width by height (default 512, 1 to 4096) and stores it in the asset, which is left unsaved (thumbnailCached; engine content keeps its own), writing it as a PNG as well when outputPath names a project-relative file. lods gives static meshes lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each half the triangles of the one before), replacing LODs past the count and hand-tuned settings, then rebuilds and saves each. mesh_materials sets the materials in the slots of a static or skeletal mesh asset, by slot index or name, so every placement shows them; an engine mesh changes for this session only and is never saved (saveSkippedReason). mesh_collision sets the collision of a static mesh asset (a fitted box, sphere or capsule, its render triangles, or none), rebuilds every placed copy and saves it. lods and mesh_collision refuse engine meshes (ENGINE_CONTENT): duplicate one into /Game first.

discovery.summary: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets (graph nodes by title too, so every call of a function), the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.
whenToUse: lookup=exists: A path must be tested for an asset, or several paths at once, before creating, importing or referencing one.
lookup=search: Assets must be found across the project by name, class, folder or asset-registry tag.

lookup=by_tag: Assets under /Game must be found by an asset-registry tag, optionally with one value, such as the ParentClass tag every Blueprint carries. A tag written by asset.set_metadata with kind=tags is in the registry only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise nothing matches (asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata reads one asset).
lookup=text: A piece of text, such as a UI label or dialogue line, must be traced to the Blueprint, widget, table row or level actor holding it.
lookup=graph: A material or Blueprint must be summarised: node counts, parameters, blend mode or graph count.
lookup=material_stats: A material's shading model, blend mode, domain, node and parameter counts, or the input pins its Main result node accepts, must be read.
lookup=source_control_state: Before editing, it must be known whether assets are checked out, modified or held by someone else.
whenNotToUse: lookup=exists: A folder's contents must be browsed rather than one path tested (use asset.list).
lookup=search|by_tag: Actors placed in the open level must be found (use control_actor.find).
lookup=text: One known Blueprint graph must be read node by node (use blueprint.inspect_graph).
lookup=graph: One Blueprint's variables, functions or components are wanted (use blueprint.get_blueprint).
lookup=material_stats: The individual nodes of a material and their connections are needed (use material.get_material_info).
lookup=source_control_state: Assets must be checked out or submitted (use asset.source_control).

assetPaths.description: Several asset paths checked in one call; the reply maps each to true or false under existsByPath.

classNames.description: Asset classes to filter: a short class name (StaticMesh, Blueprint, ObjectRedirector, InputMappingContext) or a full class path (/Script/Engine.StaticMesh).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

tag.description: Asset-registry tag name, for example ParentClass, which every Blueprint carries.

value.description: Optional tag value to match, ignoring case.

includeLevel.description: Also search the actors and components of the open level: true or false outright; omitted, only when that level lies under packagePaths (always with the default /Game).

recursive.description: Also report every /Game package the assets depend on, transitively (up to 512).

lookup.description: Which query asset variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

offset.description: Applied zero-based offset.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

matches.description: Each match: asset, where (graph and node title, widget, row, string key or actor label), field, the full text, and nodeId for a graph literal.

matchCount.description: Every match found; more than the matches returned when truncated.

scannedAssets.description: Blueprints, DataTables and String Tables searched.

truncated.description: True when limit cut the list; raise limit to see the rest.

assetClass.description: Concrete UClass name of the analyzed asset.

graphType.description: Graph kind analyzed: Material, Blueprint, None, or the class of an asset whose graph another action reads (see nextCall).

nodeCount.description: Material expression nodes in the graph.

parameterCount.description: Material parameter expressions in the graph.

textureSampleCount.description: Texture sample expressions in the graph.

isMaterialInstance.description: True when the asset is a material instance.

isTwoSided.description: True when the material renders two-sided.

isMasked.description: True when the material uses masked blending.

blueprintType.description: Blueprint kind: Class, Interface, MacroLibrary, or FunctionLibrary.

totalNodes.description: Total nodes across every Blueprint graph.

graphCount.description: Number of graphs in the Blueprint.

message.description: Explanation when the asset type carries no graph, or which action reads it.

nextCall.description: A MetaSound, Niagara or Behavior Tree asset: the execute call of the action that reads its graph.

examples.title: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets (graph nodes by title too, so every call of a function), the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.

discovery.summary: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library, and the status of a Fab import that is running.
whenToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: A Fab search hit must be judged before adding it: description, seller, rating, price, file formats, sizes, and whether the project can import it.
lookup=fab_downloads: It must be known which Fab packs are already downloaded to this machine and where they are cached.
lookup=fab_library: The Fab listings the signed-in account owns must be listed, each with an id for adding to the project (an empty table is synced by the call itself).
lookup=fab_search: Content must be found on Fab by keyword, optionally from one publisher or of one kind, or free listings only, to get listing ids and to tell a Megascans hit from a random upload.
lookup=megascans_library: The Megascans packs downloaded by Bridge on this machine must be listed before one is imported.
lookup=fab_import_status: A Fab add has returned an operationId and it must be known whether the import is downloading, importing, done or failed, and where the content landed.
whenNotToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: The listing is chosen and must be added to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_downloads: A downloaded pack must be copied into the project (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).
lookup=fab_library: A listing from the library is ready to add to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_search: Content already installed in an engine template, plugin or Bridge folder is wanted (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).
lookup=megascans_library: A listed pack should be imported into the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=megascans).
lookup=fab_import_status: The listing has not been added yet (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max. fab_import_status also takes it, in place of operationId, to report the newest import of that listing.

columnTypes.description: Column struct paths to read, for example "/Script/Fab.FabObjectNameColumn". Defaults to the name column plus "/Script/Fab.FabObjectColumn", which carries AssetId, ListingType, Seller and Source. Selecting a column is also the row filter, so naming one Fab does not write for every row will hide rows. Override this when a Fab update renames or adds columns; unresolved paths are reported rather than failing the call.

filter.description: Case-sensitive substring matched against each serialized row. Use "fab" to drop the legacy "uem" engine and plugin entries that otherwise fill the row limit.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return, clamped plugin-side.

query.description: Free-text search. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters.

seller.description: Only listings published by this seller, by name, for example Quixel Megascans. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters. Omit for every publisher.

listingType.description: Only this content kind, as a row's listingType names it, for example 3d-model or material. One token of [A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 40 characters. Omit for every kind.

operationId.description: Operation id from the add reply. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max. Give this or listingId, or neither to list the queue.

lookup.description: Which query marketplace variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

categoryPath.description: Category path, slash-joined, when Fab publishes one.

averageRating.description: Average rating as Fab reports it. Absent when the listing has none.

ratingCount.description: How many ratings the average rests on. Absent when Fab publishes no count.

licenseNames.description: Names of the licenses the listing is offered under.

isCc0.description: True when a license of the listing is CC0 (public domain, no credit needed), read from the license names: Fab's own flag is also set on CC-BY licenses. Absent when the listing publishes no licenses.

attributionRequired.description: True when a license of the listing is Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY, CC BY-SA ...): an asset used under it needs a credit line in the project naming its title, author, source and license, and saying what was changed. Absent when the listing publishes no licenses.

price.description: Starting price in Fab's own units; 0 is free. Absent when the price field has a shape this does not know (see priceShape).

currency.description: Currency code of price, when Fab publishes one.

isFree.description: True when price is 0. Derived from price: the listing's own isFree flag disagrees with it and is never reported. When the price cannot be read this falls back to that flag and priceShape says so.

priceShape.description: Key names of a price field this does not recognise, so a Fab change reports itself. Present only then.

publishedAt.description: When the listing was published, as Fab states it.

imageBase64.description: Preview image bytes, base64. Promoted to an MCP image content block.

hasImage.description: False when no preview could be inlined.

imageOmitted.description: Present when the preview was skipped for exceeding the reply cap.

descriptionKeys.description: Listing keys observed when no description field matched.

thumbnailShape.description: Thumbnail keys observed when no image URL matched.

assetFormats.description: Asset format codes this listing ships, e.g. unreal-engine, fbx, gltf.

hasUnrealBuild.description: True when the listing ships a packaged unreal-engine build, which Fab imports through its pack workflow.

formats.description: Every format the listing ships: code, and files each with name, bytes (left out when Fab publishes no size) and quality when the name carries a tier.

addFormat.description: The format add_fab_asset_to_project would import: unreal-engine, else gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz. Absent when none is importable.

distributionMethod.description: How Fab distributes a unreal-engine listing: asset_pack (content for a project) or complete_project (a whole project). Present only for a listing that ships unreal-engine.

runningEngine.description: The editor's engine version, major.minor, that supportsRunningEngine and engineMatch are judged against.

engineVersions.description: Every engine version a unreal-engine pack declares, lowest first, as Fab spells them (UE_5.4).

supportsRunningEngine.description: True when a build of the pack declares exactly the running engine. Present only for a unreal-engine listing that publishes versions.

engineMatch.description: exact, older or newer: the build the add would take against the running engine. older is the newest build for an earlier engine, newer the oldest build for a later one. Absent when no version declares an engine.

versionName.description: Name of the pack build the add would take.

pickedEngineVersion.description: The engine version that build declares, for example UE_5.4.

downloadFile.description: The file of a source format the add would download.

quality.description: Quality tier of that file (raw, high, mid or low), when the listing publishes tiers.

qualities.description: The quality tiers the source format offers, best first. add_fab_asset_to_project takes the highest of high, mid, low, raw that exists.

downloadBytes.description: Size in bytes of exactly the file or build the add would fetch. Absent when Fab publishes no size, which is every pack: unknown, never zero.

downloadSizeKnown.description: False when downloadBytes is absent because Fab publishes no size for what the add would fetch.

canAddToProject.description: True when add_fab_asset_to_project can import this listing: it ships unreal-engine as an asset pack, or gltf, glb, fbx, obj or usdz. False for a complete project, a MetaHuman listing and a listing with no importable format (addBlockedCode says which). Megascans listings are importable: the add claims the listing itself. Check this rather than hasUnrealBuild before adding.

addBlockedCode.description: Present when canAddToProject is false: COMPLETE_PROJECT, METAHUMAN_FORMAT or NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT, the code the add would answer with.

addBlockedReason.description: Present when canAddToProject is false: why this listing cannot be imported.

addWarnings.description: What would surprise the caller about adding this listing: a pack with no build for the running engine, or a mesh file large enough that the add refuses it until combineMeshes is chosen.

downloads.description: Cached Fab downloads. Each entry carries assetId and cachedFile.

cacheDirectory.description: Directory the Fab plugin caches downloads in.

cacheDirectoryExists.description: False when nothing has been downloaded yet.

fabModuleAvailable.description: True when the plugin was built against the Fab module and read the cache through its own API rather than scanning the directory.

note.description: Guidance on what to do next given the current state.

entries.description: Library rows. Each entry maps column struct name to that column's properties, read by reflection. FabObjectColumn.AssetId is the listing id add_fab_asset_to_project takes.

unresolvedColumnTypes.description: Requested column paths that do not exist in this build — usually a Fab schema change.

syncTriggered.description: True when the table held no rows and Fab's library sync was run for this call.

syncWaitedSeconds.description: How long this call waited for rows after starting the sync. Present only when the sync ran.

syncSkipped.description: Why the sync was not run on an empty table: this editor registers no Fab sync command. Present only then.

listings.description: Matched listings: listingId, title, listingType, isFree (derived from price), tags, and, when the row carried them, seller, category, averageRating, ratingCount, price, currency, isCc0, publishedAt and formats (the format codes it ships). unresolvedPriceShape names the price field's keys when the price could not be read. The listing's own isFree flag is not reported.

assets.description: Indexed library entries, verbatim from uassetsData.json.

indexExists.description: False when Bridge has never written an index here.

importAvailable.description: True when this build links the MegascansPlugin module, so import_megascans_asset can run.

phase.description: queued, resolving, downloading, importing, cancelling, done or failed.

finished.description: True once phase is done or failed; stop polling.

queuePosition.description: 1-based place in the queue while phase is queued; absent otherwise.

queue.description: The import that is running, then every add waiting behind it in the order they start: operationId, listingId, title, phase, queuePosition, elapsedSeconds, and downloadedBytes and downloadPercent when known. Absent when nothing is running or queued.

queueLength.description: How many imports are running or queued.

elapsedSeconds.description: Seconds since the add was requested; frozen once the import finished.

formatCode.description: Format Fab was asked to import.

fileName.description: The file Fab downloads (source formats only).

engineExactMatch.description: False when no build of the pack declares the running engine; engineMatch says which build was taken instead.

engineVersion.description: The engine version that build declares, for example UE_5.4.

combinesMeshes.description: True when Fab's importer merges every mesh of a file into ONE static mesh for this listing.

combineMeshesApplied.description: Present only when the add passed combineMeshes=false for a listing Fab merges meshes for: true once Interchange's mesh combining was switched off before it ran, false while that has not happened yet or could not (the import then yields the single merged mesh).

downloadedBytes.description: Bytes fetched so far, when the download folder shows them. Absent when the download cannot be observed (a unreal-engine pack, or a download that has not begun).

downloadPercent.description: 0-100, as Fab's own download notification shows it, for a unreal-engine pack and a source format alike. Absent when that notification cannot be read: before the download starts, after it ends, or when Fab shows none.

cancellable.description: Present while the import is not finished: true when a cancel would stop it right now (queued, a unreal-engine pack that is downloading, or an import Interchange is translating); false for a source-format download, which Fab gives no cancel for.

assetsSoFar.description: New assets the asset registry has gained so far.

importedRoot.description: Where the content landed: the folder Fab chose (typically /Game/Fab/... or /Game/<PackName>), or the destinationPath the add asked for once the import was moved there. Present once finished and any landed.

sampleAssetPaths.description: Up to ten imported asset paths, the static and skeletal meshes first, at their final paths when the add asked for destinationPath or assetName.

relocated.description: Present when the add asked for destinationPath or assetName: true when assets were moved or renamed.

movedCount.description: Assets moved or renamed by that relocation.

relocationNote.description: What the relocation did not do, and why: a folder or name already taken (nothing moves then), an assetName with no single asset to name, or content left where Fab put it. Absent when everything asked for was done.

saved.description: Present once the import settled and any assets landed: true when every package the import left dirty was saved, false when some could not be (see unsavedPackages, and the message and note say so in capitals). Fab leaves what it imports unsaved in memory, so a Megascans add would otherwise be lost when the editor closes. The import is saved again 15 and 60 seconds after it ends, because Interchange marks packages dirty after the last asset has appeared; read again before saving by hand.

savedCount.description: Packages that were saved. A unreal-engine pack arrives on disk already and is not dirty, so it counts none.

unsavedPackages.description: Packages that could not be saved, by name; control_editor save_all writes them once whatever blocked the save is fixed.

failureCode.description: Present when phase is failed: FAB_IMPORT_FAILED (Fab logged that it gave up), IMPORT_TIMED_OUT (nothing appeared before the ceiling), IMPORT_PARTIAL (still streaming at the ceiling; what landed is reported), CANCELLED (cancel_fab_import stopped it; whatever had landed is listed and left unsaved), or the add's own refusal code (COMPLETE_PROJECT, METAHUMAN_FORMAT, LARGE_SCENE_FILE, QUALITY_NOT_AVAILABLE, NO_IMPORTABLE_FORMAT, NO_DOWNLOAD_URL).

failure.description: Present when phase is failed: why, in words.

fabErrors.description: Error lines Fab logged while the import ran, with URLs and anything credential-shaped masked.

examples.title: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library, and the status of a Fab import that is running.

discovery.summary: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.
whenToUse: An asset needs a new name in its own folder; settings that point at it (default map, game mode) follow.
A folder must get a new name and every asset under it must go along.
whenNotToUse: Many assets need new names by pattern, prefix, suffix or a list (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=bulk_rename).
A copy under a new name is wanted, with the original kept (use asset.duplicate).

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: a folder is renamed with everything under it.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Write package metadata on an asset (kind metadata: key/value pairs, numbers and booleans as text, objects and arrays as JSON text, null skipped; updatedKeys counts them) or tag it (tags: each tag becomes a metadata key set to true; appliedTags). The asset is marked unsaved, not saved (save_all keeps it). Package metadata is editor-only: cooking strips it, so the running game cannot read it.
whenToUse: kind=metadata: Key and value notes such as author or revision must be attached to an asset; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
kind=tags: Simple labels such as Reviewed or Prop must be attached to an asset as package metadata; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
whenNotToUse: kind=metadata: The stored values must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset).
kind=metadata: A property of the asset itself must change (use inspect.set_property).
kind=tags: Actors in a level need a tag (use control_actor.add_tag).

kind=tags: Assets must be found by the tag afterwards. asset.query_asset lookup=by_tag reads the asset registry, which carries a package-metadata tag only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise it finds nothing.
kind=tags: The tags on an asset must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata, which lists them under metadata at once).

tags.description: Tag names to set; each is written as package metadata with the value "true".

kind.description: Which set metadata variant to run; omit for 'metadata'.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Revision control: initialise a repository, enable a provider, check out, submit, or commit every change.
whenToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: Assets must be checked out of revision control before they are edited.
sourceControlOp=submit: Checked-out assets must be submitted to the revision-control server with a change description.
sourceControlOp=enable: A revision-control provider such as Git or Perforce must be selected before checkout or submit can work.
sourceControlOp=init: A project with no repository needs one, with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit, in one call.
sourceControlOp=commit_all: A snapshot of every change in the project is wanted as one commit, for example after a batch of edits.
whenNotToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: The checked-out or modified state of assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=submit|commit_all: Unsaved editor changes must reach disk first (use control_editor.save_all).
sourceControlOp=submit: Every change in the project is wanted as one Git snapshot, without listing assets (use sourceControlOp=commit_all).
sourceControlOp=enable: Only the state of particular assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=init: A Perforce or Subversion provider is wanted; init builds only a Git repository (select the provider with sourceControlOp=enable).
sourceControlOp=commit_all: Only chosen assets must go in, or the project uses Perforce or Subversion (use sourceControlOp=submit).

provider.description: Provider name as the editor registers it, e.g. Git or Perforce. Omit to report the current provider without changing it.

userName.description: Commit author name, written to the repository config only.

userEmail.description: Commit author email, written to the repository config only.

sourceControlOp.description: Which source control variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

topics: faster while a key is held
cannon that fires at the player
jump on enemies to kill them
platform that moves back and forth
platform that moves up and down
win when the player reaches the goal
message when the player walks up
show game over when the player dies
restart the level when the player dies
discovery.summary: Write gameplay logic into an Actor Blueprint in one call: health that takes damage and dies, damage on touch, a pickup that heals or counts (coins, keys), a sprint key for a Character, a key that shoots projectiles for a pawn, a pawn that chases the player or patrols a route, a turret that turns to the player and fires at them, an enemy the player defeats by jumping on it, a barrel that explodes when it dies, a moving platform or elevator, walk, look and jump controls for a Character, a pawn that respawns when it falls or dies (with checkpoints), a goal that ends the level when the player reaches it, a pad that launches a Character, a teleporter, a platform that falls when a pawn lands on it, a time limit, a spawner that keeps spawning an actor class, a dash key for a Character, the health of the player or a count such as coins or score on screen, a hint on screen while the player is in an area, or a game over screen that restarts the level when the player dies. Logic none of these covers is written with edit_graph.
whenToUse: behaviour=health: A player, enemy or breakable object must take damage and die; behaviour health_hud shows it on screen.
behaviour=damage_on_touch: Spikes, lava, an enemy body or a fire must hurt what touches it.
behaviour=pickup: A health pack, coin, key or ammo box must be collected by walking into it.
behaviour=sprint: The player must run faster while holding a key.
behaviour=shoot: The player (or any possessed pawn) must shoot projectiles with a key; a projectile from manage_combat create_combat_asset damages what it hits and never hits its shooter.

behaviour=chase: An enemy or creature must run after the player; with usePathfinding (default) the level needs a NavMeshBoundsVolume (manage_level_structure create_volume), without it the pawn heads straight for the player.
behaviour=patrol: An enemy or guard must walk a route, and may chase the player who comes close.

behaviour=turret: A tower, cannon or enemy must shoot at the player who comes close; a projectile from manage_combat create_combat_asset damages what it hits. With behaviour chase too, a pawn runs at the player and shoots.

behaviour=stomp: A platformer enemy must die when the player jumps on it, and hurt the player who walks into it. A damage_on_touch the actor has is taken over (it would hurt the stomping player too); its damage becomes sideDamage when none is given.
behaviour=explosive: A barrel, crate or mine must blow up when shot or hit, hurting what stands near; it needs the health behaviour, so damage from any source sets it off.
behaviour=moving_platform: A platform, lift or elevator must travel a route by itself, every placed copy of a Blueprint alike (each copy keeps its own PlatformPoints).
behaviour=controls: A Character made with manage_character create_character_blueprint (or any Character without input) must be playable: it has no input until this runs.
behaviour=respawn: A player pawn must not be lost for good when it falls off the level or dies.

behaviour=respawn: Checkpoints: tag a trigger actor (manage_interaction create_interactable trigger, or any actor that overlaps pawns) with checkpointTag; the pawn respawns where it stood when it touched it.
behaviour=goal: A level needs an end: a finish line, an exit door, a flag the player reaches.
behaviour=launch_pad: A jump pad, bounce pad, trampoline or boost pad for the player or any Character.
behaviour=teleporter: Portals, warp pads, or a pair of teleporters between two places.
behaviour=falling_platform: A ledge or bridge must give way under the player a moment after they land on it.
behaviour=countdown: A level or a run must be finished within a time limit.
behaviour=spawner: Enemies, pickups or obstacles must keep appearing while the game runs.
behaviour=dash: A player Character needs a quick burst of movement on a key: a dash, a dodge, an air dash.
behaviour=health_hud: The player must see their own health: a health bar on the HUD.
behaviour=counter_hud: The player must see a count: coins collected, score, keys, kills.
behaviour=hint: A sign, a tutorial area or a talking spot must tell the player something (Press Space to jump).
behaviour=game_over: The player death must end the run: a game over screen, then the level starts again.
whenNotToUse: behaviour=health: The project uses the Gameplay Ability System for attributes (use manage_gas).
behaviour=damage_on_touch: A whole area must hurt or kill (use manage_level_structure create_volume with a pain causing or kill Z volume).
behaviour=pickup: The item must go into an inventory system (use manage_inventory).
behaviour=sprint: The walk speed itself must change (use manage_character configure_character walkSpeed).
behaviour=shoot: A weapon actor the pawn holds must do the shooting (use manage_combat configure_projectile for its Fire function).
behaviour=chase: The pawn walks a route too (behaviour patrol, which chases with chaseRange; chase refuses a pawn that patrols).
behaviour=chase: Senses, cover or decisions beyond chasing (use manage_ai with a Behavior Tree or State Tree).
behaviour=patrol: Senses, cover or decisions beyond walking a route and chasing (use manage_ai with a Behavior Tree or State Tree).
behaviour=turret: The player shoots with a key (behaviour shoot).
behaviour=stomp: A hazard must hurt whatever touches it, from above too (behaviour damage_on_touch).
behaviour=explosive: Damage must happen on touch (behaviour damage_on_touch).
behaviour=moving_platform: One placed actor must spin or travel (control_actor edit_component with a RotatingMovement or InterpToMovement component).
behaviour=moving_platform: A pawn must walk a route (behaviour patrol).
behaviour=controls: Only one key or action must be added (use manage_networking configure_input for the asset and blueprint edit_graph for its node).
behaviour=respawn: A pawn that should stay dead, such as an enemy: give it the health behaviour with destroyOnDeath instead.
behaviour=goal: Something must happen on every touch, by any actor (use a trigger actor from manage_interaction create_interactable).
behaviour=launch_pad: A Character must jump higher by itself (manage_character set_movement_property JumpZVelocity).
behaviour=teleporter: Moving an actor from the editor or a test (control_actor set_transform).
behaviour=falling_platform: A platform must keep moving on its own (add an InterpToMovement component with its control points).
behaviour=countdown: Something must happen once after a delay (edit_graph with a Delay or a timer node).
behaviour=spawner: Actors must be placed once, before play (use control_actor spawn).
behaviour=dash: It must run faster while a key is held (use behaviour sprint).
behaviour=health_hud: A bar floating over an actor in the world, such as over an enemy.
behaviour=counter_hud: Health as a bar (behaviour health_hud).
behaviour=hint: A value such as coins or a timer must stay on screen (behaviour counter_hud).
behaviour=game_over: The player must come back where it died or at a checkpoint (behaviour respawn; a pawn that respawns when it dies is refused here).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

destroyOnDeath.description: Destroy the actor when its health reaches 0 (default false; OnDied fires either way).

invulnerableTime.description: Seconds after a hit during which further damage is ignored, so one touch costs one hit (default 0, none); heals still count.

damage.description: Damage on each touch (default 10; negative heals).

knockback.description: Speed a touching Character is launched away from the actor at, in units per second (default 0, none).

heal.description: Health given to the pawn that collects it; it reaches an actor with health (add_health) as negative damage.

collectorClass.description: Instead of heal: the class that collects it (a Blueprint path such as /Game/Blueprints/BP_Player), whose variableName goes up by amount.

variableName.description: With collectorClass: the collector's Int or Float variable (Coins).

soundPath.description: Sound asset played at the actor: where a pickup was collected, a goal when the player reaches it, a pad on each launch, where a teleported pawn arrives, or an explosive blows up.

key.description: The key that drives it: held to sprint (default LeftShift), pressed to shoot (default LeftMouseButton) or to dash (default Q). Any key name works: SpaceBar, Gamepad_RightTrigger, Gamepad_FaceButton_Right.

inputActionPath.description: An Input Action to use instead of the one the behaviour makes next to the Blueprint (IA_Sprint, IA_Shoot, IA_Dash).

mappingContextPath.description: The Input Mapping Context its keys go in (the project's own); default the one the pawn already registers, else /Game/Input/IMC_MCP.

projectileClass.description: The projectile it shoots: a Blueprint path (/Game/Weapons/BP_Fireball) or class path.

fireRate.description: Most shots a minute (default 300 for shoot, 60 for turret).

chaseRange.description: Distance within which the pawn chases the player, in units: chase defaults to 2000, and a patrol chases only when given one (default 0, or the range of a chase it takes over).

stopDistance.description: How close it gets to the player before it stops, in units (default 100).

usePathfinding.description: Follow the navigation mesh (default true; the level needs a NavMeshBoundsVolume, from manage_level_structure create_volume); false heads straight for the player or the next point.

points.description: The route: [x, y, z] offsets from where the actor starts, in world axes, visited in turn and looped (default [[500, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]], back and forth). Each placed copy keeps its own route (PatrolPoints or PlatformPoints is instance editable).

waitTime.description: Seconds it waits at each point (default 1).

range.description: Distance within which it turns to the player and fires, in units (default 2000).

bounceSpeed.description: Upward speed the stomping Character bounces off at, units per second (default 600).

sideDamage.description: Damage to a player Character that bumps it from the side or below, at most once a second (default 0, none, or the damage of a damage_on_touch it takes over).

explosionDamage.description: Damage at the centre of the blast, less toward its edge (default 50).

explosionRadius.description: Radius of the blast in units (default 400); walls between it and an actor shield that actor.

effectPath.description: A Niagara system played at the blast (none by default).

speed.description: Units per second it travels between points (default 200).

look.description: Also turn the view with the mouse and the right stick (default true); false for a fixed camera.

fallHeight.description: How far below its respawn point the pawn may fall before it respawns, in units (default 2000).

checkpointTag.description: Actor tag that marks a checkpoint (default Checkpoint).

nextLevel.description: Level opened once the goal is reached, by name or /Game path (a path must exist). Omitted: the game stays in this level, and OnGoalReached is left for other logic.

delay.description: Seconds between reaching the goal and opening nextLevel (default 2).

launchVelocity.description: Launch velocity [x, y, z] in units per second, world axes (default [0, 0, 1200], straight up).

overrideXY.description: Replace the horizontal speed of the Character instead of adding to it (default false).

cooldown.description: Seconds before it works again: before a Character can dash again, or before a teleporter takes a pawn after one arrived on it (default 1).

fallDelay.description: Seconds it shakes before it drops (default 0.5).

respawnTime.description: Seconds after it starts to drop until it is back in place (default 3); 0 never: it is destroyed 5 seconds into its fall.

seconds.description: The time limit in whole seconds (default 60).

killAtZero.description: Kill the actor when the time is up (default true; it needs the health behaviour to die). False only fires OnTimeUp.

spawnClass.description: The actor it spawns: a Blueprint path (/Game/Enemies/BP_Slime) or class path; not the spawner itself.

maxAlive.description: Most of its spawned actors alive at once (default 5); a destroyed one frees its place.

radius.description: How far across from the spawner an actor may appear, in units (default 0: on the spawner).

dashSpeed.description: Launch speed along the facing, units per second (default 1500).

widgetPath.description: A Widget Blueprint to show instead of the one made next to the Blueprint under UI/ (WBP_HealthBar, WBP_<variable>Counter, WBP_GameOver, WBP_Hint). One without the bar or the text gets it: the health bar HUD piece (add_game_widget), a text at the top right, a full-screen shade with the message, or a dark box at the bottom with the hint.

barName.description: The ProgressBar in the widget that shows the health (default HealthBar_Bar, the bar of the health bar piece). A bar named here must already be in the widget.

label.description: Text before the number (default the variable name; empty for the number alone).

textName.description: The TextBlock in the widget that the behaviour writes: the count of counter_hud (default <variable>Counter), or the message of game_over (default GameOver_Text) or of a hint (default Hint_Text). A text named here must already be in the widget.

message.description: The text shown: a game over's message (default GAME OVER), or the hint itself (required for hint).

hideAfter.description: Seconds the hint stays once shown (default 0: while the pawn stays in the area).

restartDelay.description: Seconds before the level opens again (default 3); 0 never restarts it.

behaviour.description: Which add behaviour variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

compiled.description: The Blueprint compiled with the behaviour.

saved.description: The Blueprint was saved.

variables.description: The variables it uses: {name, status added, redefaulted or kept}.

functions.description: Functions it added, which other logic can call.

dispatchers.description: Event dispatchers it added, which other logic can bind.

replaced.description: Behaviours this one took over and removed first: a patrol takes over a chase (Chase), a stomp a damage on touch (DamageOnTouch).

respawnOnDeath.description: The pawn has the health behaviour, so dying respawns it too; add health first, then respawn again, to get it. False on a pawn with a game over, which restarts the level when it dies.

createdAssets.description: The Widget Blueprint this call made; it stays if the Blueprint is rolled back.

discovery.summary: Add a content widget to a Widget Blueprint: text, rich text, image, button, check box, combo box, slider, spin box, progress bar, text input, list/tree view, or any widget class.
whenToUse: widgetKind=text_block: A new text block widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=rich_text_block: A new rich text block widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=image: A new image widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=button: A new button widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=check_box: A new check box widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=combo_box: A new combo box widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=slider: A new slider widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=spin_box: A new spin box widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=progress_bar: A new progress bar widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=text_input: A new text input widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=list_view: A new list view widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=tree_view: A new tree view widget must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=component: A widget class is needed that no dedicated add_* action covers.
whenNotToUse: widgetKind=text_block|rich_text_block|image|button|check_box|combo_box|slider|spin_box|progress_bar|text_input|list_view|tree_view: A panel container is needed instead (see widget-panels family).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

discovery.summary: Add a function or an event to a Blueprint; an event can be bound to a component's or a Widget Blueprint widget's delegate (OnClicked), and a function named after one the parent lets a Blueprint override (a widget's OnKeyDown) is made as that override.
whenToUse: kind=function: A new callable function must be created on the Blueprint.
kind=function: A parent function with a return value must be overridden, such as a widget's OnKeyDown to handle a key.
kind=event: An event handler node must be created in the EventGraph.
kind=event: A component event such as OnComponentBeginOverlap or OnComponentHit must be handled.
kind=event: A Widget Blueprint button, slider or other widget event such as OnClicked must be handled.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

functionName.description: Function name to add or remove.

inputs.description: Function inputs, each {name, type}, with the types add_event parameters take (Float, Vector, Actor, Array<Int> ...). A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

outputs.description: Function outputs (its return values), each {name, type}, with the types inputs take.

isPublic.description: Access specifier: true public (the default), false private (callable only from this Blueprint).

pure.description: Pure function (the Details panel's Pure checkbox): its call nodes have no exec pins. Default false.

posX.description: X position of the new node in the graph (default 0, the origin). add_node and create_node move a node given no position right past any node at the origin, and refuse a given spot another node covers (NODE_OVERLAP, with a suggestedPosition).

posY.description: Y position of the new node in the graph (default 0).

parameters.description: Event parameters, each {name, type}. Types: bool, byte, int, int64, float, double, string, name, text, vector, vector2d, rotator, transform, color, linearcolor, object, class, a class, struct or enum name (Actor, HitResult), Object:/Script/Engine.Actor, Struct:<path>, Enum:<path>, and Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value>. A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

graphName.description: Event graph page to add the event to; omitted, the main EventGraph.

eventName.description: Custom event name; with componentName, the delegate to bind: a component's (OnComponentBeginOverlap, OnComponentHit, ...) or a widget's (OnClicked, OnHovered, OnValueChanged, ...).

componentName.description: Component whose delegate fires the event, added by the Blueprint or inherited (a Character's CapsuleComponent), or in a Widget Blueprint a widget of its tree that is a variable (every widget the widget handlers add is), e.g. PlayButton with eventName OnClicked. Makes a component-bound event (K2Node_ComponentBoundEvent) named by eventName.

kind.description: Which add function variant to run; omit for 'function'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

functionName.description: Function name to add or remove.

nodeGuid.description: Node guid: the function's entry node, or the event node. A built-in event that already exists in the graph may be bound without one.

resultNodeGuid.description: The function's return node, present when the function has one (it is made when outputs are declared).

overrides.description: The parent function the new one overrides (UserWidget::OnKeyDown), when functionName names one.

widgetKind=horizontal_box: A new horizontal box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=grid_panel: A new grid panel must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=uniform_grid: A new uniform grid must be added to a Widget Blueprint.
widgetKind=wrap_box: A new wrap box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.

widgetKind=scale_box: A new scale box must be added to a Widget Blueprint.

widgetKind=widget_switcher: Several pages or tabs must occupy one region with only one visible at a time.

widgetKind=safe_zone: The layout is desktop-only and no safe-area inset applies.
widgetKind=widget_switcher: All children should be visible together (use an overlay or a box).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

parentSlot.description: Parent slot to add the widget to.

positionX.description: Canvas slot X position, applied only when the parent is a canvas panel.

columnCount.description: Columns given an equal share of the width (0-64).

rowCount.description: Rows given an equal share of the height (0-64).

contentColorAndOpacity.description: Tint (0-1 values) a border applies to its content.

maxDesiredWidth.description: Maximum desired width of a size box.

maxDesiredHeight.description: Maximum desired height of a size box.

activeIndex.description: Index shown first by a widget switcher.

tree.description: The layout as one nested node {type, name, children[], slot{}, ...props}. type: a UMG class short name (CanvasPanel, Overlay, VerticalBox, HorizontalBox, Border, SizeBox, ScaleBox, UniformGridPanel, Spacer, TextBlock, RichTextBlock, Image, ProgressBar, Button). name: the widget name, unique in the Widget Blueprint (each becomes a variable a graph can read). Props: text, fontSize, color [r,g,b,a] (text colour, border brush, image tint, bar fill), justify left|center|right, autoWrap, opacity, visibility, padding (number or [l,t,r,b]: a border's inner padding), radius (rounded border, image or button) with outlineColor and outlineWidth, imageSize [w,h], texture (an image's texture path), material (an Image's or Border's brush: a UI material or instance that draws the whole widget, such as a rounded panel with its rim and gradient), percent (progress bar), width, height, maxHeight (size box). Text blocks also take typeface (Bold, Regular, Light, Italic), fontFamily, letterSpacing, outline with outlineColor, and shadowOffset [x,y] with shadowColor. slot places the node in its parent: in a canvas anchors [minX,minY,maxX,maxY], alignment [x,y], position [x,y], size [w,h], autoSize, z; in a box padding, hAlign (left|center|right|fill), vAlign (top|center|bottom|fill) and fill (a share of the free space). A Widget Blueprint with no root yet gets a canvas, and a tree root with no slot (and no positionX/Y or sizeX/Y) fills it. An unknown field is refused, not ignored; at most 200 widgets.

whenToUse: bindingKind=text: A widget's text must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=color: A widget's color must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=enabled: A widget's enabled must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=percent: A widget's percent must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.
bindingKind=visibility: A widget's visibility must follow a Blueprint variable or function at runtime.

discovery.summary: Compile a Blueprint asset, optionally saving after compile, or every Blueprint under a folder at once, answered with the ones the compiler or the graph checks flag.
whenToUse: Blueprint changes must be compiled to take effect.
A project or a folder must be audited for compile errors and graph-check warnings (after an engine upgrade, before a release): folder compiles every Blueprint under it in one call.
whenNotToUse: The Blueprint has no pending changes.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

blueprintPath.description: Canonical /Game Blueprint asset path, or the path of a level open in the editor (/Game/Maps/L_Main) to compile its level Blueprint; saveAfterCompile then saves that level.

folder.description: In place of blueprintPath: compile every Blueprint under this /Game folder (sub-folders too, widget and animation Blueprints included, at most 500) and answer with counts and the ones that failed or carry warnings, each with its diagnostics. An audit leaves each package as saved or unsaved as it was; saveAfterCompile does not apply.

saveAfterCompile.description: Whether to save the asset after compiling.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

compiled.description: blueprintPath: whether the Blueprint compiled without errors.

compilerStatus.description: blueprintPath: the Blueprint status after the compile (UpToDate, UpToDateWithWarnings, Error).

diagnostics.description: blueprintPath: every compiler message and graph-check finding, each {severity, message}.

folder.description: folder: the folder audited, as resolved.

compiledCount.description: folder: how many Blueprints were compiled.

failedCount.description: folder: how many failed to compile.

flaggedCount.description: folder: how many failed or carry warnings, the length of blueprints.

blueprints.description: folder: each Blueprint that failed or carries warnings: blueprintPath, compiled, compilerStatus, errorCount, warningCount and diagnostics. One that compiled clean is only counted.

truncated.description: folder: true when the folder holds more than 500 Blueprints and only the first 500 were compiled.

examples.title: Compile a Blueprint asset, optionally saving after compile, or every Blueprint under a folder at once, answered with the ones the compiler or the graph checks flag.

discovery.summary: Create a Blueprint asset, chosen by createMode (ensure checks first), named name in savePath (default /Game) and save it (saved). parentClass is a native class as /Script/Module.Class or a short name (Actor, Pawn, Character, PlayerController), or a Blueprint class path ending in _C; blueprintType Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary stands in for a missing parentClass, and Interface without one makes a Blueprint Interface. A parent that resolves to nothing is CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming classes of that name. properties sets class defaults, Component.Property and struct members by dotted path, reported as appliedProperties and failedProperties (the create stands either way). A Blueprint already at the path is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged; one with another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.
whenToUse: createMode=create: A new Blueprint of a known parent class is needed.
createMode=create: A pickup or hazard is needed; its parts come from edit_scs, its logic from add_behaviour.
createMode=blueprint: A Blueprint must be created with a specific type hint.
createMode=ensure: Idempotent setup requires a Blueprint to exist without failing on duplicates.
whenNotToUse: createMode=create: An existing Blueprint should be opened or modified instead.
createMode=ensure: A fresh Blueprint is always required even if one exists.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new Blueprint or asset.

savePath.description: Destination /Game folder for a new Blueprint.

parentClass.description: Parent class path for Blueprint creation (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor).

properties.description: Property bag applied to the CDO, component template, or node: name to value. A dotted name reaches a member of a component or struct (CapsuleComponent.CapsuleRadius, BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); on a Blueprint's class defaults a native component also answers to its object name (CollisionCylinder.CapsuleRadius, CharMoveComp.MaxWalkSpeed). An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

blueprintType.description: Picks the parent class when parentClass is absent: Actor, Pawn, Character or FunctionLibrary; Interface makes a Blueprint Interface (its functions with add_function, taken on with implement_interface).

createIfMissing.description: Create the Blueprint when savePath/name does not exist (default true); false only reports whether it exists.

createMode.description: Which create variant to run; omit for 'create'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

appliedProperties.description: The properties names set on the class defaults; a subobject property reads Holder.Property.

failedProperties.description: Each properties name that was not set, as "Name: reason"; the Blueprint is created anyway.

saved.description: Whether the new Blueprint reached disk.

alreadyExists.description: True when a Blueprint of that parent class was already at the path; it is answered unchanged.

parentClass.description: Path of the Blueprint's parent class.

A parent that resolves to nothing is CLASS_NOT_FOUND, naming classes of that name. properties sets class defaults, Component.Property and struct members by dotted path, reported as appliedProperties and failedProperties (the create stands either way). A Blueprint already at the path is answered with alreadyExists and left unchanged; one with another parent class is ASSET_ALREADY_EXISTS.

whenNotToUse: The animation should only stop playing (change its loop or play mode instead).

discovery.summary: Delete Blueprint graph nodes (deleteScope node, the default), or disconnect every wire of one pin (pin_links). node deletes nodeId, or every node in nodeIds (up to 500), all or nothing: an id that matches no node is NODE_NOT_FOUND and a function entry or result node is PROTECTED_NODE, with nothing deleted; their wires go with them, and the reply lists the removed guids. pin_links breaks the links of pinName on nodeId (PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the pins the node has) and names the pins it was wired to under disconnectedFrom; a pin with no links changes nothing. Either is one undo step, then the Blueprint compiles (diagnostics when it no longer compiles) and is saved. A pinName sent with deleteScope node is refused (CONTRADICTORY_SCOPE) rather than deleting the whole node.
whenToUse: deleteScope=node: A graph node must be permanently removed.
deleteScope=node: A whole dead chain of nodes must be removed in one call.
deleteScope=pin_links: All links from a specific pin must be removed (disconnect or unlink a wire).
whenNotToUse: deleteScope=node: The node should be moved rather than deleted.
deleteScope=pin_links: A single link should be redirected (use connect_pins after breaking).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

nodeIds.description: Several node ids or guids to delete in one call, in place of nodeId. Every id must resolve to a deletable node or nothing is deleted.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

deleteScope.description: Which delete node variant to run; omit for 'node'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

removed.description: Guids of the nodes that were deleted.

brokenLinks.description: How many wires of the pin were broken (0 when it had none, and nothing changed).

disconnectedFrom.description: The pins it was wired to, each as nodeGuid.pinName.

examples.title: Delete Blueprint graph nodes (deleteScope node, the default), or disconnect every wire of one pin (pin_links). node deletes nodeId, or every node in nodeIds (up to 500), all or nothing: an id that matches no node is NODE_NOT_FOUND and a function entry or result node is PROTECTED_NODE, with nothing deleted; their wires go with them, and the reply lists the removed guids. pin_links breaks the links of pinName on nodeId (PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the pins the node has) and names the pins it was wired to under disconnectedFrom; a pin with no links changes nothing. Either is one undo step, then the Blueprint compiles (diagnostics when it no longer compiles) and is saved. A pinName sent with deleteScope node is refused (CONTRADICTORY_SCOPE) rather than deleting the whole node.

discovery.summary: Copy a widget and everything under it (a list row with its label, icon and button) inside a Widget Blueprint: same properties, slot layout and children, placed right after the original or under another panel.
whenToUse: A widget or a whole panel subtree is needed again, e.g. the next row of a list or a second button like the first.
whenNotToUse: The widget should move rather than be copied (use reparent_widget).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Widget to copy; everything under it is copied too.

newName.description: Name of the copy (default the original name with _Copy; _1, _2... is added when that name is taken). Every widget under it is copied as <its own name>_Copy, made unique the same way: copying QuitButton gives QuitButton_Copy and its label QuitButtonText_Copy. copiedWidgets lists the pairs.

newParent.description: Panel the copy goes under (default the parent of the original).

index.description: Position among the children of that panel (0 = first). Default: right after the original, or last under another panel.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: Name of the copy, for later calls.

index.description: Where the copy sits among the children of that panel (0 = first).

copiedWidgets.description: Every widget copied, as {source, copy} name pairs: the children come first, each copied as <source>_Copy, and the copy of the original comes last.
