discovery.summary: Write Blueprint logic of any kind, or edit a graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, arrange nodes beside what they are wired to, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.
whenToUse: edit=add_node: A node must be added using a friendly type alias (e.g. Branch, Cast, GetVariable).
edit=create_node: A new node must be placed in a Blueprint event or function graph.
edit=create_node: An animation node (Two Bone IK, Modify Bone, Blend Space Player, Look At ...) must be placed by class in an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph or a state's graph.
edit=create_reroute_node: Wire paths need a reroute node for cleaner layout.
edit=create_struct_make_break_nodes: A MakeStruct or BreakStruct node must be placed for a known struct type.
edit=connect_pins: An exec or data link between two existing nodes must be created.
edit=set_node_property: A node-level property (e.g. comment, position) must be updated.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A pin's default literal value must be set when it has no incoming link.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A read-only text, string, name or number pin (TextRender Set Text's Value) needs a literal.
edit=add_construction_script: The Construction Script graph must be created or opened for editing.
edit=arrange_nodes: Nodes of a chain sit far from each other or from the event they hang off, and should be laid out beside what they are wired to.
edit=batch: More than a couple of nodes or links must be added to one Blueprint graph.
edit=batch: A new function and the nodes inside it must be built in one call.
whenNotToUse: edit=connect_pins: Links must be broken (use break_pin_links).
edit=arrange_nodes: Every listed node is wired only to other listed nodes: nothing anchors them, so none moves; leave the head of the chain (its event) out of nodeIds.
edit=batch: Nodes or links must be deleted (use delete_node; destructive edits are not batched).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

nodeType.description: The node to create: CallFunction (memberName, plus memberClass for a function of another class), Event (eventName: BeginPlay, Tick), CustomEvent (customEventName), VariableGet or VariableSet (memberName), Cast (targetClass), InputAxisEvent (inputAxisName), Branch, Sequence, Select, Switch, SwitchOnInt, SwitchOnEnum (enumPath: one exec output per value, named after it), SwitchOnString, DoOnce, DoN, FlipFlop, Gate, MultiGate, ForLoop, ForEachLoop, WhileLoop (each also WithBreak), MakeArray, GetArrayItem (an array's Get: pins Array, Dimension 1 for the index, Output), MakeStruct and BreakStruct (structPath), SpawnActorFromClass, GetAllActorsOfClass, Self, CallDelegate (memberName: an event dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same, plus eventName: a Bind Event node and a custom event with the dispatcher's inputs wired to it, eventNodeGuid in the reply),Timeline (timelineName; edit_timeline keys its tracks), Reroute, Comment, MathExpression (its formula goes in set_node_property Expression) (a Switch on Int is made with only Default: wire a case by its number, from "$id.0", "$id.1"..., and the case pin is added; a Sequence or a commutative math node grows its inputs the same way); a common function by name (PrintString, Delay, SetActorLocation, GetPlayerPawn, GetActorOfClass, IsValid, PlaySound2D); or a K2Node class name that inspect_graph info=node_types lists. In an Animation Blueprint's AnimGraph or a state's graph (graphName), any animation node by class: AnimGraphNode_TwoBoneIK, TwoBoneIK or Two Bone IK (info=node_types with filter IK lists them; animation_physics configure_anim_graph_node set_value sets its settings); a node the graph cannot hold is refused (NODE_NOT_ALLOWED_IN_GRAPH). For create_struct_make_break_nodes: make or break.

posX.description: X position of the new node in the graph (default 0, the origin). add_node and create_node move a node given no position right past any node at the origin, and refuse a given spot another node covers (NODE_OVERLAP, with a suggestedPosition).

posY.description: Y position of the new node in the graph (default 0).

memberName.description: The function, variable or event the node uses (PrintString, GetGameTimeInSeconds). A function whose name is not known: inspect_graph info functions finds it by what it does. A variable Blueprints cannot read, or for VariableSet write (not Blueprint-visible, read-only), is refused with VARIABLE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE.

functionName.description: Function a CallFunction node calls (the same as memberName), e.g. PrintString.

targetClass.description: Target class for a node that carries one: a Cast target, a CreateWidget or SpawnActor class, the subsystem a Get Subsystem node returns, or the class GetAllActorsOfClass and GetActorOfClass look for (their result is then typed to it, so a ForEach element wires to its functions). Required for cast and subsystem nodes, whose type is stored on the node itself and cannot be set afterwards.

timelineName.description: For nodeType Timeline: the timeline it plays, which edit_timeline keys; a name the Blueprint lacks makes one (omitted, a new Timeline_N). One node plays a timeline, in the event graph of an Actor Blueprint.

pure.description: Build a Cast node pure (no exec pins, as in the editor's Convert to pure cast); default false.

memberClass.description: The class that declares the function (KismetMathLibrary, Character, or a Blueprint path); inspect_graph info functions names it. Omitted: the Blueprint itself and the common libraries are searched.

actorName.description: For nodeType K2Node_ActorBoundEvent or K2Node_Literal, which belong in a level Blueprint: the placed actor of its level (label, name or object path) the event fires for, with eventName one of its event dispatchers (OnActorBeginOverlap), or the node references. Without it, or outside a level Blueprint, the node is refused.

inputAxisName.description: Axis name for an InputAxis event node.

inputActionPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path for an EnhancedInputAction node.

inputActionAssetPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

actionPath.description: Enhanced Input action asset path accepted in place of inputActionPath.

structPath.description: For MakeStruct or BreakStruct: the struct, a Blueprint Struct asset (/Game/Data/F_Item) or a native one (/Script/SlateCore.SlateColor, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector); without it the node is refused.

enumPath.description: For SwitchOnEnum, ForEachElementInEnum, GetNumEnumEntries, EnumLiteral and CastByteToEnum: the enum whose values become the node's pins (a Switch on Enum's outputs are named after them), a Blueprint enum asset (/Game/Data/E_Phase) or a native one (/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); without it the node is refused.

parameters.description: CustomEvent inputs, each {name, type}: float, double, int, int64, bool, byte, string, name, text, object, class, softobject, an enum or struct name (Vector, Rotator, Transform, /Script/CoreUObject.Vector) or a class name (Actor) for an object of that class. An array, set or map parameter needs add_event. A nameless entry or another type is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes.

fromNodeId.description: Node the wire leaves (its nodeGuid, an 8+ hex prefix of it, or its node name); required, or send sourceNode.

fromPinName.description: Output pin it leaves from; required, or send sourcePin.

toNodeId.description: Node the wire enters; required, or send targetNode.

toPinName.description: Input pin it enters; required, or send targetPin.

sourceNode.description: Source node id accepted in place of fromNodeId.

targetNode.description: Target node id accepted in place of toNodeId.

sourcePin.description: Output pin name accepted in place of fromPinName.

targetPin.description: Input pin name accepted in place of toPinName.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

propertyName.description: Property name to set on the CDO or component.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

propertyValue.description: set_node_property: text for NodeComment, a number for NodePosX or NodePosY, true or false for bCommentBubbleVisible or bDisabled, Enabled, Disabled or DevelopmentOnly for EnabledState, the text of a Math Expression node's Expression (each other name becomes a number input pin, except one the Blueprint has a variable of, which reads that variable; a number input is never a vector, so add to a location as VECT(x, y, z + 20) from its parts; a comparison used as a number is refused: write SelectFloat(1, 0, A > B); an input pin is never true/false, so join true/false values from other nodes with BooleanAND, BooleanOR or BooleanXOR nodes), an asset path for a reflected field. set_pin_default_value: the pin's new default as text: a number, true or false, an enum value name, a vector as X,Y,Z (0,150,110), a rotator as P,Y,R, or an asset path.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

nodeIds.description: The nodes to move, by nodeId or nodeGuid. Nodes left out stay where they are and anchor the ones listed; a node wired to nothing left in place goes back where it was and is listed under unmoved.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...that edit's own params}. Member steps come before the nodes that use them: add_variable (variableName, variableType as add_variable takes it: basic, class, struct, enum and container types, defaultValue, isPublic, exposeOnSpawn, category), add_function (functionName, inputs, outputs, pure, isPublic; the create steps of its body set graphName to the function name, and a connect or pin step that leaves graphName out runs in the graph of the node it names; with an id, "$id" is its entry node and "$id_return" its return node, which exists when outputs are declared), add_event (customEventName and parameters, or componentName plus eventName for a component or Widget Blueprint widget delegate, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked) and add_event_dispatcher (dispatcherName, parameters [{name, type}]). Node steps: create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_default_value, set_node_property, create_reroute_node. create_node also takes nodeType CallDelegate (memberName: a dispatcher, memberClass: another class's), BindEvent (the same: a Bind Event node and a custom event, eventName, wired to it; with an id, "$id_event" is that event, whose then pin runs when the dispatcher fires, and the object bound goes to "$id.self"), Message (memberClass: an interface, memberName: its function), AsyncTask (memberClass: the task or async-action class, memberName: its static factory; event graphs only), FunctionResult (one more return node in a function graph) and MathExpression with expression (the formula, checked and set as set_node_property Expression sets it, before pinDefaults, which can then name its inputs; a name in the formula that is one of the Blueprint's variables reads that variable and gets no input pin, any other name becomes an input pin). Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in fromNodeId, toNodeId and nodeId), from and to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect_pins), pinDefaults (create_node only: {PinName: value} applied to the new node; a read-only pin such as Set Text's Value gets a MakeLiteral node wired into it). "$entry" is the graph's own entry node (a Construction Script or function graph starts there: from "$entry.then"). A pure node (math, a getter) runs again for each node that reads it, so after a Set node read the new value from the Set node's Output_Get pin, not from the math that computed it. A create step without posX and posY is auto-placed, and once every step ran it moves beside a node it is wired to (right of what runs it, below-left of what reads it); one whose posX and posY overlap an existing node is placed at the nearest free position instead, and its result says where in placementWarning, so a crowded row never stops the batch (a single create_node call still refuses an overlap). Every function, variable, dispatcher and async factory a step names is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one fails the batch with nothing applied; any other failure stops the batch at that step and undoes the steps before it (members, nodes, links and pin defaults, in every graph), so a failed batch leaves the Blueprint as it was: fix that step and send the whole batch again. Only a set_node_property on a node that was already there stays, and the error names it.

edit.description: Which edit graph variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeGuid.description: Unique node identifier for subsequent graph operations.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

timelineName.description: For a Timeline node: the timeline it plays, the name edit_timeline takes.

posX.description: X coordinate the node was placed at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node was placed at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width. Slate computes the real size at draw time, so this is derived from title length and is an estimate, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height, derived from pin-row count. Offset the next node by at least this much to avoid overlap.

overlappingNodes.description: Titles of existing nodes whose estimated bounds intersect this one. Empty or absent when placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

pinTypes.description: Per-pin objects: { name, direction, type, category, subCategory }.

compilerStatus.description: Blueprint status after compile (UpToDate, UpToDateWithWarnings, Error, Dirty, BeingCreated).

compiled.description: True when the Blueprint is up-to-date (warnings allowed).

assetPath.description: Asset path of the created node (verification).

existsAfter.description: Whether the node exists after creation (verification).

connected.description: Whether the two pins are linked after the call, directly or through the conversion node the engine inserted between differing pin types (conversionInserted), read back from the graph rather than inferred from the schema call.

sourcePinName.description: Source pin that was actually used — the first output pin when fromPinName named none.

targetPinName.description: Target pin that was actually used.

sourcePinType.description: Pin category of the source pin (exec, object, real, ...).

targetPinType.description: Pin category of the target pin.

blueprintPath.description: Normalized blueprint path the link was written to.

saved.description: Whether the blueprint asset was saved after the link was made.

replacedLinks.description: Links the new one replaced, each {nodeId, nodeTitle, pinName}: a pin that holds one link (an exec output, a data input) drops its old link to take the new one. Absent when nothing was replaced.

inputPins.description: Expression: the input pins the parsed expression made, the names to wire.

boundToMembers.description: Expression: names that read the Blueprint's own variable of that name instead of making a pin; rename the input to get a pin.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

pinName.description: Pin name on a graph node.

appliedValue.description: Literal actually stored on the pin (or the resolved object path for object/class pins).

literalNodeId.description: Guid of the MakeLiteral node carrying the value when the pin itself takes no literal; setting the pin again updates that node.

moved.description: Each node that moved: nodeId, nodeTitle and its new x and y.

unmoved.description: Ids of listed nodes that stayed where they were: wired to no node left in place, or no free slot near one.

results.description: Per-step outcome: index, edit, id, success, error, nodeGuid, resultNodeGuid (add_function), pins (for created nodes), connected, appliedValue, placementWarning (a create step that was moved off an overlapping position, or placed where it still overlaps), inputPins and boundToMembers (a Math Expression's Expression step: the pins it made, and the names that read member variables instead). A step that ran and has nothing more to say (a plain connect_pins, an add_variable) is counted in succeeded, not listed; a failed batch lists only the step that failed, with its error.

nodeIds.description: Step id -> node guid for every node the batch created or reused; an add_function step with an id also adds "<id>_return" for its return node. Absent when a step failed: its nodes were removed.

succeeded.description: Steps that completed; 0 when a step failed, since the steps before it were undone.

failedIndex.description: Index of the step that stopped the batch (failures only).

examples.title: Write Blueprint logic of any kind, or edit a graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, arrange nodes beside what they are wired to, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.

topics: make a component a child of another
discovery.summary: Change the components a Blueprint adds (its Simple Construction Script), chosen by edit; each edit saves the Blueprint unless save is false. add_scs_component (add_component is the same) adds componentName of componentClass under parentComponent (its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root; by default the root), with meshPath and materialPath (refused when they do not load or the class shows no mesh or material), location, rotation, scale and properties, and compiles; a taken name is refused, as is an add during Play. modify applies operations in order (add, modify, attach) or edits one component, naming each failed one in warnings (the call fails when none applied), and compiles only with compile or applyAndSave true; reparent moves a component under another; set_property and set_transform change one template and compile, and placed copies that kept the old value follow (instancesUpdated).
whenToUse: edit=add_scs_component: A component template must be owned by the SCS tree for instanced property overrides.
edit=add_component: A component must be added to a Blueprint under the add_component verb.
edit=modify: An SCS-owned component template needs property or transform updates.
edit=reparent: An SCS component must move under a different parent node.
edit=set_property: One property on an SCS component template must be changed.

edit=set_property: Collision of the template, for every placed copy: CollisionProfileName (a preset such as OverlapAllDynamic), CollisionEnabled, or CollisionResponses ({"Pawn": "Ignore"} lets a character walk through) go through the component setters, as does PhysMaterialOverride (a physical material path).
edit=set_transform: An SCS component template transform must be updated.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_scs_component: One placed actor needs the component, not every copy of the Blueprint (use control_actor.edit_component with edit=add).
edit=reparent: The component hierarchy does not need restructuring.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

componentClass.description: Component class path for SCS node creation.

componentName.description: Name for the SCS component node.

parentComponent.description: Parent component to put the component under: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's scene component, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

attachTo.description: Socket or parent component to attach to: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's part, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

meshPath.description: Static/Skeletal mesh asset path for a mesh component.

materialPath.description: Material asset path for a component.

location.description: Relative location {x, y, z} for an SCS component template.

rotation.description: Relative rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} for an SCS component template.

scale.description: Relative scale {x, y, z} for an SCS component template, or {x, y} for a widget render transform.

properties.description: Property bag applied to the CDO, component template, or node: name to value. A dotted name reaches a member of a component or struct (CapsuleComponent.CapsuleRadius, BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled); on a Blueprint's class defaults a native component also answers to its object name (CollisionCylinder.CapsuleRadius, CharMoveComp.MaxWalkSpeed). An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

save.description: Save the Blueprint after the edit (default true, so it survives an editor restart). false leaves it compiled in memory and unsaved: a trial change to put back, or to save later with control_editor save_all.

compile.description: Compile the Blueprint after the operations (default false; applyAndSave also compiles).

operations.description: SCS operations applied in order. Each entry is an object with `type` plus that operation's own fields; `type: "add_component"` also takes componentName, componentClass (or componentType), attachTo, transform, meshPath, materialPath and a nested properties bag; `type: "modify_component"` takes the same transform, meshPath, materialPath and properties for a component that already exists (its own, or a parent Blueprint's part, edited through this Blueprint's override of it); transform is {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}} (or those three directly on the operation), and a part left out keeps its current value, while a transform that cannot be applied (a part that is not an {x,y,z} or {pitch,yaw,roll} object or a three-number array, or a component with no transform) is named in warnings, not skipped, as is a meshPath or materialPath that does not load or that its component cannot take; `type: "attach_component"` (or "reparent") moves componentName under parentComponent (or attachTo/newParent). A failed operation is named in warnings, and the call fails when none applied. Each result carries instancesUpdated (placed copies that took the change, 0 included) with up to three of their paths, and a hint, repeated in warnings, when a mesh or material lands on a hidden component.

applyAndSave.description: Whether to save the Blueprint after applying SCS changes.

propertyName.description: Property name to set on the CDO or component.

propertyValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

edit.description: Which edit scs variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Name for the SCS component node.

componentClass.description: Component class path for SCS node creation.

parent.description: Parent component to put the component under: one of this Blueprint's own, a parent Blueprint's scene component, or a native one (Mesh, CapsuleComponent).

saved.description: Whether the action succeeded.

appliedProperties.description: The names in properties that took their value; one that did not apply fails the call and is named in the error.

partWarnings.description: Mesh parts this edit left sunk or buried, worst first (at most 8, each also a warnings[] sentence): componentName, kind (sunk: below the actor's ground, a Character's capsule bottom; buried: inside otherComponent), depth in cm, insideShare (0-1, how much of the part's surface is inside the other) and issue. Measured on the real triangles of a preview instance, not on bounds. A part tagged mcp.placement.ok (set ComponentTags to ["mcp.placement.ok"]) is a deliberate embed, such as an eyeball in its socket, and is left out; mcp.placement.ok:<component> accepts the embed in that one part only (a neck in its collar, a hand round a handle) and keeps every other check. control_actor.audit_placement with blueprintPath lists every part of the Blueprint.

verifiedValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

examples.title: Change the components a Blueprint adds (its Simple Construction Script), chosen by edit; each edit saves the Blueprint unless save is false. add_scs_component (add_component is the same) adds componentName of componentClass under parentComponent (its own part, a parent Blueprint's, or the native root; by default the root), with meshPath and materialPath (refused when they do not load or the class shows no mesh or material), location, rotation, scale and properties, and compiles; a taken name is refused, as is an add during Play. modify applies operations in order (add, modify, attach) or edits one component, naming each failed one in warnings (the call fails when none applied), and compiles only with compile or applyAndSave true; reparent moves a component under another; set_property and set_transform change one template and compile, and placed copies that kept the old value follow (instancesUpdated).

discovery.summary: Make or change a Blueprint timeline, what a Timeline node plays: its length, autoplay and loop, and its float, vector, color and event tracks with their keys. The Timeline node gets a pin per track, and its Update pin fires every frame while it plays.
whenToUse: Something must change smoothly over a set time from a Blueprint (a door swinging open, a platform sliding, a light fading): key a float track from 0 to 1 and feed it to a Lerp on the Timeline node's Update.
whenNotToUse: A cinematic or a camera move is needed (use a level sequence).
A widget must animate (use edit_widget_animation).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

timelineName.description: The timeline, as its node is titled. A name the Blueprint lacks makes one; the node that plays it comes from edit_graph create_node nodeType Timeline with this timelineName, made before or after (either way it shows a pin per track).

length.description: How long it plays, in seconds (a new timeline: 5).

useLastKeyframe.description: End at the last key instead of at length.

autoPlay.description: Start when the game starts, without a Play call.

loop.description: Start over at the end, again and again.

ignoreTimeDilation.description: Play at real speed while the game is slowed down or sped up.

tracks.description: Tracks to add, or whose keys to replace (a track keeps its type): each {name, type, keys, interpolation}. name is the node pin its value comes out of; type float (default), vector, color or event (an exec pin that fires at each key time); keys [{time in seconds, value}], value a number, {x, y, z} or {r, g, b, a} by type and none for an event; interpolation auto (smooth, default), linear or constant. Every track is checked before anything changes; a bad one is named by its index (tracks[1].keys[0]).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

created.description: True when this call made the timeline.

useLastKeyframe.description: Whether it ends at its last key.

autoPlay.description: Whether it starts on its own.

tracks.description: Every track: name (its node pin), type and keys (the key count).

nodeGuid.description: The Timeline node that plays it; absent until one is made.

examples.title: Make or change a Blueprint timeline, what a Timeline node plays: its length, autoplay and loop, and its float, vector, color and event tracks with their keys. The Timeline node gets a pin per track, and its Update pin fires every frame while it plays.

discovery.summary: Change a Blueprint's variables, chosen by edit. add_variable adds variableName of variableType with defaultValue, category and the isPublic, isReplicated and exposeOnSpawn flags (a taken name is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, a default the type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then); rename_variable renames a variable or a component and its graph nodes follow; set_variable_metadata sets a variable's tooltip, category or replication; set_metadata sets metadata pairs on the class or one variable; set_default writes a class default value, an inherited property included.
whenToUse: edit=add_variable: A Blueprint needs a new member variable with a type and default.
edit=rename_variable: A member variable needs a new name.
edit=rename_variable: A component (Simple Construction Script node) needs a new name.
edit=set_variable_metadata: Variable metadata such as tooltip or category must be updated.
edit=set_metadata: Freeform metadata must be attached to a Blueprint or its members.
edit=set_default: A default property must be set on the CDO; if the property denotes a component, the component CDO is targeted.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_variable: A graph-local variable is needed (use create_node with a local variable).
edit=rename_variable: The variable should be removed rather than renamed.
edit=set_default: An SCS component template property is the target (use set_scs_property).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

variableName.description: Variable name to add, remove, rename, or modify.

variableType.description: Variable type, any case. Basic: Boolean, Byte, Integer, Int64, Float, Double, String, Name, Text, Vector, Vector2D, Vector4, Rotator, Transform, Color, LinearColor. References: Object or Class (any UObject), or Object:<class>, Class:<class>, SoftObject:<class>, SoftClass:<class> with a class name or path (Actor, /Script/UMG.Widget, /Game/Blueprints/BP_Door); a bare class name or path is an object reference to that class. Structs: struct:<path> (struct:/Game/Data/F_Item), a /Script path (/Script/Engine.HitResult) or a struct name (HitResult). Enums: enum:<object path> (enum:/Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel, enum:/Game/Enums/E_State.E_State). Containers: Array<T>, Set<T> or Map<Key,Value> (also Array:T, Set:T, Map:Key,Value); a map key is Byte, Integer, Int64, Name, String or an enum. Example: Array<Object:/Script/UMG.Widget>. An unknown spelling is refused with TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED and the reason.

defaultValue.description: Default value for the variable, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 100} for a Vector, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}). A value its type cannot take is refused with DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED and the variable is not added.

isPublic.description: Instance Editable (the editor's eye toggle): true, the default when left out, shows the variable on placed instances in the Details panel; false keeps it to the Blueprint itself.

exposeOnSpawn.description: Expose on Spawn: the variable becomes an input pin on SpawnActor and Create Widget nodes for this class, set as the actor is made (before its BeginPlay). Makes it instance-editable too, as the editor does.

oldName.description: Current name of the variable or component.

newName.description: New name for a renamed variable, function, or component.

variableNames.description: Several variables to give the same metadata in one call (one compile and save), in place of or besides variableName.

propertyName.description: A member variable to put the metadata on (as set_variable_metadata does); omitted, the keys go on the Blueprint class.

propertyValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

edit.description: Which edit variable variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

variableName.description: Variable name to add, remove, rename, or modify.

variableNames.description: Every variable that took the metadata.

value.description: Property value re-read from the Class Default Object after the write. Emitted on the literal path only and omitted when the value cannot be exported to JSON.

instancesUpdated.description: Placed actors (in loaded levels) that still held the old default and took the new value, as the Details panel propagates a class default; an actor that overrides the value keeps it. Save the level to keep them.

examples.title: Change a Blueprint's variables, chosen by edit. add_variable adds variableName of variableType with defaultValue, category and the isPublic, isReplicated and exposeOnSpawn flags (a taken name is VARIABLE_NAME_CONFLICT, a type that resolves to nothing TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED, a default the type refuses DEFAULT_NOT_APPLIED; nothing is added then); rename_variable renames a variable or a component and its graph nodes follow; set_variable_metadata sets a variable's tooltip, category or replication; set_metadata sets metadata pairs on the class or one variable; set_default writes a class default value, an inherited property included.

discovery.summary: Build a widget animation, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes a named animation of a given length (a taken name is refused), add_track gives one widget an opacity, color or render-transform track, add_keyframe keys a value at a time on a widget (adding the track and binding when missing) or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys, all checked before any is written). get_widget_animation reads it back.
whenToUse: edit=create: A new UMG widget animation must be created for property keyframing.
edit=add_track: A widget needs an empty property track in a widget animation before keys are added.
edit=add_keyframe: A property value must be keyframed at a specific time in a widget animation.
edit=add_keyframe: A whole widget animation (a logo popping in, a menu sliding up, a pulse) must be keyed in one call (keys).
whenNotToUse: edit=create: A Blueprint graph animation is needed (use animation_physics).
edit=create: An animation must be seen playing in PIE: write the value that sets it off with inspect.set_property and watch (a short pop ends before a later call can read it).
edit=add_keyframe: The track should be removed rather than keyframed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

trackType.description: Animation track type: opacity/renderOpacity (RenderOpacity), color (ColorAndOpacity), translation/scale/angle/shear or transform (RenderTransform).

slotName.description: Name of the widget in the widget tree that the track animates.

propertyValue.description: The key value, by trackType: opacity a number 0-1; color {r,g,b,a} or [r,g,b,a]; translation, scale or shear {x,y} or [x,y]; angle a number in degrees; transform any of {translation:{x,y}, scale:{x,y}, angle, shear:{x,y}}. A value of the wrong shape is refused before anything is added.

value.description: A plain number for an opacity or angle key, in place of propertyValue.

keys.description: Many keyframes in one call, in place of time: each {time, propertyValue or value, and any of slotName, trackType, interpolation that differ from the call's own}. Every key is checked before any is written: a refused one is named by its index (keys[3]) and nothing is added. The Widget Blueprint is saved once.

edit.description: Which edit widget animation variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

duration.description: Length of the new animation in seconds.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

slotName.description: Widget the track animates.

propertyName.description: Widget property driven by the track (RenderOpacity, ColorAndOpacity, RenderTransform).

trackClass.description: MovieScene track class that owns the section.

createdTrack.description: Whether the property track was created by this call.

createdBinding.description: Whether the widget binding was created by this call.

bindingGuid.description: MovieScene possessable GUID bound to the widget.

keysAdded.description: With keys: how many keyframes were added; the other fields describe the last one.

frameNumber.description: Key position in MovieScene tick-resolution frames.

keyCount.description: Keys on the last channel written after this call.

examples.title: Build a widget animation, chosen by edit, each saved: create makes a named animation of a given length (a taken name is refused), add_track gives one widget an opacity, color or render-transform track, add_keyframe keys a value at a time on a widget (adding the track and binding when missing) or a whole animation across several widgets in one call (keys, all checked before any is written). get_widget_animation reads it back.

discovery.summary: Create or restructure a Widget Blueprint, chosen by edit. create makes one named name in path (default /Game/UI), or at widgetPath, from parentClass (default UserWidget; a native widget class or a Widget Blueprint class path, anything else INVALID_PARENT_CLASS), with an empty widget tree, then compiles and saves it (compileSucceeded, saveSucceeded); a taken path is ALREADY_EXISTS. set_parent_class reparents it to a UserWidget class or Widget Blueprint, refreshes, compiles and saves (INVALID_CLASS, CYCLIC_PARENT). rename_widget renames slotName to newName and carries graph references, bindings, animations and navigation along (ALREADY_EXISTS, NAME_CONFLICT). reparent_widget moves slotName under the panel newParent at index (default last; the same parent reorders), keeping its slot layout; a move under its own child is INVALID_PARENT.
whenToUse: edit=create: A new UMG Widget Blueprint must be created.
edit=set_parent_class: A Widget Blueprint must inherit from a specific UserWidget subclass.
edit=rename_widget: A widget name must change so bindings and lookups can address it.
edit=reparent_widget: An existing widget must move into another panel without being recreated.
edit=reparent_widget: Children of a panel must be reordered (same newParent, with index).
whenNotToUse: edit=create: A non-widget Blueprint is needed (use create or create_blueprint).
edit=set_parent_class: The Widget Blueprint already has the correct parent.
edit=rename_widget: A Blueprint or Widget Blueprint asset itself should be renamed (use asset.rename).
edit=reparent_widget: The widget is being added for the first time (use the matching add action).

path.description: Destination /Game folder for a new Widget Blueprint.

folder.description: Destination /Game folder for a Widget Blueprint.

newName.description: New name for a renamed variable, function, or component.

newName.description: New name for a renamed variable, function, or component.

animationBindingsRenamed.description: Animation bindings that now name the widget by newName.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

index.description: Where the widget now sits among the children of the new parent (0 = first).

applied.description: The widget as it is now: visibility, renderOpacity, renderTransform, slotClass, and the canvas anchors, alignment, position, size, zOrder and autoSize or the box padding and horizontal and vertical alignment.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

examples.title: Create or restructure a Widget Blueprint, chosen by edit. create makes one named name in path (default /Game/UI), or at widgetPath, from parentClass (default UserWidget; a native widget class or a Widget Blueprint class path, anything else INVALID_PARENT_CLASS), with an empty widget tree, then compiles and saves it (compileSucceeded, saveSucceeded); a taken path is ALREADY_EXISTS. set_parent_class reparents it to a UserWidget class or Widget Blueprint, refreshes, compiles and saves (INVALID_CLASS, CYCLIC_PARENT). rename_widget renames slotName to newName and carries graph references, bindings, animations and navigation along (ALREADY_EXISTS, NAME_CONFLICT). reparent_widget moves slotName under the panel newParent at index (default last; the same parent reorders), keeping its slot layout; a move under its own child is INVALID_PARENT.

discovery.summary: Read a Blueprint, chosen by info. blueprint returns its parent class, type, compile status (hasCompileErrors), variables (name, type, category, replication, default), functions with their parameters, events, graphs with node counts, components (name, class, parent, root) and class defaults; property reads one value from its class defaults: propertyName is a variable or inherited property, or Component.Property for a component it adds, and a name found nowhere is PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its variables.
whenToUse: info=blueprint: Blueprint parent class, components, or variables must be inspected.
info=property: A single property must be read from the Blueprint CDO.
info=property: One default of a Blueprint component must be read, for example Shield.bVisible.
whenNotToUse: info=blueprint: The full graph or node details are needed (use blueprint.inspect_graph).

One it finds nowhere is refused with PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing the variables. Omitted, the reply is the whole Blueprint summary, as get_blueprint gives.

info.description: Which get blueprint variant to run; omit for 'blueprint'.

hasCompileErrors.description: Whether the last compile reported errors.

items.description: Variable entry: name, type, category, replication, default value.

defaults.description: Class default values keyed by variable name: a bool as true/false, anything else as its property text.

metadata.description: Blueprint metadata recorded by the bridge.

propertyValue.description: Value to assign to the property. An object or class reference takes a path (a Blueprint class path ends in _C); null or "None" clears it.

examples.title: Read a Blueprint, chosen by info. blueprint returns its parent class, type, compile status (hasCompileErrors), variables (name, type, category, replication, default), functions with their parameters, events, graphs with node counts, components (name, class, parent, root) and class defaults; property reads one value from its class defaults: propertyName is a variable or inherited property, or Component.Property for a component it adds, and a name found nowhere is PROPERTY_NOT_FOUND, listing its variables.

topics: search blueprints for a component class
discovery.summary: List a Blueprint's own components (SCS nodes) with class, parent, root flag and relative transform, plus the components it inherits from parent Blueprints and its native parent class; or, given a folder (path) and componentClass, every Blueprint under it that has such a component, owned or inherited.
whenToUse: The SCS node hierarchy must be inspected before modifying components.
An inherited component must be named as an attach parent for add_scs_component.
Every Blueprint with a kind of component (a TextRender label, a light, an audio source) must be found in one call: path plus componentClass.
whenNotToUse: A single component property is needed (use get or set_scs_property).
The assets that use a Blueprint are wanted (use asset.inspect_asset lookup=dependencies with referencers true).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: A folder (e.g. /Game/Blueprints) to scan instead of one Blueprint: each Blueprint under it, subfolders included, that has a component matching componentClass, its own or inherited, is listed under blueprints (at most 300 Blueprints are opened; truncated says when more exist).

componentClass.description: Only components of this class or a subclass, by name part or /Script path: "TextRender" matches TextRenderComponent, "PointLight" PointLightComponent, "PrimitiveComponent" every primitive. Filters one Blueprint's listing too.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

components.description: SCS node descriptors with name, class, and parent.

inheritedComponents.description: Components inherited from parent Blueprints (their own components) and from the native parent class (a Character's CollisionCylinder): componentName, componentType, isSceneComponent, ownerClass, and overridden when this Blueprint restyled the part. A scene component of either kind is valid as parentComponent or attachTo.

blueprints.description: With path: each matching Blueprint as blueprintPath and components (componentName, componentType; inherited and ownerClass on one it inherits), in path order.

blueprintCount.description: With path: how many Blueprints matched.

scanned.description: With path: how many Blueprints were opened.

truncated.description: With path: true when the folder holds more than 300 Blueprints and the rest were not opened.

examples.title: List a Blueprint's own components (SCS nodes) with class, parent, root flag and relative transform, plus the components it inherits from parent Blueprints and its native parent class; or, given a folder (path) and componentClass, every Blueprint under it that has such a component, owned or inherited.

discovery.summary: Read a Widget Blueprint's animations: without animationName, each one's length and track count; with it, every widget the animation drives and each track's keys per channel (translation.x, angle, scale.x, r, value ...) as [seconds, value] pairs, the names add_animation_keyframe takes.
whenToUse: An animation built with add_animation_keyframe must be checked: which widgets it moves, when, and to what values.
An existing menu or HUD animation must be understood before it is changed.
whenNotToUse: Only the animation names or the widget tree are needed (use get_widget_info).

durationSeconds.description: With animationName: the animation's length in seconds.

trackCount.description: With animationName: tracks in the animation, those on its widgets included.

widgets.description: With animationName: each widget it drives, by its name in the widget tree.

items.description: {widget, tracks: [{property (RenderTransform, RenderOpacity, ColorAndOpacity ...), kind (transform, float, color, or the track class), channels: {name: [[seconds, value], ...]}}]}; at most 100 keys a channel.

examples.title: Read a Widget Blueprint's animations: without animationName, each one's length and track count; with it, every widget the animation drives and each track's keys per channel (translation.x, angle, scale.x, r, value ...) as [seconds, value] pairs, the names add_animation_keyframe takes.

discovery.summary: Read a Widget Blueprint: its widget tree (each widget with its class and parent, so a panel's children), or one slot layout (padding, alignment, size rule).

info=slot: The layout of a single widget must be inspected before adjusting it.
whenNotToUse: info=widget: A single widget property is needed (use get or set_style).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

widgetClass.description: Widget class, e.g. TextBlock or CanvasPanel.

slotClass.description: Class of the slot holding this widget (omitted when it occupies none).

isVariable.description: Whether the widget is exposed as a Blueprint variable.

text.description: Literal text of a TextBlock or button label (omitted for widgets that carry none).

rootWidget.description: Name of the widget tree root (omitted when the tree is empty).

animations.description: Names of the Widget Blueprint animations.

assetPath.description: Asset path of the inspected Widget Blueprint (verification).

assetName.description: Asset name of the inspected Widget Blueprint (verification).

existsAfter.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint exists after inspection (verification).

assetClass.description: Class of the inspected Widget Blueprint (verification).

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

widgetClass.description: Class name of the inspected widget.

isVisible.description: Whether the widget draws, derived from `visibility` (false only for Collapsed and Hidden).

visibility.description: The widget's design-time Visibility, the same value set_visibility writes.

slotClass.description: Class name of the slot holding the widget (omitted when the widget occupies no slot).

canvasSlotInfo.description: Canvas geometry of the widget (omitted unless the slot is a canvas panel slot).

discovery.summary: Make a Blueprint implement an interface (a Blueprint Interface asset or a native interface class), or drop it with remove. The reply lists the interface functions that became graphs to fill and the ones that are events to handle.
whenToUse: Actors must talk without casting to each other: make the interface (create with blueprintType Interface, its functions with add_function), then implement it on each class that answers.
whenNotToUse: Only one known class is ever called: a cast node is simpler (edit_graph).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

interfacePath.description: The interface: a Blueprint Interface asset path (/Game/Interfaces/BPI_Interactable) or a native interface class path or name.

remove.description: Drop the interface instead (its function graphs go with it).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

interfaces.description: Every interface the Blueprint implements now.

functionGraphs.description: Interface functions with outputs: graphs to fill (edit_graph graphName).

events.description: Interface functions without outputs: events to handle in the event graph.

changed.description: False when the Blueprint was already in the asked state.

examples.title: Make a Blueprint implement an interface (a Blueprint Interface asset or a native interface class), or drop it with remove. The reply lists the interface functions that became graphs to fill and the ones that are events to handle.

discovery.summary: Inspect a Blueprint graph: its nodes (every one, those whose title, pin default, text or object path matches a filter, or the unused ones), node details, pin details, the available node types, or the functions a node can call found by what they do in plain words (game time, random number in range), with the memberName, memberClass and pins create_node takes.
whenToUse: info=graph: The full node list of a graph must be inspected in one call.
info=graph: A large graph must be read in parts: filter by node title or by what a pin holds, page with offset/limit.
info=graph: The node that builds or uses a given asset, class or literal must be found, e.g. the Create Widget node for WBP_MainMenu.
info=graph: Leftovers must be found after an edit: unusedOnly lists the nodes that do nothing, to delete them.
info=graph: A level Blueprint's nodes must be read: blueprintPath takes the path of a level open in the editor (/Game/Maps/L_Main).
info=node: A single node's pins, type, and links must be inspected.
info=node: What an event or function does must be read: followExec on its entry node lists every node its exec wires reach, with their inputs, in one call.
info=pins: Pin-level details including linkedTo connections must be inspected for a single node.
info=node_types: The set of creatable node types must be enumerated before node creation.
info=node_types: An animation graph node class must be found by part of its name (filter IK, Blend, Bone) before create_node places it in an AnimGraph.
info=functions: A graph needs a node whose function name or class is not known: get memberName, memberClass and the pin names before create_node or a batch.
info=functions: A create_node or batch step failed with FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND: find the function by what it does.
info=functions: What an object of a class can do must be listed (memberClass Character, words jump).
whenNotToUse: info=node_types: A specific node type is already known.
info=functions: The function name and class are already known (create_node directly).
info=functions: The node is not a function call (Branch, Cast, a loop, an array's Get, which is nodeType GetArrayItem, a timeline): node_types lists those.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

graphName.description: Target graph name (Event Graph, Construction Script, etc.).

includePins.description: When true, graph details include per-node pins and links.

filter.description: Only nodes whose title or name, or whose pin default value or default object path, contains this text (case-insensitive, spaces ignored), e.g. "IA_Move", "Set bLocked", or "WBP_MainMenu" for the Create Widget node whose Class pin holds /Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu.WBP_MainMenu_C; or whose input is wired from a variable or component of that name, so "Arm" lists every node that reads or moves the Arm component (find each writer before driving it from Tick).

unusedOnly.description: Only nodes that do nothing: a call no exec wire reaches, or a getter, math or other pure node whose result nothing reads (what is left behind when the node that read it was deleted; the compiler says nothing). Events, input actions and function entries never count. Combines with filter.

offset.description: Skip this many matching nodes (paging).

limit.description: Return at most this many nodes; totalCount and hasMore say what is left. Use it with includePins on a big graph.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

nodeGuid.description: Node GUID accepted in place of nodeId.

followExec.description: Also walk this many nodes (1-50) along the exec wires leaving the node, depth-first (a Branch's then side before its else), and list each under chain with its inputs.

pinName.description: Report only this pin; omitted, every pin on the node.

words.description: A few plain words for what the node does (game time, random number in range, distance between actors); a function matches on its name, keywords, category and description, best first, at most 10.

memberClass.description: Only functions an object of this class calls on itself (Character, or a Blueprint path), no library functions.

info.description: Which inspect graph variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodes.description: Node descriptors (nodeId, nodeName, nodeTitle, and position x and y; pins if includePins=true).

hasMore.description: More matches lie past the ones returned.

nodeId.description: Id of an existing node: the nodeGuid edit_graph returned when it made the node, or a nodeId inspect_graph lists.

nodeComment.description: Node comment, empty when it has none.

x.description: Node X position in the graph.

y.description: Node Y position in the graph.

pins.description: Pin descriptors (pinName, direction, pinType, pinSubType: the class, struct or enum it carries, container: array, set or map when the pin holds many pinType values, valueType: the value type of a map, linkedTo[] of {nodeId, pinName, nodeTitle}, and for a visible input nothing is wired to the literal it holds: defaultValue, defaultTextValue or defaultObjectPath).

animationAsset.description: An animation graph node that plays an asset (a Sequence Player, a Blend Space Player ...): the path of the animation it plays. Absent on other nodes and on a player with no asset.

animationAssetClass.description: The class of that animation asset (AnimSequence, BlendSpace ...).

settings.description: An animation graph node's editable settings, name to value (a Sequence Player: Sequence, PlayRate, StartPosition, bLoopAnimation ...; at most 24, lists left out). Absent on any other node. graphName is the AnimGraph, or the name of the state whose graph holds the node.

chain.description: With followExec: each node the exec wires reach, in walk order: nodeId, nodeTitle, via (the "Title.Pin" exec output that led to it) and inputs (each input pin as its literal value, or "<- Title.Pin" for the node feeding it).

className.description: Node class name, the nodeType create_node takes (K2Node_CallFunction, AnimGraphNode_TwoBoneIK).

displayName.description: Localized node display name shown in the Blueprint palette.

nodeTypes.description: Available Blueprint node types, each an object with className and displayName.

count.description: Total number of node types listed.

memberName.description: The function name create_node takes as memberName.

memberClass.description: The class create_node takes as memberClass (/Script/Engine.KismetSystemLibrary).

displayName.description: The node title the editor shows.

category.description: Its palette category (Math|Random), empty when it has none.

pure.description: A pure node: no exec pins, its outputs are read where they are wired.

latent.description: True for a latent node, one that finishes later as Delay does: it works in an event graph, never inside a function.

target.description: The class of object it acts on, wired to its Target (self) pin; on a Blueprint of that class an unwired Target is the Blueprint itself. Absent for a library function.

description.description: The first line of its tooltip.

pinType.description: The pin category: bool, int, real, string, text, name, byte, struct, object, class or wildcard.

pinSubType.description: The class, struct or enum it carries.

container.description: array, set or map when it holds many.

valueType.description: The value type of a map.

inputs.description: Its input pins besides exec and Target.

pinType.description: The pin category: bool, int, real, string, text, name, byte, struct, object, class or wildcard.

pinSubType.description: The class, struct or enum it carries.

container.description: array, set or map when it holds many.

valueType.description: The value type of a map.

outputs.description: Its output pins besides exec; ReturnValue is the result.

examples.title: Inspect a Blueprint graph: its nodes (every one, those whose title, pin default, text or object path matches a filter, or the unused ones), node details, pin details, the available node types, or the functions a node can call found by what they do in plain words (game time, random number in range), with the memberName, memberClass and pins create_node takes.

discovery.summary: Look at a Widget Blueprint without running the game: it is drawn offscreen for a screen size and returned as a PNG image, as the game creates it: Construct graphs do not run, so texts are the designer defaults, and widgets set Collapsed or Hidden stay hidden.
whenToUse: A Widget Blueprint must be seen after an edit (layout, colours, fonts) without running PIE.
whenNotToUse: What the running game shows is needed, runtime texts included (play, then control_editor screenshot mode full_editor_window).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

resolution.description: Screen size the widget is drawn for, "WxH" (default "1280x720"); the project DPI scaling for that size applies, as in the game.

openEditor.description: Also open it in the Widget Blueprint editor, which takes focus (default false).

waitForShaders.description: true: when the drawing left shaders compiling (the editor compiles a material's UI shaders the first time it is drawn: right after the editor starts, or after a material edit), wait for them, at most 25 seconds, and draw again; shaderWait in the reply says how long it waited. Default false: draw once and report shadersCompiling.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

imageBase64.description: The drawn widget as PNG, base64; returned as an image.

editorOpened.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint editor was opened (openEditor).

shadersCompiling.description: Shader compile jobs still outstanding when the widget was drawn. Above 0, images and borders that use a material may be drawn blank and a warning says so; pass waitForShaders to draw after they finish.

shaderWait.description: With waitForShaders while shaders compiled: waitedSeconds, jobsLeft (still outstanding when the wait ended) and timedOut (true when jobs were left after the 25 second cap).

discovery.summary: Remove a function the Blueprint defines (kind function: functionName), recompiled and saved; one still called is refused with FUNCTION_IN_USE naming each call node to delete first, and inherited or engine functions are NOT_FOUND. kind=event: An event node must be permanently removed from the graph.
whenNotToUse: kind=function: The function should be renamed rather than removed.
kind=event: The event should be reconnected rather than removed.

graphName.description: Event graph page to search; omitted, the main EventGraph.

sizeRule.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: Auto sizes it to its content, Fill shares the free space between the Fill children by their fillValue weights (case-insensitive). Two buttons in a row that should share it evenly are both Fill with the same fillValue; a ScrollBox child that is Fill spans the box when it is shorter, so a vertical alignment of center can center it.

fillValue.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: the Fill weight, 0 or more (1 by default; a child of 2 gets twice the space of a child of 1). Given without sizeRule it makes the child Fill.

alignment.description: CanvasPanel child: the pivot {x, y}, each 0-1. Any other slot (box, overlay, border, scroll box): x is the horizontal and y the vertical alignment, each a number (0 left/top, 0.5 center, 1 right/bottom) or a word: "fill", "left", "center", "right", "top", "bottom"; leave one out to keep it. {"x": "fill", "y": "center"} spans the width and centers vertically.

scale.description: Relative scale {x, y, z} for an SCS component template, or {x, y} for a widget render transform.

text.description: Text content for a text block or button.

texturePath.description: Texture asset path for an image or brush.

renderOpacity.description: Render opacity (0-1) applied to the widget and everything under it.

propertyName.description: Any other widget property, by reflection (such as WidgetStyle or Brush): read without value, written with it. A dotted path reaches into a struct: Font.OutlineSettings.OutlineSize (a number) outlines the text of a TextBlock and Font.OutlineSettings.OutlineColor colors that outline; ShadowOffset ({X, Y}) with ShadowColorAndOpacity gives it a drop shadow.

value.description: New value for propertyName: a string, number or bool, or an object or array for a struct property.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for a widget that draws a brush (Image, Button, Border). Switches the brush to a RoundedBox; 0 restores square corners.

outlineColor.description: Outline color (0-1 values) drawn around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

outlineWidth.description: Outline thickness in pixels around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

hoverSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when the pointer moves onto it (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

pressSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when it is pressed (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

justification.description: Text justification of a TextBlock or RichTextBlock: left, center or right. To centre the widget itself in its slot use set_alignment.

fontFamily.description: Font asset for a TextBlock, e.g. /Engine/EngineFonts/Roboto or a project font.

typeface.description: Face of the TextBlock font: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light... A face the font lacks is refused with the list it has.

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between the letters of a TextBlock, in thousandths of an em (0 normal, 100 airy, negative tighter).

copyStyleFrom.description: Name of another TextBlock in the same Widget Blueprint whose font, colour and shadow this one takes; the other fields in the call then apply on top.

layoutProperty.description: Which set widget layout variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

applied.description: The widget as it is now: visibility, renderOpacity, renderTransform, slotClass, and the canvas anchors, alignment, position, size, zOrder and autoSize or the box padding and horizontal and vertical alignment.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

appliedFields.description: set_style: the style fields that were written (text, fontSize, colorAndOpacity, cornerRadius...).

discovery.summary: Change a water body, chosen by setting: the one named by waterBodyName, targetActor or actorName, else the level's first. waves gives it Gerstner waves (waveHeight, waveLength, steepness, direction) that its surface and anything floating on it follow, and fails when the body does not keep them; material sets the material that draws its surface (its WaterMaterial, read back as waterMaterial; a material without the Used with Water usage gains it and is left unsaved); collision turns collision on its components on or off (collisionEnabled); settings writes water body actor properties by engine name. material and collision are one undo step; a call with nothing to set, or whose settings name nothing the body has, is refused, and a material that does not load fails the call.

waveHeight.description: Height (amplitude) of the largest wave in cm; the body's other waves shrink to 15% of it, as a real sea's do. A calm harbour is about 5-10, open sea 50 or more.

waveLength.description: Wavelength of the longest wave in cm, crest to crest; the shortest waves are 13% of it (a harbour is about 1500-2500).

amplitude.description: Same as waveHeight; waveHeight wins when both are given.

steepness.description: Crest sharpness of the short waves, 0 (smooth swell) to 1 (peaked); the long waves take about half. Keep it under about 0.3: steep crests from many waves fold the surface over itself.

direction.description: Wind direction: its yaw sets where the waves travel.

discovery.summary: Create a light actor in the level being edited: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (or any light class), at location (default 0, 0, 300), made Movable, with intensity, color and, in properties, shadow, radius and cone settings. The reply lists what was applied, refused (a setting this kind of light lacks) or adjusted; the spawn is one undo step and the level is left unsaved. During Play it still goes into the edited level, not the running game.
whenToUse: A point, spot, directional, rect or sky light must be added to the level being edited, with its intensity, color or shadow settings.
whenNotToUse: An existing light should be reconfigured: control_actor.edit_component sets its component values.
The light must exist in the running PIE world: manage_effect.create_dynamic_light spawns into the active world, this one into the level being edited.
manage_level.create_light runs this same handler; use this one, which documents every property.
The light is always created Movable; a static or stationary light needs its mobility changed afterwards with control_actor.edit_component.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

lightType.description: Light kind: point, spot, directional, rect or sky (any case), or the class name PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight or SkyLight. A light class of your own goes in lightClass.

lightClass.description: Light class name or path, for a class lightType does not name, including a Blueprint light (/Game/Lights/BP_Lamp.BP_Lamp_C); build_environment list_light_types lists the loaded ones. Wins over lightType.

name.description: Name for the new actor, asset, or volume.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}; 0, 0, 300 when omitted.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees. A spot or directional light shines along its forward axis, so pitch -90 points it straight down.

intensity.description: Brightness: the light component's Intensity, set as given, in the component's own units (a directional light is in lux). Left out, the engine default stays. properties.intensity wins over it.

color.description: Light color {r, g, b, a}. Linear 0-1 channels, stored by the engine as the 8-bit sRGB color: {r: 1, g: 0.7, b: 0.42} reads back as (255, 218, 173). A missing channel reads 0 (alpha 1). properties.color wins over it.

properties.description: Light component settings, applied to the lights they fit; the reply lists what went in as details.applied, what did not as details.refused ("name: why") and any value replaced for being out of range as details.adjusted. Keys: intensity (0 or more; a negative reads 0), color (as above), castShadows (true or false), useAsAtmosphereSunLight (true or false; a directional light given properties is the atmosphere sun unless this says false), attenuationRadius (above 0, point and spot lights; an invalid value reads 1000), innerConeAngle and outerConeAngle (0 to 180 degrees, spot lights; clamped), sourceWidth and sourceHeight (above 0, rect lights; an invalid value reads 100). A sky light takes only the top-level intensity and color. Any other key, or one that does not fit the light, is refused by name.

topics: two copies in the same place
discovery.summary: Sweep every actor in the level and report the ones that interpenetrate another actor, sit sunk below the surface under them, float above it, lean off vertical, or have a face in the same plane as another surface (z-fighting flicker), and the unfinished content they show (a slot on the engine's default grid material, a text still reading "Text", a copy pasted onto the original); or, with blueprintPath, the mesh parts of one actor Blueprint that are buried in each other or sunk below its capsule.
whenToUse: A level was assembled programmatically and needs checking before anyone looks at it.
Actors appear to clip through each other, stand in the ground, or lie on their side.
A placement pass should be verified without flying the viewport around to eyeball it.
Judging what was already in the level, or what an import, a merge or a script outside the MCP left: a call's own warnings cover only the actors that call changed.
A level must be checked for slop before anyone plays it: default_material, placeholder_text and duplicate name what was left unfinished.

Surfaces flicker, or another material shows through in ragged patches (z-fighting): the coplanar face pairs responsible are listed under coplanarFaces, with the direction to push each one; control_actor fix_coplanar fixes them all in one call.

A character, vehicle or prop is assembled from mesh components in a Blueprint (a driver in a seat, legs on a body): blueprintPath checks every part against every other on their real triangles and against the capsule bottom, so a leg sunk into the seat or a foot through the floor is named with its depth.
whenNotToUse: Checking only what one call just did: every call that spawns, moves, duplicates or re-meshes actors already runs these checks on the actors it changed (spawn and set_transform answer placementWarning; every other call lists what it finds in its reply's warnings).

A finding is a deliberate composition (a keep bedding its towers into its platform, an island meant to hang in the air, a signpost leaning by design): tag that actor mcp.placement.ok with control_actor.add_tag and it drops out of the sweep entirely -- as tilt subject, and as both subject and target for overlap -- rather than being re-reported every time. Coplanar faces are still reported for tagged actors, because they flicker whatever the intent.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

nameFilter.description: Only examine actors whose label or object name contains this text (an actor that shares its label with another is reported by object name, e.g. StaticMeshActor_75). Omit to sweep the whole level.

limit.description: Maximum problem entries to return (1-200, default 25). Entries come worst-first, so a small limit still shows the placements that matter; flagged is always the true total.

minSeverity.description: Drop findings whose severity (worst penetration, ground error, tilt displacement, or the side of the largest z-fighting patch, in world units) is below this. Use it to skip cosmetic grazes on a large level.

kinds.description: Report only these problem kinds, e.g. ["coplanar"] to list z-fighting alone in a platformer full of platforms that float on purpose. default_material: a visible mesh slot drawing the engine's default grid (no material, or one made from it). placeholder_text: a text render still reading the engine default "Text" (give it its label, or an empty text when a script writes it in play). duplicate: an actor that is a copy of another in the same place with the same meshes, drawn twice. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for these, as for coplanar, when its contentIssues hold them. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for coplanar when it has coplanarFaces. An actor whose bounds touch or overlap another actor's vertical face (a window band on a hall, an awning on a facade) is mounted, never floating or unsupported. Two faces pointing down with something solid right below them (pieces lying on a floor) are not reported as coplanar: no camera sees them. Omit for every kind.

maxTilt.description: Degrees off vertical an actor may lean before it is reported as tilted (1-90, default 30). Lean is the angle between the up vector of the actor and world up, so yaw never counts and a fully inverted actor reads 180. Raise it for a level whose props are deliberately strewn about; lower it to catch subtler leans.

blueprintPath.description: Audit the mesh parts of this actor Blueprint instead of the level: a preview instance (the level is untouched) has every visible static mesh part measured against every other and against its ground (a Character's capsule bottom). problems[] then lists componentName, kind (buried: inside otherComponent; sunk: below the ground), depth and severity in cm, insideShare and the issue; minSeverity is the tolerance (default 0.5 cm), and kinds, nameFilter and maxTilt are refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT). A part tagged mcp.placement.ok in its ComponentTags is a deliberate embed (an eyeball in its socket) and is left out; mcp.placement.ok:<component> accepts the embed in that one part only and keeps every other check. Blueprint component edits report the same for the parts they touch, as partWarnings.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

flagged.description: Actors with a placement problem (part findings, with blueprintPath), before the limit.

byKind.description: Count of flagged actors per problem kind: sunk, floating, overlapping, unsupported, tilted, coplanar, default_material, placeholder_text, duplicate.

problems.description: Findings worst-first: actorName, kind, severity in world units, the issue in words, suggestedZ when a resting height can be computed, overlappingActors when it intersects others (up to 8, each with actorName, actorClass and penetrationDepth), and coplanarFaces when faces z-fight: one entry per pair with direction (the axis both faces point along, e.g. -Y), component, otherActor, otherComponent, gap and overlapU x overlapV. Fix a pair by moving the face about 2 units along direction (this piece shows) or against it (the other shows, right for a piece sunk into it, such as a ramp in the floor), by moving or scaling the actor. contentIssues lists the unfinished content it shows: kind (default_material, placeholder_text, duplicate), component and the issue; their severity is the size in cm of what shows them.

truncationNote.description: Present when the limit cut the list short; says how to reach the rest.

blueprintPath.description: With blueprintPath: the Blueprint whose parts were measured.

groundZ.description: With blueprintPath: the ground the parts were measured against (the capsule bottom of the preview instance); absent when the root is not a capsule.

discovery.summary: Fix z-fighting in one call: every actor with a face in the same plane as another surface moves a unit, so one surface is clearly in front, repeating until nothing is left to move. A piece lying wholly inside the other face (a door on a wall) comes forward; one only partly inside (a ramp sunk into the floor) goes back so the other shows. Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once.
whenToUse: audit_placement reported coplanar faces, or surfaces flicker between two materials.
A level was built from boxes placed flush against each other and should be cleaned up before anyone looks at it.
whenNotToUse: Only some actors may move: limit the call with nameFilter. A tag of mcp.placement.ok does not exempt an actor, because no two faces flicker on purpose.

nameFilter.description: Only fix pairs where the label or object name of either actor contains this text. Omit for the whole level.

moved.description: One entry per actor: actorName, offset {x, y, z} it moved by, resized when both of its faces on one axis moved (for example "grew 2.0 units along X"), and pairs, each face with the other actor and whether it was brought forward or pulled back.

Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once.
