topics: what the user is looking at
discovery.summary: Read editor state: selected actors, viewport, world settings (with whether the game is playing or paused), project settings, editor settings, or focus: what the user is working on (open editors, a Blueprint's selected nodes, recent errors).
whenToUse: editorState=selected_actors: The current editor selection must be inspected.
editorState=viewport: Viewport and camera state must be inspected.
editorState=world_settings: The current level's world settings must be inspected.
editorState=project_settings: Project settings must be inspected.
editorState=editor_settings: Editor settings must be inspected.
editorState=focus: A request names something the user has in front of them ("this node", "the Blueprint I have open", "fix that error") and it must be resolved to an asset, a graph or a node.
editorState=focus: Work should start from the editor state the user left (the selected nodes, the open editors).
whenNotToUse: editorState=selected_actors: All actors are needed; use list_objects.
editorState=viewport: A screenshot is needed; use control_editor.
editorState=focus: Only the selected actors are needed (use editorState selected_actors).
editorState=focus: The whole log is wanted (use the log read).

editorState.description: Which get editor state variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

shadersCompiling.description: Every get_editor_state variant: shader compile jobs still outstanding. Above 0 the viewport, and a screenshot of it, shows the engine default material (black foliage, grey ground) for what they cover; a warning says so.

packageName.description: Package name of the world asset.

hasBegunPlay.description: Whether the world has begun play.

isPlayInEditor.description: Whether this world is a PIE world.

isPaused.description: Whether game time stands still: control_editor pause, or the game paused itself (a title screen or a pause menu). Nothing moves or simulates until control_editor resume (unpauseGame for a pause the game holds).

killZ.description: Z height below which actors are killed.

enableWorldBoundsChecks.description: Whether world bounds checks are enabled.

defaultGameMode.description: Default GameMode class path set on WorldSettings.

startInVR.description: Whether the project starts in VR.

useDistanceScaledCamera.description: Whether distance-scaled camera speed is used.

isPIEActive.description: Whether a PIE session is active.

gRunningCommandlet.description: 1 when running as a commandlet, else 0.

openEditors.description: Each asset open in an editor, most recently used first: asset (its path) and editor (BlueprintEditor, MaterialEditor, ...).

blueprints.description: Each open Blueprint editor, most recently used first: blueprint (path), graph (the graph whose editor last had keyboard focus; absent until one has) and selectedNodes [{title, nodeId, class}]; nodeId is what the graph tools take.

selectedActors.description: Labels of the actors selected in the level (at most 50).

recentWarnings.description: The distinct warnings and errors logged in the last minute ("3x Category: message"), at most 10, a Blueprint runtime error first with the node that raised it.

scriptErrors.description: The Blueprint runtime errors of the last play session, as runtime_report lists them (message, node, nodeId, graph, blueprintPath, count).

Several properties of one target must be read in one call (propertyNames).
The same properties must be read from several objects in one call (objectPaths), e.g. the state of every moving platform.
whenNotToUse: All properties are needed; use inspect_object or inspect_cdo.

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint asset /Game path (for CDO/component inspection without spawning).

On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

value.description: The value read; its type follows the property.

targets.description: With objectPaths: each target as {objectPath as given, propertyName and value, or properties and missingProperties with propertyNames, error when it could not be read}.

properties.description: With propertyNames: each property that resolved, as {propertyName (its own spelling), value}, plus propertyPath (the path as asked) when that differs, so two .Text reads stay apart.

missingProperties.description: With propertyNames: each name that did not resolve, as "Name: reason".

discovery.summary: Read performance (FPS, frame rate and time, thread and GPU ms), memory usage (used, available, peak), scene statistics (actors by category, components, hidden actors), or frame cost: the thread that bounds the frame and what in view weighs on it (movable shadow-casting lights, heavy meshes, translucency, ticking actors).
whenToUse: statsKind=performance: Performance metrics must be inspected.
statsKind=memory: Memory usage must be inspected.
statsKind=scene: Scene-level statistics must be inspected.
statsKind=frame: The game or the editor runs slowly and the cause must be found.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

statsKind.description: Which get stats variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

threadTimersAreProcessGlobal.description: Thread timers are process-global, not per-world.

busiestThreadMs.description: Slowest of the game, render, RHI and GPU thread times, in milliseconds.

threadTimeDerivedFps.description: FPS implied by busiestThreadMs; unaffected by editor idle throttling.

frameDeltaMayBeEditorThrottled.description: True outside PIE, where an idle editor throttles the frame delta and makes fps read far lower than actual.

estimatedFps.description: Estimated frames per second from delta time.

fps.description: Reported frames per second (same as estimatedFps).

gameThreadMs.description: Game thread time in milliseconds; while Play In Editor runs it also holds the editor's own UI and viewports, so worldTickMs is the game's share.

worldTickMs.description: The measured world's own tick in milliseconds (actors, components and physics, from the start of its tick to the end of its tick groups), averaged over about 30 frames: the game's share of gameThreadMs. Absent until the world has ticked.

actorCount.description: Actor count of the measured world.

windowMinimized.description: True when the editor window is minimized: no frame is drawn, so renderThreadMs, rhiThreadMs and gpuMs are left from the last drawn frame and the frame delta is the background throttle. Restore it (control_editor configure_editor setting window) before measuring. Absent otherwise.

videoMemoryOverBudgetMB.description: How far video memory is over budget, the figure the viewport's "Video memory has been exhausted" line prints: another application holding the GPU (a game) or a scene that does not fit, which slows every frame. Absent when it fits.

isBenchmarking.description: Whether the engine is in benchmarking mode.

useFixedTimeStep.description: Whether a fixed time step is active.

peakUsedPhysicalBytes.description: Peak used physical memory in bytes.

peakUsedVirtualBytes.description: Peak used virtual memory in bytes.

peakUsedPhysicalMB.description: Peak used physical memory in megabytes.

peakUsedVirtualMB.description: Peak used virtual memory in megabytes.

totalWorldActors.description: Raw world actor count including editor-internal actors (explains the gap vs actorCount).

busiestThread.description: The slowest thread: game, render, rhi or gpu. It sets the frame time unless the frame waits (busiestThreadMs under half of frameTimeMs: an unfocused editor, vsync or a frame rate cap), which the message then says.

primitivesInView.description: Primitive components drawn in the last half second, a stand-in for the draw calls the render thread issues.

meshesInView.description: Static mesh components drawn in the last half second.

naniteMeshesInView.description: Of meshesInView, those whose mesh has Nanite data (drawn as Nanite while Nanite is on).

heaviestMeshes.description: Up to 5 static meshes drawn without Nanite in the last half second, most triangles first: mesh, triangles (LOD 0 times instances, summed over every component drawing it), components, instances and actor (one that shows it).

movableShadowLightCount.description: Visible movable lights that cast shadows; each renders its shadows again every frame.

movableShadowLights.description: Up to 5 of them, widest reach first: actor, light (Directional, Point, Spot or Rect) and radius (0 for a directional light, which reaches everything).

translucentPrimitiveCount.description: Primitive components drawn in the last half second with at least one translucent material.

translucentPrimitives.description: Up to 5 of them, most translucent sections first: actor, component and translucentSections.

tickingActorCount.description: Actors that tick, by their own tick or a component's.

tickingActorsByClass.description: Up to 5 classes with the most ticking actors: class, count and ticks, what ticks on them: "Event Tick" (the Blueprint graph implements Tick), "actor Tick" (its C++ class ticks) or a component class (a movement, rotating or timeline component ticks without any graph).

examples.title: Read performance (FPS, frame rate and time, thread and GPU ms), memory usage (used, available, peak), scene statistics (actors by category, components, hidden actors), or frame cost: the thread that bounds the frame and what in view weighs on it (movable shadow-casting lights, heavy meshes, translucency, ticking actors).

discovery.summary: Read reflection data, chosen by kind. class (className or classPath) gives the class path, parent and ancestors, module, flags (abstract, blueprintable, actor, component and more), every property it declares or inherits (name, type, category, where declared, editable, Blueprint-visible; at most 200 listed, propertyCount the total), the default value of each on its class default object, and its function count. cdo reads a Blueprint class default object without spawning anything (blueprintPath): its default values (propertyNames picks some) and its default components (componentName or componentNames narrows them). struct reads the members of a user struct (structPath): name, type, default and tooltip.
whenToUse: kind=class: A class's hierarchy and defaults must be read.
kind=struct: A Blueprint Struct's member layout must be read.
kind=cdo: A Blueprint's default properties and components must be read.
whenNotToUse: kind=class: A specific instance is in scope; use inspect_object.
kind=struct: Struct values must be read or written; use manage_asset struct actions.
kind=cdo: A spawned world actor is in scope; use inspect_object.

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint asset /Game path (for CDO/component inspection without spawning).

componentName.description: Component name on the actor.

componentNames.description: Return only these components in components, by name (case-insensitive); a name that matches none is listed under missingComponents.

kind.description: Which inspect class variant to run; omit for 'class'.

className.description: Class name or /Script/ class path to inspect.

classPath.description: Full /Script path of the resolved class.

parentClass.description: Immediate super-class name ("None" when the class has no super).

module.description: Module that declares a C++ class (empty for a Blueprint class).

generatedBy.description: Blueprint asset that generated the class, when it is Blueprint-generated.

ancestors.description: Super-classes from the parent up to Object.

properties.description: kind=class: every property the class declares or inherits (name, type, category, declaredIn, editable, blueprintVisible, deprecated). kind=cdo: the requested property values by name.

propertyCount.description: Properties the class has, including any past the 200 listed.

propertiesTruncated.description: True when the class has more than the 200 properties listed.

defaultProperties.description: Default value of each property on the class default object, as text.

defaultObjectPath.description: Path of the class default object.

functionCount.description: Functions the class declares or inherits.

result.description: Struct layout: structName, structPath, parentStruct(Path), isRowStruct, isUserDefined, members[] (name/type/default/tooltip/guid/metadata/innerStruct), memberCount.

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint asset /Game path (for CDO/component inspection without spawning).

componentCount.description: Number of default components on the CDO.

cdoProperties.description: Default property values on the Class Default Object.

discovery.summary: Deep-inspect an actor or asset, or read a typed detail view of an actor, level, material, texture or mesh (its size, bounds, pivot, LODs and material slots, each with the triangles and bounds of the geometry it covers).
whenToUse: objectKind=object: An object's properties and structure must be read.
objectKind=actor: A world actor's details must be read using the get_actor_details verb.
objectKind=level: The current level's world settings summary must be read.
objectKind=material: A material asset's details must be read.
objectKind=mesh: A mesh asset's details must be read.
objectKind=mesh: It is not known which material slot holds which part of a mesh (legs, hull, claws): each slot lists the triangles and mesh-space bounds of its LOD0 geometry.
objectKind=texture: A texture asset's details must be read.
whenNotToUse: objectKind=object: A Blueprint CDO without a spawned actor is needed; use inspect_cdo.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

objectPath.description: Object path of the world actor or asset (e.g. /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo_PersistentLevel).

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

componentName.description: Component name on the actor.

objectKind.description: Which inspect object variant to run; omit for 'object'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

objectPath.description: Full object path of the inspected object.

class.description: Class name of the inspected object.

classPath.description: Full /Script class path of the inspected object.

isActor.description: True when the object is a world actor rather than an asset.

isStaticMesh.description: True when the object is a StaticMesh asset.

isSceneComponent.description: True when the object is a scene component.

isSelected.description: True when the actor is selected in the editor.

isHidden.description: True when the actor is hidden in the editor viewport.

isVisible.description: True when the object is visible.

isActive.description: True when the component is active.

staticMesh.description: Static mesh asset path assigned to the object, when it has one.

location.description: World location as {x, y, z}.

rotation.description: World rotation as {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees.

transform.description: Combined transform: location, rotation and scale.

components.description: Attached components with their names, classes and transforms.

materialSlots.description: Mesh assets: every material slot as {slotIndex, slotName, material (asset path, empty for none), triangles and sections (what LOD0 draws with the slot), bounds (where that geometry is, in mesh space: origin is its center, extent its half size, with min, max, size and radius)}. bounds is absent for a slot LOD0 draws nothing with, and for every slot when slotBoundsAvailable is false. A Nanite mesh reports its fallback mesh. A skeletal mesh is read in its reference pose.

materialSlotCount.description: Mesh assets: how many material slots the mesh has.

slotBoundsAvailable.description: Mesh assets: false when the render data keeps no CPU copy of its vertices, so each slot has its triangle count but no bounds.

discovery.summary: Read placed actors, chosen by lookup. list pages through the actors of the level (the running game during Play): filter narrows by name, limit (default 100) and offset page through them, with totalCount and isPieWorld; control_actor list adds class, tag, folder, near and property filters. by_tag lists the actors carrying tag (name, path, class), stopping at limit (default 200) with the total. metadata gives one actor name, label, path, class, tags and location. bounding_box gives its world bounds as origin and extent (half the size on each axis), every component counted. export writes it as T3D text (exportedText), and also to outputPath inside the project when given.
whenToUse: lookup=list: All actors in the current level must be enumerated.
lookup=by_tag: All actors with a given tag must be enumerated.
lookup=metadata: An actor's metadata must be inspected.
lookup=bounding_box: An actor's bounds must be read.
lookup=export: An actor must be serialized to text or to an external file.
whenNotToUse: lookup=by_tag: Actors must be found by class; use find_by_class.
lookup=metadata: Metadata must be written; use manage_asset or control_actor set_metadata.
lookup=bounding_box: The actor does not have a visible mesh.
lookup=export: The actor should be duplicated in-scene; use control_actor duplicate.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

offset.description: Matching objects to skip before the first one returned, for paging (default 0); hasMore says whether more follow.

objectPath.description: Object path of the world actor or asset (e.g. /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo_PersistentLevel).

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

format.description: Exporter format by file extension, default T3D (the text form of the object); fails with EXPORT_FAILED when no exporter for that format handles the object.

outputPath.description: File to also write the export to, inside the project (relative to it, or absolute under it), e.g. Saved/Exports/Actor.t3d. A path outside the project is refused with INVALID_PATH.

lookup.description: Which query object variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

totalCount.description: Total actor count in the world.

isPieWorld.description: Whether the world is a PIE world.

examples.title: Read placed actors, chosen by lookup. list pages through the actors of the level (the running game during Play): filter narrows by name, limit (default 100) and offset page through them, with totalCount and isPieWorld; control_actor list adds class, tag, folder, near and property filters. by_tag lists the actors carrying tag (name, path, class), stopping at limit (default 200) with the total. metadata gives one actor name, label, path, class, tags and location. bounding_box gives its world bounds as origin and extent (half the size on each axis), every component counted. export writes it as T3D text (exportedText), and also to outputPath inside the project when given.

discovery.summary: Cast rays at a static mesh asset in its own local space and read where each one meets the surface: the point, the surface normal and the material slot. Places a part, a print or a decal on a curved surface without a placed actor or collision.
whenToUse: A part, decal or print must sit exactly on a mesh surface (a chest, a hull, a rock) and the surface position at a given height or side is unknown; the decalRotation and location of a hit place a DecalComponent there directly.
A surface profile must be sampled: one ray per row or column across the area.
whenNotToUse: Only the overall size or pivot of the mesh is needed (use get_mesh_details).
Parts of a Blueprint must be checked for sinking into each other (use control_actor.audit_placement).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset path, e.g. /Game/Meshes/SM_Rock. Rays meet its source triangles, so a Nanite mesh answers at full detail.

origin.description: Ray start {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space, in cm; start outside the mesh to find its outer surface.

direction.description: Ray direction {x, y, z}; any length, it is normalized.

start.description: Line start {x, y, z} in local space, with end in place of origin and direction (the form raycast_world takes).

end.description: Line end {x, y, z} in local space; nothing past it is reported.

rays.description: Rays in the mesh's local space, each {origin, direction} or {start, end}; each answers in hits at the same index.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

meshPath.description: The mesh the rays were cast at.

hitCount.description: How many rays met the surface.

hit.description: Whether this ray met the surface.

location.description: Nearest point where the ray meets the surface, {x, y, z} in local space.

normal.description: Surface normal there, turned to face back along the ray (from outside, the outward normal).

distance.description: Distance from the ray origin, in cm.

materialSlot.description: Name of the material slot whose triangle was hit.

decalRotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} for a DecalComponent placed at location in the same space, so its texture prints upright and readable on this surface: the decal projects into the surface along its X axis, and its DecalSize is (projection depth, half the print height, half the print width).

hits.description: One entry per ray, in order.

examples.title: Cast rays at a static mesh asset in its own local space and read where each one meets the surface: the point, the surface normal and the material slot. Places a part, a print or a decal on a curved surface without a placed actor or collision.

discovery.summary: Trace lines through the level against collision and read what each one hits first: the point, the surface normal, the distance, the actor and the component. Finds the ground under a point, checks a line of sight, and proves a wall, floor or volume really blocks. Traces the running game while Play In Editor runs.
whenToUse: The ground height under a point, or what a jump or a drop would land on, must be known.
A line of sight between two points (a camera, an enemy, the player) must be checked.
A placed wall, floor, platform or blocking volume must be proven to block: a mesh or volume with no collision is traced straight through.
whenNotToUse: The surface of a mesh asset must be found without placing it (use raycast_mesh).
Only an actor's overall size is needed (use query_object lookup bounding_box).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

start.description: Line start {x, y, z} in world space, in cm.

end.description: Line end {x, y, z} in world space; nothing past it is reported.

rays.description: Lines in world space; each answers in hits at the same index.

channel.description: Collision channel traced: Visibility (default), Camera, WorldStatic, WorldDynamic, Pawn, PhysicsBody, Vehicle, Destructible, or a project trace channel by its name. What blocks depends on each component's response to that channel: most meshes block Visibility, a character capsule blocks Pawn.

traceComplex.description: Trace the render triangles of meshes that allow it instead of their simple collision (default false: the shapes the game's movement collides with).

ignoreActors.description: Actors (label, name or path) the lines pass through, such as the player pawn a line starts inside; an unknown name is refused.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

hit.description: Whether this line hit something that blocks the channel.

location.description: Where the line first hits, {x, y, z} in world space.

actorName.description: Label of the actor hit.

componentName.description: Component whose collision the line hit.

startedInside.description: True when start was already inside the collision it reports: the line begins in a wall, or in a pawn left out of ignoreActors.

hits.description: One entry per line, in order.

examples.title: Trace lines through the level against collision and read what each one hits first: the point, the surface normal, the distance, the actor and the component. Finds the ground under a point, checks a line of sight, and proves a wall, floor or volume really blocks. Traces the running game while Play In Editor runs.

discovery.summary: Report the live state of a running PIE game: the player controller, pawn, view target and camera, plus up to 25 matching actors with class, transform, tags, components and the live values of the variables or properties named in propertyNames; actors are reported only while PIE runs.
whenToUse: Runtime state of actors/components/properties must be inspected during PIE.
PIE-only runtime state must be inspected.
A Blueprint failed while the game ran (Accessed None): scriptErrors names the node, graph and Blueprint.
whenNotToUse: The editor is not in PIE; the report then holds only the last play session's scriptErrors.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

componentName.description: Component name on the actor.

propertyName.description: Property to read or write: a name, or a dotted path through structs and object references at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled). On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or dotted path); used when propertyName is absent. Give this or propertyName.

propertyNames.description: Properties to read, each a name or dotted path: read on each matching actor itself (its Blueprint variables, such as bIsOpen, land in the actor properties) and on each reported component (in that component properties). A name found on none of the listed actors is listed once in propertiesNotFound.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

worldName.description: Name of the world the report describes.

worldType.description: World type, e.g. PIE or Editor.

isPIE.description: Whether a PIE session is active.

actors.description: Matching runtime actors, at most 25, each with its components and, under propertyNames, the values found: properties on the actor itself and properties on each component. Only when filter, actorName, componentNames or propertyNames selects them.

propertiesNotFound.description: The propertyNames found on none of the listed actors or their components (a misspelt or missing variable).

count.description: Number of actors returned after filtering; absent with actors.

totalActorCount.description: Total actors in the inspected world.

playerController.description: Object path of the active PlayerController (inspect_object it for details).

pawn.description: Object path of the possessed pawn; inspect it to find where the player actually is.

viewTarget.description: Object path of the current view target.

playerCameraManager.description: PlayerCameraManager described as a runtime actor, plus cameraLocation and cameraRotation as {x,y,z} / {pitch,yaw,roll} objects.

scriptErrors.description: Blueprint runtime errors (an Accessed None, an infinite loop) of this play session, or of the last one until the next play starts: message, blueprintPath, graph, node and nodeId (as edit_graph takes them; function when no node resolves), objects that raised it, count, firstGameSeconds, and values (the object's Blueprint variables at the first hit). Absent when none fired.

examples.title: Report the live state of a running PIE game: the player controller, pawn, view target and camera, plus up to 25 matching actors with class, transform, tags, components and the live values of the variables or properties named in propertyNames; actors are reported only while PIE runs.

discovery.summary: Write one or more properties of a component on a placed actor, as control_actor edit_component set_property does: propertyName or a dotted propertyPath with value, or properties for several. One undo step, the level left unsaved; while Play runs it changes the playing copy. The actor is named by actorName, name or objectPath.
whenToUse: A single component property value must be written.
whenNotToUse: The component does not own the property; use get_components to enumerate.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

objectPath.description: Object path of the world actor or asset (e.g. /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo_PersistentLevel).

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

componentName.description: Component name on the actor.

propertyName.description: Property to read or write: a name, or a dotted path through structs and object references at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled). On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or dotted path); used when propertyName is absent. Give this or propertyName.

value.description: Property value to set, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"X": 0, "Y": 0, "Z": 100} for a vector, an object or asset path, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}), which replaces the whole map.

properties.description: Several component properties at once, name or dotted path to value, in place of propertyName and value.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Write one or more properties of a component on a placed actor, as control_actor edit_component set_property does: propertyName or a dotted propertyPath with value, or properties for several. One undo step, the level left unsaved; while Play runs it changes the playing copy. The actor is named by actorName, name or objectPath.

discovery.summary: Write a property value on a world actor, asset, or Blueprint CDO; several at once (properties), or the same on several objects (objectPaths).
whenToUse: A single property value must be written.
Several properties of one target must be written in one call (properties).
The same property must be written on several objects in one call (objectPaths), e.g. one volume on every ambient sound.

A placed actor's component property must be written ("StaticMeshComponent0.StaticMesh", "Mesh.BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled"): a StaticMesh, collision, SimulatePhysics or Mobility key goes through the component's own setter, as control_actor edit_component writes it.
whenNotToUse: The property is read-only or the target is a packed asset.

A value the object works out from another of its settings: the object puts the write back and the call fails with PROPERTY_SET_FAILED naming both values, so change that setting instead. A value the object only adjusts (a clamp) is written, and the message names what it became.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

objectPath.description: Object path of the world actor or asset (e.g. /Game/Maps/Demo.Demo_PersistentLevel); while PIE runs, GameInstance, GameMode, GameState, PlayerController, PlayerPawn, PlayerState or HUD names that object of the running game, and a live widget goes by the name control_editor simulate_input widget_list reports (WBP_HUD_C_0 or WBP_HUD; its widgets are properties: CoinBox.RenderTransform).

actorName.description: World actor name to inspect.

name.description: Actor name identifier (alias of actorName).

blueprintPath.description: Blueprint asset /Game path (for CDO/component inspection without spawning).

propertyName.description: Property to read or write: a name, or a dotted path through structs and object references at any depth (BodyInstance.CollisionEnabled). On an actor the path may start with a component's name, including one added in the level (MyAudio.VolumeMultiplier). A bare name that is not on the object itself resolves to the one struct member carrying it. Give this or propertyPath.

propertyPath.description: Same as propertyName (a name or dotted path); used when propertyName is absent. Give this or propertyName.

value.description: Property value to set, in the form get_property reads back: a number, string or bool, {"X": 0, "Y": 0, "Z": 100} for a vector, an object or asset path, an array for an Array or Set, and a JSON object of key: value for a Map ({"Apple": 3}), which replaces the whole map.

markDirty.description: Default true: mark the package dirty and save an asset package. false leaves the package untouched and unsaved, so the change lives in memory only.

properties.description: Several writes on the same target in place of propertyName and value: {name or dotted path: value}, e.g. {"BoxExtent": {"X": 20, "Y": 90, "Z": 100}, "CollisionProfileName": "OverlapAllDynamic"}. Each is written as a single call would be and reported under properties; the call fails naming any that did not apply. watch applies to single writes only.

objectPaths.description: The same write on several targets in one call, in place of objectPath: each entry is a target as objectPath takes it (an actor, "Actor.Component", an asset, a class default), written as a single call would be, with properties too. Answered under targets; the call fails naming each target that did not take the write, and the others keep it.

watch.description: Sample a property right after the write, in the same call, to see what the write sets off before it ends: a HUD pop or fade runs on real time, even with PIE paused, and is over before a later call can read it. The reply lists each value the property took with its time t in seconds (Lives on GameInstance with watch {objectPath: "WBP_HUD", propertyName: "LivesBox.RenderTransform"}).

propertyName.description: The property to sample; a dotted path reaches through widgets and structs (LivesBox.RenderTransform). Omitted, the property the call writes.

objectPath.description: The object to sample, as objectPath takes it (GameInstance, a live widget such as WBP_HUD); omitted, the object written.

durationSeconds.description: Real seconds to sample (default 0.5, at most 20).

intervalSeconds.description: Seconds between samples (default 0: every frame); a sample is kept only when the value changed.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

watch.description: With watch: objectPath, propertyName, samples ({t, value}, kept when the value changed), sampleCount, changed (it took more than one value) and frames.

properties.description: With properties: each write as {propertyName, applied, value read back}.

targets.description: With objectPaths: each target as {objectPath as given, applied, the value read back (properties with properties), actorPath, saved, saveSkippedReason}.

applied.description: With properties: how many writes applied; with objectPaths: how many targets.

saved.description: Whether the target's package was written to disk after the write; with properties, the last write's save, which holds every write of the call. False with saveSkippedReason when nothing was saved.

saveSkippedReason.description: Why nothing was saved: markDirty was false, a running-game or transient object (the change lasts until PIE stops), level content (saved with its level), engine content, or a save that failed (the change is only in memory).

instancesUpdated.description: A write to a class default or component template: how many placed copies, and derived Blueprints' defaults with their own copies, still held the old default and took the new one, as the details panel does; one that overrides the value keeps it. Absent for any other target.

blueprintCompiled.description: True when the target was a Blueprint CDO and the Blueprint was recompiled, so the value now applies to newly spawned instances. The reply (value, actorPath, actorClass) is read back from the recompiled class default object and the Blueprint package is saved; a variable the Blueprint declares keeps the value as its default, and the call fails with PROPERTY_SET_FAILED, never success, when the compile did not keep it. A Default__ objectPath resolves to the Blueprint's current default object; a copy a compile left behind (a REINST_ class, or a Blueprint object in /Engine/Transient with no game running) fails with STALE_TARGET. False for plain world actors and assets, where no compile is involved.

materialRebuilt.description: True when the target lives inside a material or material function (a material expression such as a TextureObjectParameter, as <material>.<material>:<nodeName>) and that material was rebuilt, so its parameter lists, which every material instance reads, show the write at once (a new ParameterName, a new default Texture). Absent for any other target.

examples.title: Write a property value on a world actor, asset, or Blueprint CDO; several at once (properties), or the same on several objects (objectPaths).

discovery.summary: Configure navigation: nav mesh settings, agent properties, area cost or class, nav links, smart links, or rebuild the nav mesh. A level with no nav mesh yet gets one from a NavMeshBoundsVolume (manage_level_structure create_volume).
whenToUse: setting=mesh_settings: The loaded level RecastNavMesh needs generation tuning.
setting=agent_properties: The navigation agent dimensions must change.
setting=area_cost: A navigation area class needs a different traversal cost.
setting=area_class: A placed actor should carve a specific navigation area.
setting=nav_link: A placed nav link actor needs endpoint or snap tuning.
setting=link_type: A link must switch between the simple and smart form.
setting=smart_link_behavior: A smart link needs area-class switching or an obstacle.
setting=rebuild: NavMesh geometry is stale after level or settings edits.
whenNotToUse: setting=nav_link: Use create_nav_link_proxy to place the link first.

tileSizeUU.description: NavMesh tile size in Unreal units (default: 1000).

agentStepHeight.description: Maximum step height the agent can climb (default: 35).

areaCost.description: Pathfinding cost multiplier for the area (1.0 = normal).

fixedAreaEnteringCost.description: Flat cost added once when a path enters the area; left unchanged when omitted.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

componentName.description: NavModifierComponent to retarget when the actor carries several; defaults to the first one.

startPoint.description: Start of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

endPoint.description: End of the link, relative to the link actor (its location and rotation).

direction.description: Which way agents may cross: BothWays (default), LeftToRight (start to end) or RightToLeft.

snapRadius.description: How far from each end of the point link the navmesh is looked for (default 30).

linkType.description: simple (the point link of the proxy) or smart (its smart link, which can switch on and off).

linkEnabled.description: Switch the smart link on (true) or off.

enabledAreaClass.description: Navigation area class the smart link marks while on, e.g. /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Default.

disabledAreaClass.description: Navigation area class the smart link marks while off, e.g. /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Null (impassable).

broadcastRadius.description: Radius, in units, of the agents told when the smart link switches; the engine default 0 tells none.

broadcastInterval.description: Seconds between repeats of that notice; 0 sends it once.

bCreateBoxObstacle.description: true sets the box obstacle of the smart link, which marks the navmesh with obstacleAreaClass.

obstacleAreaClass.description: Area the box obstacle marks (default /Script/NavigationSystem.NavArea_Null, impassable).

obstacleExtent.description: Half size of the box obstacle (default 100 on each axis).

obstacleOffset.description: Offset of the box obstacle from the link actor.

setting.description: Which configure navigation variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level.

discovery.summary: Edit a Behavior Tree graph: add composite, task, decorator, service or generic nodes and subnodes, connect or break connections, configure or remove nodes.
whenToUse: edit=add_composite: A Behavior Tree needs a Selector, Sequence or Simple Parallel branch.

edit=add_task: A Behavior Tree branch needs a leaf task. An enemy that chases the player is a Sequence with a MoveTo task whose Blackboard key (an Object key such as TargetActor) holds the player, run on its AI controller with run_behavior_tree.
edit=add_decorator: A Behavior Tree branch needs a conditional gate.
edit=add_service: A Behavior Tree branch needs recurring background work.
edit=add_node: A Behavior Tree graph needs a node placed at explicit coordinates.
edit=add_subnode: A graph node needs a decorator or service attached by class.
edit=connect: A parent graph node must be linked to a child.
edit=break_connections: A graph node must be detached from its links.
edit=configure_node: An existing Behavior Tree node needs property edits.
edit=set_node_properties: A graph node needs property or comment edits.
edit=remove_node: A graph node must be deleted.

nodeName.description: Name for the created composite node.

nodeId.description: ID of the node.

discovery.summary: Edit a Blackboard asset (blackboardPath), chosen by edit, each saved: add_key adds keyName of keyType (an Object key a MoveTo target uses wants baseObjectClass /Script/Engine.Actor; an Enum key takes enumType), set_value sets the default a key starts with (UE 5.4+, Enum, Object and Class keys 5.5+), set_key_instance_synced shares one value across every AI. A taken name (NAME_TAKEN), a value of the wrong kind, a key of a parent Blackboard (KEY_IN_PARENT) and engine content are refused.
whenToUse: edit=add_key: A Blackboard needs a new typed entry, such as the actor an AI chases or the place it moves to.
edit=set_value: A Blackboard key needs a different authored default, such as a speed or a starting state.
edit=set_key_instance_synced: A Blackboard key must share its value across instances.

keyName.description: Blackboard key name, matched in any case.

baseObjectClass.description: Class an Object key holds or a Class key names, as a class path or name (e.g. /Script/Engine.Actor); Object and Class keys only. Without it the key is based on Object, which actor-only key filters such as the MoveTo target skip.

enumType.description: Enum an Enum key holds, by path (/Game/Enums/E_State, /Script/Engine.ECollisionChannel); Enum keys only. Without it the key has no enumerators to hold.

isInstanceSynced.description: Share the value of the key across every Blackboard component using this asset, so a value one AI sets reaches them all.

value.description: The default, in the kind the key holds: a boolean, a number, {x, y, z}, {pitch, yaw, roll}, text, an enumerator, or an asset or class path.

edit.description: Which edit blackboard variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

baseClass.description: Class path an Object or Class key is based on.

saved.description: Whether the Blackboard reached disk.

value.description: The default the key now holds, as the engine writes it.

discovery.summary: Make an AIController Blueprint run a Behavior Tree whenever it possesses a pawn (control run, the default: On Possess calls Run Behavior Tree with its BehaviorTree variable), take that out again (stop), only set the variable that holds the tree (assign_tree), or bind a Blackboard to a controller or tree (assign_blackboard). The run logic is engine nodes in the Blueprint, compiled and saved, so it works in a packaged game; a Blueprint that is not an AIController is refused (NOT_AI_CONTROLLER).

discovery.summary: Set the movement limits on the CharacterMovement component of a Character Blueprint (an AI pawn) and save it: maxWalkSpeed, maxAcceleration, brakingDeceleration (walking), rotationRate (yaw, degrees per second), maxFlySpeed, jumpZVelocity and avoidanceWeight, plus useAccelerationForPaths (path following speeds up and slows down like a player instead of moving at full speed at once), orientRotationToMovement (turn to face where it goes) and useRVOAvoidance (steer around other agents). Only what is sent changes, 0 included; a negative number or a call that sets nothing is refused, as is a Blueprint with no CharacterMovement component (COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND). propertiesSet names what changed and currentValues reads the main values back.

whenNotToUse: The pawn has no CharacterMovement component; the call reports the missing component instead.

orientRotationToMovement.description: Rotate the pawn toward its movement direction; left unchanged when omitted.

avoidanceWeight.description: RVO avoidance weight (0 or more); left unchanged when omitted.

maxFlySpeed.description: Maximum flying speed; left unchanged when omitted.

jumpZVelocity.description: Initial upward jump velocity; left unchanged when omitted.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

whenToUse: setting=distance: Use it to configure distance attenuation: inner radius (or a box's size per axis), falloff distance and curve, and air absorption (a low-pass that muffles the sound with distance).

extent.description: A Box shape's half-size on each axis in cm, {x, y, z}, each above 0: a zone the length of a hall without reaching as far sideways. It replaces the size innerRadius gives a box; another shape is refused.

enableReverbSend.description: Whether the sound sends to reverb.

reverbDistanceMin.description: Distance at which the reverb send starts.

reverbDistanceMax.description: Distance at which the reverb wet level reaches its maximum.

discovery.summary: Change a Sound Class or Sound Mix, chosen by setting, each saved: parent sets or clears a class's parent (a loop is refused), properties sets its volume, pitch, low-pass, LFE bleed and center-channel volume, mix_modifier adds or edits the adjuster a mix applies to a class (and the mix fades), mix_eq sets the mix's four EQ bands. A call that sets nothing is refused.
whenToUse: setting=parent: Use it to set the parent of a Sound Class, or clear it with an empty parentClass, keeping both classes' child lists in step (a mix modifier applying to children walks them). A parent that does not load (PARENT_NOT_FOUND), or that is the class itself or one of its children (CYCLIC_PARENT), is refused. Saved unless save is false.

setting=properties: Use it to set the properties of a Sound Class, each only when sent: volume and pitch (multipliers, 1 leaves them as authored), lowPassFilterFrequency (Hz; 20000 leaves the sound unfiltered), lfeBleed and voiceCenterChannelVolume (0-1). The reply lists all five; a call that sends none is refused. Saved unless save is false.

setting=mix_modifier: Use it to add a Sound Class modifier to a Sound Mix, or edit the one the mix already has for that class (replaced true), keeping what is not sent: volumeAdjuster and pitchAdjuster (multipliers; a new modifier starts at 1) and applyToChildren (default true). fadeInTime and fadeOutTime set the fades of the mix itself. Saved unless save is false.

setting=mix_eq: Use it to configure Sound Mix equalization: the four bands through eqSettings (frequencyCenterN, gainN, bandwidthN for N 0-3), or the low, mid, highMid and high fields on top of them. Sending a band switches the EQ on unless applyEQ is false; eqPriority ranks the mix against other active mixes. Values are clamped (gain 0-4, frequency 0-20000 Hz, bandwidth 0-2) and the reply lists every band after clamping; a call that sets nothing is refused.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

parentClass.description: Canonical /Game SoundClass asset path of the new parent; an empty string clears the parent.

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

lowPassFilterFrequency.description: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz.

lfeBleed.description: Share of the sound sent to the LFE channel (0 to 1).

voiceCenterChannelVolume.description: Share of the sound sent to the centre speaker (0 to 1).

volumeAdjuster.description: Volume multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

pitchAdjuster.description: Pitch multiplier applied by the mix modifier.

applyToChildren.description: Whether the modifier also applies to the child sound classes (default true).

applyEQ.description: Whether the mix applies its EQ (default true).

eqPriority.description: EQ priority of the mix; the active mix with the highest priority supplies the EQ.

eqSettings.description: Four-band EQ as {frequencyCenter0..3, gain0..3, bandwidth0..3}; a missing key keeps its value.

lowFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 0 in Hz.

lowGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 0 (0 to 4).

midFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 1 in Hz.

midGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 1 (0 to 4).

highMidFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 2 in Hz.

highMidGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 2 (0 to 4).

highFrequency.description: Centre frequency of EQ band 3 in Hz.

highGain.description: Linear gain of EQ band 3 (0 to 4).

setting.description: Which configure sound class variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Change the mix of the sound being heard (the running game while one plays, else the editor; inGame says which), chosen by control: push and pop put a Sound Mix on the mix stack and take it off, set_base sets the base mix beneath them, and set_class_override and clear_class_override change how a mix adjusts the volume and pitch of one Sound Class, which applies while that mix is pushed or base. Mixes and classes are named by asset path or bare name (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when one does not load). Runtime state only: nothing is saved.
whenToUse: control=push: Use it to push a Sound Mix (mixName: an asset path or a bare asset name) onto the mix stack of the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which). While pushed, its sound class adjustments (volume, pitch, EQ) apply, such as ducking music under dialogue; pop_sound_mix removes it. A name that loads no Sound Mix is ASSET_NOT_FOUND. Runtime state only: nothing is saved.

control=pop: Use it to pop a Sound Mix that push_sound_mix pushed, on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which); its adjustments fade out over the fade-out time of the mix. A mix pushed twice needs two pops, and popping one that is not pushed changes nothing.

control=set_base: Use it to make a Sound Mix the base mix of the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which): the one mix that always applies beneath any pushed ones, replacing the previous base. Runtime state only.

control=set_class_override: Use it to override how a Sound Mix adjusts one Sound Class (soundClassName) and its child classes: volume and pitch multipliers (default 1), reached over fadeTime seconds (default 1); the class joins the mix when the mix lacks it. It acts on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which), only while that mix is pushed or the base mix, and leaves the asset unchanged. A name that loads no mix or class is ASSET_NOT_FOUND.

control=clear_class_override: Use it to remove the override set_sound_mix_class_override put on a Sound Mix for soundClassName, fading back over fadeOutTime seconds (default 1), on the sound being heard: the running game while one plays, else the editor (inGame says which).

control.description: Which control sound mix variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

inGame.description: True when the change went to the running game (Play In Editor), whose sound is the one heard; false for the editor.

examples.title: Change the mix of the sound being heard (the running game while one plays, else the editor; inGame says which), chosen by control: push and pop put a Sound Mix on the mix stack and take it off, set_base sets the base mix beneath them, and set_class_override and clear_class_override change how a mix adjusts the volume and pitch of one Sound Class, which applies while that mix is pushed or base. discovery.summary: Create a MetaSound or edit it: add inputs, outputs and nodes, connect or disconnect nodes, remove nodes, set input and node literals, or run many edits in one batch.
whenToUse: edit=create: Use it to create a MetaSound asset, named by name and path or by its full assetPath, and return its asset path. A MetaSound already at that path is refused (ASSET_EXISTS), never replaced. A one-shot source (the default: On Play in, On Finished out) is never virtualized by the engine, so one left playing on an AudioComponent that starts out of earshot is dropped for good; make a drone, hum or ambience with oneShot false.
edit=add_input: Use it to add an input to a MetaSound graph.
edit=add_output: Use it to add an output to a MetaSound graph.
edit=add_node: Use it to add a node to a MetaSound graph.
edit=connect_nodes: Use it to connect two MetaSound graph pins.

edit=disconnect: Use it to remove a link from a MetaSound graph: the one into targetNodeId.targetInputName, or every link out of sourceNodeId.sourceOutputName; with both ends given, that exact link. Refused when there is no such link.
edit=remove_node: Use it to remove one node, or several with nodeIds, and every link on them from a MetaSound graph; graph inputs and outputs (On Play, Out Mono) are refused. All or nothing.
edit=set_default: Use it to set the default of a MetaSound graph input, or with nodeId the literal on a node input (an oscillator frequency, an envelope time, a note array).
edit=batch: Use it to run many MetaSound graph edits in one call: add nodes, inputs and outputs, connect pins and set literals, with $id references between steps.

name.description: Name of the asset, actor or mapping to create, or of the mapping to remove.

path.description: Canonical /Game folder for the created asset.

oneShot.description: false makes a continuous source with no On Finished output: the engine treats it as looping, so a hum or ambience whose AudioComponent starts out of earshot resumes when the listener comes near. Default true (it plays until On Finished fires).

save.description: Persist the asset to disk (default true); false leaves the change in memory only.

inputType.description: Graph input data type (Float, Int32, Bool, String, Trigger, Audio).

defaultValue.description: Value in the data type of the input: a number (Float, Int32, Time, enums), a boolean, a string, or a JSON array of them for an array input such as Float:Array. Converted to the declared type; a mismatch is refused.

nodeClassName.description: Node class name; short names such as Sine resolve against the MetaSound registry (UE.Sine.Audio).

nodeType.description: Node type or class short name.

sourceOutputName.description: Output pin name on the source node.

targetInputName.description: Input pin name on the target node.

nodeId.description: Graph node id (the id add_node returned, or one from get_metasound_graph).

nodeIds.description: Several node ids to remove in one call, in place of nodeId; every one must exist or nothing is removed.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200, stopping at the first failure; every add_node class is looked up first, so a node class the registry does not hold fails the batch with nothing applied, and so is every pin a connect or set_default names on a node the batch adds (a wrong one fails with PIN_NOT_FOUND and that node's pins). Each is {edit, ...the params of that edit}: edit is add_node, connect, disconnect, remove_node, set_default, add_input or add_output (the add_metasound_node, connect_metasound_nodes, disconnect_metasound_nodes, remove_metasound_node, set_metasound_default, add_metasound_input, add_metasound_output params). Optional per step: id (names the node it creates; later steps use "$id" in nodeId/nodeIds/sourceNodeId/targetNodeId), from/to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect; interface nodes such as the On Play input are named with the explicit fields).

discovery.summary: Fade a sound an actor or audio component plays. soundName is an actor label or name, or an audio component name; componentName picks one of that actor's audio components (refused, listing the ones it has, when it names none), else the first. in (re)starts the sound from its beginning, rising from silence to targetVolume (default 1) over fadeInTime; out lowers it to targetVolume (default 0) over fadeOutTime and then stops it, whatever the level, and changes nothing when it was not playing; to_volume changes the volume of the sound playing to targetVolume over fadeTime (default 1 s), stopping it at 0 (the default), and is refused with SOUND_NOT_PLAYING when nothing plays. The engine ignores a fade out to a level at or above the current one. While a game runs in the editor, the name resolves in the game first. The reply names the actor and component, the fade time and volume used, and playing (whether the sound plays after the call).
whenToUse: fade=to_volume: Use it to fade a named sound instance to a target volume.
fade=in: Use it to fade a sound instance in.
fade=out: Use it to fade a sound instance out.

componentName.description: Name of the component to create or address.

actorName.description: Name of the actor that was spawned or acted upon.

componentName.description: Name of the audio component that was created, spawned or faded.

fadeTime.description: Seconds the fade takes, as used.

discovery.summary: Play a sound: 2D, at a location (played or spawned), attached to an actor, or prime it for playback. A 2D sound (looping music too) plays until stop_sound. measure plays it 2D and reports how loud it played (peak and average dB, silent). The sounds already playing are listed by console_command au.DumpActiveSounds.
whenToUse: playback=2d: Use it to play a sound asset 2D, tied to no place, at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, on the running game while one plays, else in the editor; it plays to its end, a looping one until stop_sound. A path that loads no sound is ASSET_NOT_FOUND, and an editor with sound off answers NOT_PLAYED.

playback=at_location: Use it to play a sound once at location (and rotation), at volume and pitch (default 1) from startTime seconds, with an optional attenuationPath and concurrencyPath (ASSET_NOT_FOUND when one does not load). It plays in the running game while one plays, heard from its listener, else in the editor. Fire and forget: only stop_sound with all true stops it.
playback=spawn_at_location: Use it to spawn a transient sound at a world location.

playback=attached: Use it to play a sound attached to an actor (actorName; in the running game while one plays, else in the level) on the component or socket attachPointName names, else on its root, at volume and pitch. The reply gives componentName, attachedTo and playing; an unknown actor is ACTOR_NOT_FOUND and an unknown attach point ATTACH_POINT_NOT_FOUND.
playback=prime: Use it to prime a sound asset for playback.

playback=measure: Use it to play a sound 2D and measure how loud it played, from the mixer's own meter: peak and average level in dB and a timeline, with silent: true when it played but produced no audio (an empty Sound Cue, a MetaSound whose audio output is unconnected). A Sound Wave also gets the peak, RMS and length of the recording itself (wavePeakDb, waveRmsDb, waveSeconds), which hold however slowly the editor draws. Answers when the sound ends or after maxSeconds.

soundPath.description: Canonical /Game sound asset path (SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound).

componentName.description: Name of the component to create or address.

attachPointName.description: Socket or bone name to attach the sound to.

maxSeconds.description: Longest the measurement runs, in seconds (default 5, 0.2 to 20). A sound that ends sooner ends it then; looping sounds, music and MetaSounds that never trigger On Finished play until this.

playback.description: Which play sound variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

componentName.description: Name of the audio component that was created, spawned or faded.

peakDb.description: Loudest level the sound reached, in dB of full scale (0 is full scale, -120 means no signal). The mixer meters each sound after its own volume and before distance attenuation; the editor being in the background does not lower it.

averageDb.description: Mean level over every reading in dB, the release tail included.

silent.description: True when the peak stayed below -60 dB: the sound played but produced no audio; the warning says the likely cause.

envelopeUpdates.description: Meter readings that arrived, about one per editor frame; 0 means the engine never rendered the sound.

endedBecause.description: finished (the sound ended on its own), maxSeconds (cut there, as looping sounds and music always are) or stopped (stopped by another call, or its Play-In-Editor world ended).

timeline.description: Loudest reading in dB in each timelineStepSeconds step from the start, null for a step no reading landed in (a slow editor frame).

timelineStepSeconds.description: Seconds each timeline entry covers: 0.05 for sounds up to 5 s, longer so there are at most 100 entries.

wavePeakDb.description: A Sound Wave only: the loudest sample of the recording itself, in dB of full scale, read from its imported audio rather than the meter, so it holds however few frames the editor drew. Before volume. Compare sounds by this when matching levels.

waveRmsDb.description: A Sound Wave only: the average (RMS) level of the whole recording in dB, before volume.

waveSeconds.description: A Sound Wave only: the length of the recording in seconds.

edit=set_emitter_properties: Emitter config must change.

edit=connect_pins: Modules must wire together.

parameters.description: Several values written together and saved once, in place of parameterName and parameterValue: each {parameterName, parameterValue} names a user parameter, a module input or a module's static switch as get_niagara_info lists it (InitializeParticle.Lifetime, InitializeParticle.Ribbon Width Mode), and emitterName and save apply to every entry. With actorName (edit=set_parameter) each entry is a user parameter of that placed effect, in place of parameterName and value. The reply lists every entry (parameterName, applied, error); the call fails PARAMETER_BATCH_INCOMPLETE naming any that did not apply, and the others stay written.

discovery.summary: LODs for the meshes the geometry tools make. generate (lodOp generate, the default) bakes the dynamic mesh of actorName or targetActor into a new static mesh asset saved at outputPath (default /Game/GeneratedMeshes/<actor>_LOD) with lodCount LODs in all (default 4, LOD 0 included, each later one half the triangles of the one before) and replies assetPath, lodCount and the LOD 0 triangles; the actor keeps its dynamic mesh. set_settings and set_screen_sizes change the static mesh asset the first static mesh component of the actor draws, so every actor drawing it changes, and save it (saved says whether it was written); an engine mesh is refused with ENGINE_CONTENT (duplicate it into /Game and assign the copy first). set_settings rebuilds LOD lodIndex (default 1; INVALID_LOD_INDEX past the LODs the mesh has, so generate them first) at trianglePercent of the base triangles (default 50, or 100 minus reductionPercent; above 0 and at most 100), recomputing normals or tangents when asked. set_screen_sizes writes screenSizes, LOD 0 first, as the screen size at which each LOD takes over, and turns the automatic screen sizes off; values past the LODs the mesh has are ignored (screenSizesSet counts those written).

numRings.description: Number of rings for sphere, capsule, torus, arch.

length.description: Length along the primary axis: the capsule shaft, or the ramp run.

innerRadius.description: In cm, per variant. Disc and ring: the centred hole (disc default 0, solid; ring 25). Pipe: the inner wall (default 40). Torus and arch: the TUBE radius, its round cross-section, not a hole (default 20 torus, 25 arch); the opening under an arch is radius - innerRadius. Spiral stairs: the radius of the central well.

outerRadius.description: Outer radius for ring and pipe primitives.

angle.description: Sweep in degrees: torus default 360 (less leaves an open segment), arch default 180, a half ring. Both lie flat in the local XY plane, starting on local +X and turning toward +Y; give a rotation to stand an arch up.

steps.description: Number of steps (default 8; numSteps wins when both are sent).

numSteps.description: Number of steps for stair primitives.

floating.description: Build the stairs as free-floating steps with no solid underside.

numTurns.description: Number of turns for spiral stairs (converted to a curve angle).

shapes.description: Shapes combined in order onto shapes[0] (which must be a union) as one signed distance field, then meshed. Sizes are cm in the mesh's local space. Each joined shape takes a blend: the radius of the soft fillet where it meets what came before. An entry with mirror or repeat stands for all its copies (at most 1024 shapes in all), applied in its place in the order.

type.description: sphere (radius), ellipsoid (radii), box (extent = half size, rounding), capsule (radius, length of the straight part, along local Z), cylinder (radius, length, rounding, along local Z), torus (radius to the tube centre, thickness = tube radius, in local XY), cone (radius at the bottom, topRadius, length, along local Z, rounded ends). radius also sets an ellipsoid's radii and a box's extent when those are left out; any other size a type does not read is refused.

operation.description: union adds the shape (default), subtract carves it out of what came before (a recess, socket or groove), intersect keeps only the overlap.

center.description: Shape centre in the mesh's local space, cm (default 0,0,0); with relativeTo, in that shape's frame.

relativeTo.description: Index of an earlier shapes[] entry to place this one on: center, rotation, repeat and mirror are then measured from that shape's centre along its own turned axes (not scaled by its size), so the eyes, mouth or buttons of a leaning or turned part stay on it without working out the rotation. mirror then reflects across that shape's own planes.

rotation.description: Shape rotation {pitch, yaw, roll} in degrees; turns the shape's local Z axis for capsule, cylinder, cone and torus.

radius.description: Radius in cm (sphere, capsule, cylinder, cone base; torus: distance to the tube centre). Default 50.

radii.description: Ellipsoid radii along local X, Y, Z in cm.

extent.description: Box half size along local X, Y, Z in cm.

rounding.description: Box or cylinder edge rounding radius in cm (0 = sharp).

length.description: Capsule straight length, cylinder or cone height, in cm (default 100).

topRadius.description: Cone radius at the top in cm (0 = point; larger than radius widens upward).

blend.description: Smooth-join radius in cm with the shapes before it: 0 is a hard edge; a few cm reads as a soft fillet on a union and as a rounded rim on a subtract.

materialId.description: Material slot of the surface this shape forms (default 0). A subtract shape owns the surface it carves, so a carved visor can take its own slot.

mirror.description: Also add this shape reflected across the mesh's own plane through the origin normal to each listed axis ("y" mirrors y to -y): both eyes, both ears or a pair of legs from one entry. Each axis doubles the copies so far, so ["x","y"] gives four; repeat copies are mirrored too.

repeat.description: Copies of this shape with the same size, blend, operation and materialId: a row with offset, or a ring with axis. A row of stitches, rivets round a rim or curls round a head is one entry. The reply's parts[] still lists one entry per shapes[] item, with copies.

count.description: How many, the shape itself included.

offset.description: Row: each copy moves this much further from the previous one, cm.

axis.description: Ring: turn the copies about this mesh axis through pivot (each copy turns with it).

angle.description: Ring: total sweep in degrees (default 360, evenly spaced all round; a smaller arc puts the last copy at its end).

pivot.description: Ring: a point on the turning axis, cm (default 0,0,0).

resolution.description: Grid cells along the longest side of the shapes' bounds (default 128, 16-256): higher is finer and slower; 160-200 suits a hero part.

primitive.description: Which create primitive variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

parts.description: One entry per shape, saying which surface it formed.

groupId.description: Polygroup of the surface this shape formed (index+1).

triangles.description: Triangles of that surface; 0 when another shape covered it entirely.

copies.description: How many shapes this entry became with its repeat and mirror (the shape itself included); absent for a single shape.

warning.description: Present when a union shape is under two grid cells across: its surface can come out ragged, or as almost nothing when it formed under 24 triangles; raise resolution or thicken it.

resolution.description: Grid cells along the longest side, as used.
