topics: author a mesh from vertices and faces
discovery.summary: Edit a procedural/dynamic mesh: create one, append vertices, triangles, a whole polygon cage (append_polygons), parts laid out in rows and grids (append_cuboids), a loft through cross sections (append_loft) or copies of a detailed static mesh (append_mesh) in one call, delete the triangles of a region (delete_triangles), give triangles material ids by region (set_material_id), bake AO, edge, cavity and height masks for materials to read (bake_vertex_colors), set vertex positions, colors or UVs, split normals, translate, or subtract another mesh.
whenToUse: edit=create: A mesh must be built vertex by vertex rather than from a primitive.
edit=create: An existing static mesh asset must be cut, trimmed or edited: create with meshPath, edit, then bake it with convert_to_static_mesh.
edit=append_vertex: A mesh is being authored point by point.
edit=append_triangle: A face must be added to an authored mesh in one call.

edit=append_polygons: A smooth, rounded model starts as a coarse cage: append its vertices and faces here (one polygroup per face), then optimize_mesh subdivide with scheme catmull_clark and iterations 2 or 3.
edit=append_polygons: Faces must be built from an explicit vertex list, quads and larger polygons included, with polygroups or material ids set up front.
edit=append_cuboids: A model is built from rectangular parts: posts and rails, beams, pillars, crates and containers, panels, windows, steps or furniture.

edit=append_cuboids: The same part repeats in a row, a grid or a block (repeat count with offset, rows with rowOffset, layers with layerOffset), each copy taking the next id of materialIds for colour variety.
edit=append_loft: A shape changes its cross section along its length: a ship hull or a car body (sections narrowing to the bow or nose), a fuselage, a bottle, a horn, a tapered column.
edit=append_loft: A pointed end is wanted: give endPoint (or startPoint) and the last section closes as a fan to it.
edit=append_loft: Parts of the skin need their own materials: edgeMaterials gives each edge of the section loop an id, so the strip it sweeps (a waterline band, a stripe, a window row) keeps it.

edit=append_mesh: A model needs detail an existing mesh already has: containers on a ship, window frames on a facade, seats in rows, bolts on a plate, crates in a stack. Copy the detailed part here instead of approximating it with boxes, then bake with convert_to_static_mesh.
edit=append_mesh: The copies need different colours: give materialIds a list for the painted slot and each copy takes the next id.
edit=delete_triangles: A part of an authored mesh must go: faces nobody sees, a piece built in the wrong place, every triangle of one material id before it is rebuilt.
edit=set_vertex_position: An authored vertex must be nudged without rebuilding the mesh.
edit=set_vertex_color: Authored geometry must carry colour the material reads.
edit=bake_vertex_colors: A material needs masks (dirt in crevices, wear on edges, a height gradient) without textures: bake once the shape is final, then convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite.

edit=bake_vertex_colors: Channels: R is ambient occlusion (1 open, 0 occluded); G is 1 minus the convex edge (1 on flat or concave surface, lower along an outward fold such as a rim); B is 1 minus the concave cavity (1 on flat or convex surface, lower in a crease); A is height (0 at the bottom of the bounds, 1 at the top, along local Z).
edit=bake_vertex_colors: White means no effect for every channel except height, so a mesh that was never baked, which reads (1, 1, 1, 1), behaves like one whose masks are all quiet.

edit=bake_vertex_colors: The values reach the static mesh unchanged: the conversion cancels the sRGB encoding the static-mesh build applies (UE 5.1 and later), so a material's VertexColor node reads the baked value and a stored byte is the value times 255.

edit=set_material_id: One mesh needs several materials: give each part an id (0 is the default), then bake with convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite and list one material per id in materials; entry i is the material of id i.
edit=set_material_id: Triangles must be picked by where they are: region.box, region.normal (the top faces are {x:0,y:0,z:1}), region.groupIds or region.materialIds.
edit=set_uvs: An authored vertex needs an exact UV rather than a generated one.
edit=split_normals: Authored geometry shades too soft across its creases.
edit=translate: Authored geometry must shift inside its own local space.
edit=difference: A caller reaches for the CSG name for a subtraction.
whenNotToUse: edit=create|append_polygons: A parametric shape is enough; use a create_* primitive.
edit=append_cuboids: Separate actors are wanted rather than one mesh: use control_actor.spawn.
edit=append_loft: The shape is round about one axis: use model_mesh with modeling=revolve.
edit=append_loft: The shape follows a curved path with one profile: use model_mesh with modeling=sweep or extrude_along_spline.
edit=append_mesh: Each copy must stay a separate actor (moved, hidden or destroyed on its own): use control_actor.spawn.
edit=delete_triangles: A solid must be cut by another shape: use boolean_subtract.
edit=set_vertex_color: A material parameter is the right place for the colour.
edit=bake_vertex_colors: The mesh will be rebuilt afterwards by morphology or remesh_voxel, which drop vertex colours; bake after them.
edit=set_uvs: The whole mesh needs unwrapping; use auto_uv or unwrap_uv.
edit=split_normals: Normals only need recomputing; use recalculate_normals.
edit=translate: The actor itself should move; set its transform instead.
edit=difference: The canonical spelling is available; use boolean_subtract.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

enableCollision.description: Enable simple collision on the created DynamicMesh actor.

meshPath.description: Static mesh asset to start from: its geometry is copied in, each section as the material id of its slot, in the mesh's own local space. Omitted, the mesh starts empty.

position.description: Position {x, y, z} for the operation.

v0.description: First corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle. The triangle faces the side (v1 - v0) x (v2 - v0) points to, as append_polygons faces do; the other side is culled.

v1.description: Second corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle.

v2.description: Third corner {x, y, z} of the appended triangle.

groupID.description: Polygroup id assigned to the appended triangle.

vertices.description: New points {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space, at most 20000. The faces of this call index into this list, so its first point is index 0. Points are never merged with the mesh's existing ones, and a point no face uses is left out.

faces.description: Faces, each a list of three or more vertex indices into vertices (at most 20000 faces). List a face's corners so that (v1 - v0) x (v2 - v0) points outward, and let two faces that share an edge run along it in opposite directions; the call refuses a face wound the other way, or an edge shared by more than two faces, and names the face. A face with more than three corners is triangulated (it may be concave) and all its triangles keep the face's polygroup. The new faces get smooth normals, shared where they meet; split_normals creases the hard edges.

faceGroups.description: Polygroup id of each face, one entry per face, 0 to 1000000 (default: a new unique group per face). Subdivision with catmull_clark treats every polygroup as one face of the cage, so leave this out for a cage of separate faces; give several faces one id to make one flat region.

faceMaterials.description: Material id of each face, one entry per face, 0 to 255 (default 0). A material id becomes a static-mesh material slot when the mesh is baked with convert_to_static_mesh or convert_to_nanite.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z, in the mesh's local space.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z; larger than min on every axis.

materialId.description: Material id of every face of the box and its copies (default 0); a baked asset gets one slot per id.

materialIds.description: Material ids the copies take in turn (copy k takes entry k modulo the list length), counted along count, then rows, then layers: colour variety across a stack or a row. Replaces materialId.

open.description: Faces to leave out, by the direction they face: a face nobody sees (the bottom of a post on a floor, the faces two touching boxes share) costs triangles and can flicker.

count.description: Copies along offset, the box itself included (default 1).

offset.description: Step from one copy to the next, e.g. {x: 200} for one every 2 m.

rowOffset.description: Step from one row to the next.

layers.description: Layers of those rows (default 1), e.g. the tiers of a stack.

layerOffset.description: Step from one layer to the next.

repeat.description: Lay the box out count x rows x layers times, each copy moved by offset per step, rowOffset per row and layerOffset per layer. A step larger than the box leaves a gap between copies.

boxes.description: Boxes to append, at most 2500 once repeats are unrolled: each an axis-aligned box from min to max, its six faces wound outward and each face its own polygroup.

sections.description: Cross sections in order along the shape, 2 to 256, each a list of {x, y, z} points in the mesh's local space, the same count in every section (3 or more for a closed loop). Point k of one section joins point k of the next, so list every section in the same turning order from the same starting place. A section need not be flat (a raked bow); a section a few cm across gives a blunt end, endPoint a sharp one.

closed.description: Each section is a closed loop and the loft a closed tube (default true). false joins open polylines into a sheet (an awning, a curved panel), its faces turned by the order of the points; flip reverses them.

caps.description: Close a closed tube's first and last sections with a flat face each (default true), unless startPoint or endPoint closes that end.

startPoint.description: Close the first section as a fan of triangles to this point instead of a flat cap: a bow, a nose cone, a spire. Needs closed true.

endPoint.description: Close the last section as a fan of triangles to this point instead of a flat cap: a bow, a nose cone, a spire. Needs closed true.

edgeMaterials.description: Material id of each edge of the section loop, one per edge (point k to point k+1; a closed loop has as many edges as points, an open one one fewer): the strip each edge sweeps keeps it, for a painted band, a stripe or a row of windows. Default 0.

capMaterialId.description: Material id of the end caps and tip fans (default 0).

flip.description: Reverse every face. A closed tube is turned outward from the first section's turning order and the way the sections run, so flip is for an open sheet or an inside surface (a tunnel seen from within).

location.description: Where the copy's pivot goes, in the target mesh's local space (default 0, 0, 0).

rotation.description: Turn of the copy in degrees (default none).

scale.description: Scale of the copy on each axis (default 1, 1, 1); a negative axis mirrors it, faces still turned outward.

materialIds.description: The target material id of each material slot of the copied mesh, one entry per slot in slot order (the reply's sourceSlots, or inspect_object objectKind=mesh, says how many): an id, or a list of ids the copies take in turn (copy k takes entry k modulo the list length) for colour variety across a stack or a row. Omitted, each slot keeps its own index as its id.

count.description: Copies along offset, the copy itself included (default 1).

offset.description: Step from one copy to the next, e.g. {x: 200} for one every 2 m.

rowOffset.description: Step from one row to the next.

layers.description: Layers of those rows (default 1), e.g. the tiers of a stack.

layerOffset.description: Step from one layer to the next.

repeat.description: Lay the copy out count x rows x layers times, each copy moved by offset per step, rowOffset per row and layerOffset per layer. A step larger than the copy leaves a gap between copies.

placements.description: Where the copies go, at most 2500 once repeats are unrolled: each placement a transform in the target mesh's local space, an optional repeat on up to three axes (its steps add to location and are not turned by rotation), and how the copy's material slots map to the target's material ids.

lod.description: Which geometry is copied: source (default) is the full-detail source mesh; render is the mesh as it draws, for a Nanite mesh its fallback, often a twentieth of the source triangles: use it to lay out many copies of a Nanite part within the mesh's 500000-triangle budget.

triangleIndices.description: Triangle ids the operation is limited to; omit to apply it to the whole mesh. Give this or region, not both.

region.description: Pick the triangles to work on by where they are or what they carry, instead of by id; give this or triangleIndices, not both. Every filter given must hold, so they AND together. Boxes and directions are in the mesh's local space, not world space. A region that matches nothing is refused (REGION_EMPTY) with the mesh's local bounds in the message, and the reply's trianglesSelected says how many triangles were picked.

box.description: Triangles whose centroid lies inside this box (inclusive), in the mesh's local space.

min.description: Corner with the smallest x, y and z.

max.description: Corner with the largest x, y and z.

normal.description: Direction {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space; picks the triangles that face it, within normalAngle. {x: 0, y: 0, z: 1} is the top faces.

normalAngle.description: Degrees either side of normal that still count as facing it (default 30).

groupIds.description: Triangles that belong to one of these polygroup ids; a mesh without polygroups is all group 0.

materialIds.description: Triangles that carry one of these material ids (a mesh without material ids is all 0).

vertexIndex.description: Index of the vertex the operation targets.

setAll.description: Apply the colour to every vertex instead of one.

aoRays.description: Hemisphere rays per vertex for occlusion (default 32, clamped to 8-256); the bake cuts them on a very dense mesh to keep the call short, and the reply says how many it used.

aoDistance.description: How far an occluder can be, in cm (default 15% of the bounds diagonal); nearer geometry darkens R, farther geometry is ignored.

curvatureScale.description: Strength of the G and B masks (default 1): a fold of a quarter turn (90 degrees) is a full edge or cavity at 1; use 2 to make a 45 degree fold full, 0 to switch both masks off.

blurIterations.description: Neighbour-averaging passes over R, G and B (default 1, 0 to 16); 0 keeps the masks per vertex and noisy.

materialId.description: Material id to set, 0 to 255. The baked asset gets the highest id used + 1 slots.

splitAngle.description: Angle threshold in degrees above which normals are split.

translation.description: Translation {x, y, z} applied to every mesh vertex.

targetActor.description: Target actor name for boolean operations.

toolActor.description: Tool actor name for boolean operations.

keepTool.description: Keep the tool actor after the operation.

edit.description: Which edit dynamic mesh variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

enableCollision.description: Enable simple collision on the created DynamicMesh actor.

triangleCount.description: With meshPath: triangles copied from the asset.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

vertexIndex.description: Index of the vertex the operation targets.

vertexCount.description: Vertex count of the mesh after the call.

triangleIndex.description: Index of the triangle the operation targets.

vertexIndex0.description: Index of the first appended corner.

vertexIndex1.description: Index of the second appended corner.

vertexIndex2.description: Index of the third appended corner.

verticesAdded.description: Points appended: those some face uses.

trianglesAdded.description: Triangles the faces came to once larger polygons were triangulated.

groupCount.description: Distinct polygroups the mesh holds after the call.

copies.description: Copies appended once repeats were unrolled.

sourceSlots.description: Material slots of the copied mesh: the entries each placement's materialIds needs.

materialIdsInUse.description: Every material id the mesh carries now, ascending: one material each when it is baked.

position.description: Position {x, y, z} for the operation.

verticesModified.description: Number of vertices whose colour changed.

aoRays.description: Rays per vertex that were traced.

averages.description: Mean of each channel over the vertices, {r, g, b, a}, to see at a glance whether a mask did anything.

splitAngle.description: Angle threshold in degrees above which normals are split.

translation.description: Translation {x, y, z} applied to every mesh vertex.

discovery.summary: Polygon modeling on a mesh: extrude, inset, outset, offset faces, bevel, chamfer, bridge, loft, sweep, revolve, shell, loop cut, edge split, poke faces, group triangles into quads, or extrude/duplicate along a spline. Extrude, inset, outset, offset, bevel, chamfer and poke work on every triangle, on triangleIndices, or on a region picked by box, facing direction, polygroup or material id. Dynamic meshes are always triangles.
whenToUse: modeling=extrude: Faces must be extruded along a direction; pick them with triangleIndices or a region (the top faces are region.normal {x:0,y:0,z:1}).
modeling=inset: Faces must be inset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=outset: Faces must be outset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=offset_faces: Faces must be offset; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=bevel: Edges must be beveled; pick the faces whose edges bevel with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=chamfer: Edges must be chamfered; pick the faces whose edges chamfer with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=bridge: Two edge loops must be bridged.
modeling=loft: A lofted surface between profiles must be created.
modeling=sweep: A swept solid must be created.
modeling=revolve: A lathe/revolve solid must be created.
modeling=shell: A hollow shell must be generated.
modeling=loop_cut: An edge loop must be inserted.
modeling=edge_split: Specific edges must be subdivided.
modeling=poke: Faces must be split from their centre, or pushed out into pyramids or spikes; pick them with triangleIndices or a region.
modeling=quadrangulate: A triangulated mesh must be edited as quads.
modeling=extrude_along_spline: A mesh must be swept along a spline path.
modeling=duplicate_along_spline: Copies of a mesh must be distributed along a spline.
whenNotToUse: modeling=poke: The whole mesh should be refined evenly; use subdivide.
modeling=quadrangulate: Real quad topology is needed in an exported asset; meshes in Unreal are always triangles.

normal.description: Direction {x, y, z} in the mesh's local space; picks the triangles that face it, within normalAngle. {x: 0, y: 0, z: 1} is the top faces.

normalAngle.description: Degrees either side of normal that still count as facing it (default 30).

groupIds.description: Triangles that belong to one of these polygroup ids; a mesh without polygroups is all group 0.

materialIds.description: Triangles that carry one of these material ids (a mesh without material ids is all 0).

segments.description: Subdivisions for a rounded bevel (UE 5.4 or later); omit or 0 for a flat bevel.

splineActorName.description: Spline actor name for extrude/sweep along spline.

cap.description: Close open ends: the tube ends of a loft, sweep or extrude along a spline, or for a revolve flat discs from the first and last profile points to the axis (revolve default true).

steps.description: Path steps along a sweep (default 16; the profile uses half as many sides), or segments around the axis for a revolve (default 16, 3 to 512; 48 or more reads as round).

name.description: Name for the new asset or node.

location.description: World location {x, y, z}.

rotation.description: Rotation {pitch, yaw, roll}.

radius.description: Distance from the axis in cm, 0 or more.

height.description: Height above the base in cm.

profile.description: Points from bottom to top, at least 2. For a hollow shape with walls, go up the outside and back down the inside. A closed loop (end on the first point) with cap false turns a solid ring section, such as a moulding or a tyre. Omit for a small built-in vase.

angle.description: Degrees to turn the profile about local Z, 1 to 360 (default 360), starting on local +X and turning toward +Y; less leaves an open wedge whose two cut faces are not closed.

edges.description: Edge ids to split at their midpoints.

respectUVSeams.description: Never pair two triangles across a UV seam (default true).

respectHardNormals.description: Never pair two triangles across a hard edge (default false).

modeling.description: Which model mesh variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

trianglesSelected.description: Triangles the operation worked on: the triangleIndices or region selection, else every triangle of the mesh.

trianglesAfter.description: Triangle count after (before + 2 per poked triangle).

skipped.description: Degenerate or missing triangles that were left alone.

singleTriangleGroups.description: Triangles left in a group of their own.

largerGroups.description: Groups of more than two triangles.

examples.title: Polygon modeling on a mesh: extrude, inset, outset, offset faces, bevel, chamfer, bridge, loft, sweep, revolve, shell, loop cut, edge split, poke faces, group triangles into quads, or extrude/duplicate along a spline. Extrude, inset, outset, offset, bevel, chamfer and poke work on every triangle, on triangleIndices, or on a region picked by box, facing direction, polygroup or material id. Dynamic meshes are always triangles.

topics: round the edges of a cage
discovery.summary: Optimize, smooth or repair a mesh: simplify, remesh (uniform or voxel), subdivide (pn tessellation, or Catmull-Clark, Loop and bilinear surfaces from a polygroup cage), morphology (voxel offset: dilate, contract, close to fillet where unioned parts meet, open), merge or weld vertices, remove degenerates, fill holes, flip or recalculate normals, recompute tangents.
whenToUse: optimization=simplify_mesh: A mesh must be simplified.
optimization=remesh_uniform: A uniform remesh is needed.

optimization=remesh_voxel: A watertight voxel remesh is needed, for example to fuse unioned or overlapping parts into one skin. The grid cell is targetEdgeLength, or the longest side divided by voxelCount (default 128). The surface is rebuilt, so UVs, material ids, polygroups and vertex colours are dropped: run auto_uv, set_material_id and bake_vertex_colors afterwards.

optimization=subdivide: A mesh must be refined. For a smooth, rounded model, author a coarse polygon cage (edit_dynamic_mesh append_polygons, one polygroup per face, or create_box) and subdivide it with scheme catmull_clark, iterations 2 or 3.
optimization=subdivide: The cage carries material ids and polygroups through the subdivision, so assign them with set_material_id first.
optimization=morphology: Joined parts need a smooth blend: boolean_union them, then morphology close with a distance about the fillet radius, then auto_uv, set_material_id and bake_vertex_colors.
optimization=morphology: A mesh must grow or shrink evenly (dilate, contract), or small bumps must go (open).
optimization=merge_vertices: Duplicate vertices must be welded/merged.
optimization=weld_vertices: Vertices must be welded by threshold.
optimization=remove_degenerates: Degenerate triangles must be removed.
optimization=fill_holes: Mesh holes must be capped.
optimization=flip_normals: Normals must be flipped (inside-out).
optimization=recalculate_normals: Normals must be recalculated.
optimization=recompute_tangents: Tangents must be recomputed for correct shading.
whenNotToUse: optimization=subdivide: Edges must stay sharp; subdivision rounds every edge of the cage.
optimization=morphology: Edges must stay crisp; the grid rounds every feature narrower than about twice distance.
optimization=morphology: UVs, material ids, polygroups or vertex colours must survive; the surface is rebuilt from the grid, so set them afterwards.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Actor name in the level.

targetActor.description: Target actor name for boolean operations.

voxelCount.description: Grid cells along the mesh's longest side for the voxel operations (default 128, clamped to 16-256): more cells keep thinner detail and cost more time and triangles. The reply's voxelSize is the resulting cell width in cm.

iterations.description: Subdivision level, 1 to 6 (default 1). Each level quadruples the face count, so 2 or 3 is enough for a smooth result; the call is refused past 500000 triangles.

scheme.description: Subdivision scheme (default pn). pn: PN tessellation, which adds triangles and keeps the shape. catmull_clark: a smooth subdivision surface over a polygon cage, where every polygroup is one face (build the cage with edit_dynamic_mesh append_polygons, or start from create_box, which has one polygroup per face); the surface rounds toward the cage, and polygroups and material ids carry through. loop: smooths the triangles as they are and needs no cage. bilinear: cuts the cage into quads without smoothing. iterations is the level.

operation.description: dilate grows the surface outward by distance, contract shrinks it inward; close (the default) fills creases and rounds the seams where parts meet, a fillet up to about twice distance wide; open shaves off bumps and thin parts smaller than distance.

distance.description: Offset distance in cm (default 2% of the mesh's longest side). Keep it above one voxel (the longest side divided by voxelCount) or the effect barely registers.

optimization.description: Which optimize mesh variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

cageFaces.description: Cage faces: polygroups for catmull_clark and bilinear, triangles for loop; absent for pn.

voxelCount.description: Grid cells along the longest side after clamping.

voxelSize.description: Width of one grid cell in cm.

note.description: What the rebuild dropped, and a hint when distance is under one voxel.

examples.title: Optimize, smooth or repair a mesh: simplify, remesh (uniform or voxel), subdivide (pn tessellation, or Catmull-Clark, Loop and bilinear surfaces from a polygroup cage), morphology (voxel offset: dilate, contract, close to fillet where unioned parts meet, open), merge or weld vertices, remove degenerates, fill holes, flip or recalculate normals, recompute tangents.

discovery.summary: Split a static mesh asset into one static mesh per connected part (or per material slot), each with its own pivot, the materials it uses and a collision choice.
whenToUse: A library pack or kit came in as one static mesh and its props must be placed one by one: split it, then place each new mesh (offset says where its pivot stood in the source, so the original layout can be rebuilt).
A mesh must be separated by material slot (by material).
whenNotToUse: A dynamic mesh actor being modelled must become an asset (use convert_to_static_mesh).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

meshPath.description: The static mesh asset to split; it is not changed.

by.description: parts (default): one mesh per separate object, where connected pieces whose bounds touch or come within gap cm are one object (a crate's planks stay one crate); material: one per material slot.

gap.description: With by parts: pieces whose bounds come within this many cm of each other are one object (default 2).

outputPath.description: Folder for the new meshes (default: the folder of the source mesh).

namePrefix.description: Names are <namePrefix>01, <namePrefix>02 ..., largest part first (default <source name>_Part); a name already taken refuses the split before anything is made.

pivot.description: Each new mesh's pivot: bottom (default), the bottom centre of its bounds, so it stands on what it is placed on; center; or source, the source's own origin.

minTriangles.description: Objects with fewer triangles are left out (default 12): loose bits, decal cards.

maxParts.description: More parts than this (default 64) refuses the split with nothing made.

dropRepeats.description: Leave out an object that only repeats a larger one where it stands, such as an LOD copy an importer merged into the mesh (default true).

dryRun.description: Answer the meshes the split would make (size, triangles, offset, and exists when the name is taken) and create nothing, to tune gap and minTriangles first. A large pack can take longer than one call waits.

collision.description: Collision for the baked asset: box (default) is one box the size of the bounds, which pawns can stand on (on a converted-over asset too); complex uses the render triangles as simple collision too, exact but costly; none gives the asset no collision at all.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

meshes.description: One entry per new mesh, largest first: assetPath, triangles, size [x, y, z], offset [x, y, z] (its pivot in the source's space), slots; saved: false when it could not be written to disk.

skippedSmall.description: Objects left out for having fewer than minTriangles triangles.

droppedRepeats.description: Objects left out as repeats of a larger one.

examples.title: Split a static mesh asset into one static mesh per connected part (or per material slot), each with its own pivot, the materials it uses and a collision choice.

discovery.summary: Configure an interactable: door, chest or switch properties, a door that follows a switch, or its interaction trace.
whenToUse: setting=door: An existing door needs a new open angle, open time or locked state; fields left out keep their value.
setting=door: A door must open and shut with a switch or lever (switchPath); each placed door then gets its placed switch as LinkedSwitch (control_actor.set_blueprint_variables).
setting=chest: An existing chest needs its locked state, lid open angle, open time or loot table path changed; fields left out keep their value.

setting=switch: An existing switch needs a different type (a pressure_plate is on while stood on, a button or lever flips per press), a toggle-back rule or a reset delay; fields left out keep their value.
setting=trace: The trigger of an interactable Blueprint must be resized: every sphere gets radius traceDistance, every box gets extent traceDistance by traceRadius.
setting=trace: Give traceDistance, traceRadius and traceType together, since an omitted one resets to 200, 50 or sphere; traceType only stores a name.
whenNotToUse: setting=door|chest|switch: The Blueprint does not exist yet or lacks the components its create step adds (use manage_interaction.create_interactable).
setting=door|chest|switch: One placed actor needs its own values, not the Blueprint default (use control_actor.set_blueprint_variables).
setting=trace: The Blueprint has no sphere or box component to resize (add one with manage_interaction.create_interactable, kind=component).
setting=trace: Only one of several sphere or box components should change, since every one is resized (use blueprint.edit_scs).

doorPath.description: Canonical /Game door actor Blueprint asset path.

openAngle.description: Open angle in degrees (a new door gets 90, a new chest lid 100).

openTime.description: Seconds the door or lid takes to swing fully open or shut (a new door gets 0.5, a new chest 0.6).

switchPath.description: The switch, lever or trigger Blueprint (from create_interactable) the door follows: on when switched on, shut when off. The door is then locked against opening when a pawn walks up, unless locked is given.

chestPath.description: Canonical /Game chest actor Blueprint asset path.

canToggle.description: Whether the switch can toggle back off.

traceType.description: Free-text name stored in the TraceType Name variable of the Blueprint (default sphere). It does not choose or change a trace shape: the shape comes from the sphere and box components, which traceDistance and traceRadius resize.

traceDistance.description: Interaction trace distance in world units.

traceRadius.description: Cross-section of each box component in world units (default 50): a box gets extent traceDistance by traceRadius. Sphere components ignore it.

setting.description: Which configure interactable variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Create an interactable: a door or chest that opens when a pawn comes near, a switch or lever a pawn presses (it fires OnSwitchChanged), a trigger actor, an interactable interface, or an interaction component.
whenToUse: kind=door: A door Blueprint is needed with a pivot, a door mesh and a trigger box, plus open-angle, timing, lock and key variables; the door swings open (yaw, over openTime) while a pawn overlaps the trigger and it is unlocked, and autoClose shuts it autoCloseDelay seconds after the last pawn leaves. Calling it again on an existing door adds that opening logic.

kind=chest: A chest Blueprint is needed with a base mesh, a lid mesh on a pivot, a trigger sphere and an optional locked state; its lid swings open (pitch, over openTime) while a pawn overlaps the trigger and the chest is unlocked.

kind=switch|lever: A switch, button or lever needs an actor Blueprint with mesh parts and an overlap sphere as its trigger; a pawn walking into it switches it and OnSwitchChanged(bActivated) fires, which a door can follow (configure_interactable setting door, switchPath).

kind=trigger: A reusable overlap-volume Blueprint is needed with a box, sphere or capsule as its root shape; it is on while a pawn is inside and fires OnSwitchChanged(bActivated), which a door can follow.
kind=interface: A Blueprint interface is needed that defines Interact, CanInteract and GetInteractionPrompt for actors to implement.
kind=component: An existing Blueprint, such as a player, needs a named overlap sphere whose radius is the interaction range.
whenNotToUse: kind=door|chest|switch|lever|trigger: An actor must be placed in the level from an existing Blueprint (use control_actor.spawn).
kind=door|chest|switch: An existing door, chest or switch only needs new settings (use manage_interaction.configure_interactable).
kind=lever: Switch type, toggle and reset settings must be editable later, which only a switch Blueprint allows.
kind=trigger: A single trigger volume is wanted in the level with no Blueprint asset (use manage_level_structure.create_volume).
kind=interface: A normal actor Blueprint is needed, not an interface (use blueprint.create).
kind=component: A component other than an overlap sphere is needed (use blueprint.edit_scs).

folder.description: Canonical /Game folder that receives the created asset.

openAngle.description: Open angle in degrees (a new door gets 90, a new chest lid 100).

openTime.description: Seconds the door or lid takes to swing fully open or shut (a new door gets 0.5, a new chest 0.6).

autoClose.description: Whether it closes by itself after the last pawn leaves (default false: it stays open).

autoCloseDelay.description: Seconds after the last pawn leaves before an autoClose door or lid shuts (default 3).

triggerShape.description: Trigger volume shape (box, sphere, or capsule).

componentName.description: Name for the component added to the Blueprint.

traceDistance.description: Interaction trace distance in world units.

kind.description: Which create interactable variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Edit a crafting recipe made by create_inventory_asset, chosen by setting. add_recipe_ingredient adds ingredientItemPath (an existing item), consumed quantity at a time (default 1), as Ingredient_<n>. recipe_requirements writes requiredLevel and requiredStation, only the ones sent. A recipe of a custom class is refused, so set its own fields with inspect.set_property. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: setting=add_recipe_ingredient: A recipe needs one more ingredient item with the quantity it consumes.
setting=add_recipe_ingredient: The ingredient is stored under the key Ingredient_<n>, one past the highest n in use (the first is Ingredient_0).
setting=recipe_requirements: A recipe must require a minimum character level or a named crafting station.
setting=recipe_requirements: Only the requirement fields sent are written, so level and station change independently; sending neither is refused.
whenNotToUse: The recipe asset does not exist yet (use manage_inventory.create_inventory_asset).
The recipe is a custom class, not one made by manage_inventory.create_inventory_asset (use inspect.set_property).

ingredientItemPath.description: Ingredient item asset; one that names no asset is refused (ASSET_NOT_FOUND).

quantity.description: How many of the ingredient one craft consumes, 1 or more (default 1).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true, for every inventory action). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

requiredLevel.description: Minimum character level to craft, 0 or more. Only the requirement fields sent are written.

requiredStation.description: Crafting station the recipe needs, stored as given (a station type such as Forge). Only the requirement fields sent are written.

setting.description: Which configure crafting variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

A recipe of a custom class is refused, so set its own fields with inspect.set_property. Saved unless save is false (saved).

A missing item or reference is ASSET_NOT_FOUND. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: setting=properties: An item needs custom fields such as a name, description, weight or value written onto its data asset.
setting=icon: An item needs an icon texture or material path recorded on it.
setting=stacking: An item must be marked stackable with a maximum stack size, or flagged as unique.
setting=stacking: Only the stacking fields sent are written, so one can change without the others; sending none is refused.
setting=category: An item must be filed under an existing item category asset.

setting=properties: The target is a Blueprint or class default rather than an item data asset (use inspect.set_property).
setting=icon: The icon image is not in the project yet (use asset.import).

setting=category: The category asset does not exist yet: it is refused with ASSET_NOT_FOUND (create it with manage_inventory.create_inventory_asset, kind=item_category).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true, for every inventory action). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

stackable.description: Whether the item stacks. Only the stacking fields sent are written.

maxStackSize.description: Most items one stack holds, 1 or more. Only the stacking fields sent are written.

uniqueItems.description: Whether duplicate instances of the item are disallowed (bUniqueItem). Only the stacking fields sent are written.

discovery.summary: Edit a loot table made by create_inventory_asset, chosen by setting. add_entry adds itemPath (an existing item) with lootWeight (default 1) and a quantity range (default 1 to 1) as LootEntry_<n>, returning n as entryIndex. remove_entry drops the entry with that entryIndex, or every entry for itemPath (removedCount; no match is NOT_FOUND). quality_tiers replaces the tiers with tiers ({name, dropWeight}) or the five defaults. Data only: the game reads the table, and nothing rolls loot by itself. Saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: setting=add_entry: A loot table needs another item entry with a drop weight and a quantity range.

setting=add_entry: The entry is stored under the key LootEntry_<n>, one past the highest n in use, and n comes back as entryIndex; an earlier removal never makes a new entry overwrite a surviving one.
setting=remove_entry: A loot table entry must be dropped, chosen by the entryIndex that adding it returned or by its item, which removes every entry for that item.

setting=quality_tiers: A loot table needs quality tiers with drop weights; the tier list is replaced whole, and the five default tiers are written when tiers is omitted (an empty or malformed list is refused).
whenNotToUse: The loot table asset does not exist yet (use manage_inventory.create_inventory_asset).
The table only needs to be read (use manage_inventory.get_inventory_info).

lootWeight.description: Chance of this entry relative to the others in the table, 0 or more (default 1).

minQuantity.description: Fewest the entry grants, 0 or more (default 1).

maxQuantity.description: Most the entry grants, at least minQuantity (default minQuantity, or 1).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true, for every inventory action). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

entryIndex.description: Number n of the LootEntry_<n> key of the entry to remove: the entryIndex add_loot_entry returned, or the n in a LootEntry_<n> key of get_inventory_info properties. It is a key suffix, not a position: removing an entry renumbers nothing, and a new entry takes one past the highest suffix in use.

name.description: Quality tier name.

dropWeight.description: Relative drop weight for the tier.

tiers.description: Quality tiers, each {name, dropWeight}: a name without commas or equals signs and a weight of 0 or more. A malformed entry or an empty list is refused; omitted, the five defaults are written (Common 60, Uncommon 25, Rare 10, Epic 4, Legendary 1). Replaces the tiers already there.

setting.description: Which configure loot variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

kind=loot_table: Entries or tiers must go into an existing loot table (use manage_inventory.configure_loot).
kind=crafting_recipe: Ingredients or requirements must be added to an existing recipe (use manage_inventory.configure_crafting).

During Play it streams in the running game, as the Load and Unload Stream Level nodes do, and settles before the reply; otherwise the editor, which keeps every sublevel loaded, shows or hides it as the Levels panel does, and unload hides it with a warning. discovery.summary: Edit the level Blueprint of the open level (levelPath names another loaded level; by default the persistent level), chosen by edit. open opens its editor; add_node adds a node by class or alias (an event bound to a placed actor with actorName and eventName, a reference to one, a component getter with memberClass and memberName) and lists its pins; connect_nodes links two pins through the graph schema, which refuses incompatible ones (CONNECTION_REFUSED, with its reason) and adds the conversion node a cast needs; remove_node removes a node by id, name or title; set_pin_default_value sets an input pin. The level stays unsaved unless save is true (saved), and a transient /Temp level is refused.
whenToUse: edit=open: The level blueprint graph must be edited.
edit=add_node: A new node must be added to level scripting.
edit=add_node: Level logic must react to a placed actor (K2Node_ActorBoundEvent with actorName and eventName) or use one (K2Node_Literal with actorName).
edit=add_node: A function of a class outside the common Blueprint libraries must be called (K2Node_CallFunction with functionName and memberClass).

edit=add_node: A placed actor's component must be used, such as the light component whose SetLightColor changes a light (K2Node_VariableGet with memberClass and memberName, its self pin fed from the actor's K2Node_Literal).
edit=connect_nodes: Two level blueprint nodes must be wired together.
edit=remove_node: A level blueprint node must be deleted, or an unbound K2Node_CallFunction ("Could not find a function named None") must be repaired.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A level blueprint node's input pin needs a literal value instead of a wire (a light color, a print string, a number).
whenNotToUse: edit=open: A sub-level blueprint is needed; use the asset path directly.

edit=add_node: The level Blueprint's nodes must be read, or edited beyond these edits; blueprint.inspect_graph and blueprint.edit_graph take the open level's path (/Game/Maps/L_Main) as blueprintPath.
edit=connect_nodes: The nodes are in a Blueprint asset, not the level Blueprint; use blueprint.edit_graph (edit=connect_pins).
edit=set_pin_default_value: The node is in a Blueprint asset, not the level Blueprint; use blueprint.edit_graph (edit=set_pin_default_value).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

save.description: Save the level after the edit (default false, because saving also writes every other unsaved change in that level); the reply says saved: false while it is only in memory.

functionName.description: Function to bind when nodeClass is K2Node_CallFunction (e.g. PrintString); short function names may also be passed as nodeClass.

memberClass.description: Class that declares functionName when it is not in the common Blueprint libraries, or memberName: a native class name or a Blueprint asset path. The node's Target (self pin) takes an object of that class, so an actor's function or component getter is fed from its K2Node_Literal, while a component's function (a light's SetLightColor is LightComponent's) takes the component that getter returns, not the actor. One that names no class is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT.

memberName.description: Variable a K2Node_VariableGet or K2Node_VariableSet reads or writes, required by both and refused for other nodes: a level Blueprint variable (its own or inherited, such as Tags), or with memberClass a property of that class, such as a placed actor's component (PointLightComponent on PointLight, StaticMeshComponent on StaticMeshActor); with memberClass the node always has the self pin the actor's K2Node_Literal feeds, even for Actor. A wrong name is refused with that class's components listed (VARIABLE_NOT_FOUND), and one Blueprints cannot read, or for a VariableSet write (not Blueprint-visible, read-only), with VARIABLE_NOT_ACCESSIBLE.

actorName.description: Placed actor (label, name or object path) in the edited level that a K2Node_ActorBoundEvent fires for or a K2Node_Literal references; required by both, refused for other nodes. A label two actors share is refused with their names, and an actor of another loaded level with that level (ACTOR_IN_OTHER_LEVEL).

eventName.description: Event dispatcher of actorName that a K2Node_ActorBoundEvent binds, e.g. OnActorBeginOverlap or OnActorEndOverlap; a wrong name is refused with the actor's events listed. Refused for any other node: BeginPlay or Tick go in nodeClass (EventBeginPlay, EventTick).

sourceNodeName.description: Source node: the nodeName or nodeId add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title. An exact match wins; otherwise the last node whose name or title contains it.

targetNodeName.description: Target node: the nodeName or nodeId add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title. An exact match wins; otherwise the last node whose name or title contains it.

nodeId.description: The node: the nodeId or nodeName add_level_blueprint_node returned, or its title, matched exactly (a node that only contains it is not taken). A name or title several nodes share is refused with their names (AMBIGUOUS_NODE).

unboundOnly.description: Remove every call-function node that has no bound function instead of a named node.

pinName.description: Input pin name or display name, as add_level_blueprint_node lists them (NewLightColor on SetLightColor).

propertyValue.description: The pin's new default: a number, true or false, text, an enum value name, an asset path, a vector as X,Y,Z or {x,y,z}, a rotator as P,Y,R or {pitch,yaw,roll}, a color as {r,g,b,a}.

edit.description: Which edit level blueprint variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeName.description: The node whose pin was set.

appliedValue.description: Literal actually stored on the pin (or the resolved object path for an object or class pin).

literalNodeId.description: Guid of the MakeLiteral node carrying the value when the pin itself takes no literal.

saved.description: Whether the level was saved.

setting=add_mapping: Use it to add an Enhanced Input mapping with optional trigger and modifier types, or move one to another key (replaceKey) to remap a control with its modifiers.

setting=map_action: Use it to map an Enhanced Input Action to a key in a context, with an optional trigger and modifier on that mapping; mapping the same action and key again redefines it, and replaceKey moves the mapping of the action from that key to this one.
setting=set_trigger: Use it to add a trigger to an Enhanced Input Action; a trigger of that class already on the action is kept, not stacked.
setting=set_modifier: Use it to add a modifier to an Enhanced Input Action, or to one mapping when contextPath and key are given; a modifier of that class already there is kept, not stacked.
setting=enable_mapping: Use it to enable an Enhanced Input Mapping Context on the PIE local player at a priority; outside PIE it fails with PIE_NOT_RUNNING.

replaceKey.description: A key the action is already mapped to: its mapping moves to key (the remap of a control), keeping its triggers and modifiers unless triggerType or modifierType is sent, and that key stops firing the action. discovery.summary: Configure client-side prediction: client, movement, server correction, or add prediction data (a variable replicated only to the owning client).
whenToUse: setting=client: Use it to set whether a Character Blueprint always replicates its movement transform timestamp (CharacterMovement bNetworkAlwaysReplicateTransformUpdateTimestamp); other Blueprints are refused.
setting=movement: Use it to set a Character Blueprint's movement network smoothing mode and smoothing distances; only the fields sent are written, other Blueprints are refused.
setting=server_correction: Use it to set how long a Character Blueprint's simulated proxies smooth server corrections; other Blueprints are refused.

setting=add_data: Use it to add a Blueprint variable, or convert an existing one of the same type, that replicates only to the owning client (COND_AutonomousOnly) for client-side prediction state. discovery.summary: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.
whenToUse: setting=property: Use it to turn replication of a Blueprint variable on or off, optionally with its replication condition.
setting=condition: Use it to set a Blueprint property replication condition.
setting=rep_notify: Use it to make a Blueprint variable RepNotify: it replicates, and clients call repNotifyFunc when its new value arrives.
setting=net_role: Use it to choose how clients see an Actor Blueprint's actors: ROLE_None turns replication off, ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy turn it on.
setting=dormancy: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's default network dormancy.
setting=always_relevant: Use it to set always-relevant replication behavior.
setting=only_relevant_to_owner: Use it to set owner-only relevancy behavior.
setting=autonomous_proxy: Use it to make every replicated variable of a Blueprint replicate to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly), or undo that; fails when it has no replicated variable.
setting=priority: Use it to configure actor network bandwidth priority.
setting=update_frequency: Use it to configure actor network update frequency.
setting=cull_distance: Use it to configure network relevancy cull distance.
setting=push_model: Use it to turn push-model replication on or off for every replicated variable of a Blueprint; fails when it has none.
setting=replicated_movement: Use it to configure replicated movement.
setting=replication_graph: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's spatially loaded (World Partition) and net load on client defaults; only the fields sent are written.
setting=net_driver: Use it to write the game net driver's rate limits to its class defaults and DefaultEngine.ini, and to the running net driver when there is one; only the fields sent are written.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

propertyName.description: Property name.

condition.description: Replication condition, a ELifetimeCondition name such as COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly or COND_AutonomousOnly; an unknown name is refused.

repNotifyFunc.description: Function clients call when the variable's new value arrives; the variable also becomes replicated. It must take no parameters and return nothing: the Blueprint's own or an inherited one is used, a missing one is created empty (functionCreated), one with parameters or a return value is refused (the compiler drops it), and a name another member holds is NAME_TAKEN.

role.description: How clients see the actor: ROLE_None (not replicated), ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy (replicated). ROLE_Authority is refused: the server always has it.

dormancy.description: Net dormancy, a ENetDormancy name: DORM_Never, DORM_Awake, DORM_DormantAll, DORM_DormantPartial or DORM_Initial; an unknown name is refused.

isAutonomousProxy.description: true: every replicated variable replicates to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly). false: variables using COND_AutonomousOnly go back to COND_None; other conditions stay.

spatiallyLoaded.description: World Partition: stream the actor in by distance (AActor bIsSpatiallyLoaded).

netLoadOnClient.description: Load the placed actor on clients with the map (AActor bNetLoadOnClient).

maxClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxClientRate (bytes per second per LAN client).

maxInternetClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxInternetClientRate (bytes per second per internet client).

netServerMaxTickRate.description: Game net driver NetServerMaxTickRate (server ticks per second).

setting.description: Which configure replication variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

repNotifyFunc.description: The function clients call when the variable's new value arrives.

functionCreated.description: Whether repNotifyFunc did not exist and was created empty (it needs a body to do anything).

compiled.description: Whether the Blueprint compiled cleanly after the change.

saved.description: Whether the asset was saved to disk.

examples.title: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.

discovery.summary: Blueprint RPCs, chosen by setting. create makes a function graph named functionName (a free name: NAME_TAKEN otherwise) in an Actor or ActorComponent Blueprint (INVALID_TARGET otherwise) whose calls run where rpcType says: Server, Client or NetMulticast. inputs are its parameters ({name, type}); reliable defaults to true. The function body is the graph of that name, built with manage_blueprint edit_graph, and it is called like any function. The Blueprint compiles and saves, and actorReplicates says whether it replicates, without which no RPC leaves the machine. reliability makes an existing RPC (that function, or a custom event set to replicate) reliable or not; a non-replicating one is NOT_AN_RPC. validation true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs validate, so check the parameters at the start of the body. changed false means the flag already had that value and nothing was compiled or saved.
whenToUse: setting=create: Use it to create a Blueprint RPC: a function graph named functionName whose calls run where rpcType says, with inputs as its parameters. Actor and ActorComponent Blueprints only.
setting=validation: Use it to clear an RPC's validation flag (withValidation false); true is refused, since a Blueprint RPC has no validation step.
setting=reliability: Use it to make an RPC reliable or unreliable.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

functionName.description: The RPC. For setting=create, a new name that no function, variable, event or other member of the Blueprint or its parent class holds (NAME_TAKEN). For validation and reliability, an existing RPC: a function create made, or a custom event set to replicate in the editor (NOT_FOUND, or NOT_AN_RPC for one that does not replicate).

rpcType.description: Where the call runs: Server (called on a client, on an actor its player owns, and run on the server), Client (called on the server, run on the owning player client) or NetMulticast (called on the server, run there and on every client). Multicast is accepted too, in any case; anything else is refused.

reliable.description: Reliable: resent until it arrives, in order. Unreliable calls can be dropped under load, which suits frequent cosmetic updates. Creating defaults to true.

inputs.description: RPC parameters, each {name, type}, with the types add_function inputs take (Float, Vector, Actor, Array<Int> ...), sent with every call. A nameless entry or a type no pin takes is refused (TYPE_RESOLUTION_FAILED) before anything changes. Default none.

withValidation.description: true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs have a validation step, so check the parameters at the start of the RPC body instead. false clears a validation flag an earlier call stored (changed says whether one was there).

setting.description: Which configure rpc variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

functionName.description: The RPC the call created or changed: its function graph, or the replicated custom event.

rpcType.description: Server, Client or NetMulticast: where the call runs (the server, the owning player client, or the server and every client).

reliable.description: Whether the RPC is reliable: resent until it arrives, in order. An unreliable call can be dropped under load.

compiled.description: Whether the Blueprint compiled cleanly after the change.

saved.description: Whether the asset was saved to disk.

actorReplicates.description: Whether the Blueprint itself replicates (Replicates in its class defaults). Its replicated variables and RPCs reach no other machine until it does; nothing here turns it on.

withValidation.description: The validation flag asked for; only false gets this far, since a Blueprint RPC has no validation step.

changed.description: Whether the call changed anything. false: the flag already had the value asked for, so nothing was compiled or saved.

examples.title: Blueprint RPCs, chosen by setting. create makes a function graph named functionName (a free name: NAME_TAKEN otherwise) in an Actor or ActorComponent Blueprint (INVALID_TARGET otherwise) whose calls run where rpcType says: Server, Client or NetMulticast. inputs are its parameters ({name, type}); reliable defaults to true. The function body is the graph of that name, built with manage_blueprint edit_graph, and it is called like any function. The Blueprint compiles and saves, and actorReplicates says whether it replicates, without which no RPC leaves the machine. reliability makes an existing RPC (that function, or a custom event set to replicate) reliable or not; a non-replicating one is NOT_AN_RPC. validation true is refused (NOT_SUPPORTED): only C++ RPCs validate, so check the parameters at the start of the body. changed false means the flag already had that value and nothing was compiled or saved.

discovery.summary: Configure multiplayer for the project: the default game port for LAN hosting and joining, the online subsystem (Null, Steam, EOS...), and the local split-screen layout. Written to DefaultEngine.ini.
whenToUse: setting=lan_play: Use it to set the project default game port ([URL] Port in DefaultEngine.ini) that listen servers bind and joins without a port connect to; packaged games use it from their next launch and the running editor at once.

splitScreenType.description: Split-screen layout name: None (off), TwoPlayer_Horizontal, TwoPlayer_Vertical, ThreePlayer_FavorTop, ThreePlayer_FavorBottom, ThreePlayer_Vertical, ThreePlayer_Horizontal, FourPlayer_Grid, FourPlayer_Vertical or FourPlayer_Horizontal.

The other kinds add a ready node: surface_sampler, spline_sampler, mesh_sampler (meshPath, checked to load), volume_sampler, static_mesh_spawner (meshPath), actor_spawner (actorClass), spline_spawner, density_filter, distance_filter, height_filter (an attribute range filter), slope_filter (Normal To Density), bounds_filter (culls points outside actor bounds), bounds_modifier, the landscape, spline, actor, texture (texturePath) and volume data nodes, transform_points, copy_points, merge_points, project_to_surface and self_pruning. settings sets any property of the new node by name (INVALID_SETTINGS for one it lacks); nodeName titles it and x, y place it. The reply gives nodeId (for connect_pcg_pins), title, nodeType, settingsApplied and saved; saved unless save is false.

nodeKind=spline_sampler: Points must be sampled along a spline.
nodeKind=mesh_sampler: Points must be sampled on a mesh.

nodeKind=actor_spawner: Actors must be spawned at points.
nodeKind=spline_spawner: Actors/meshes must be spawned along a spline.
nodeKind=density_filter: Points must be filtered by density.
nodeKind=distance_filter: Points must be filtered by distance.
nodeKind=height_filter: Points must be filtered by height.
nodeKind=slope_filter: Points must be filtered by slope.
nodeKind=bounds_filter: Points must be filtered by bounds.
nodeKind=bounds_modifier: Point bounds must be modified.
nodeKind=landscape_data_node: A PCG graph must sample landscape data.
nodeKind=spline_data_node: A PCG graph must sample a spline.
nodeKind=actor_data_node: A PCG graph must sample existing actors.
nodeKind=texture_data_node: A PCG graph must sample a texture.
nodeKind=volume_data_node: A PCG graph must sample a volume.
nodeKind=transform_points: Points must be transformed.
nodeKind=copy_points: Points must be copied from one set to another.
nodeKind=merge_points: Multiple point sets must be merged.
nodeKind=project_to_surface: Points must be projected onto a surface.
nodeKind=self_pruning: Overlapping points must be pruned.
whenNotToUse: nodeKind=node: Pins must be connected; use connect_pcg_pins.

discovery.summary: Build a PCG graph, chosen by edit. create makes a graph asset and create_subgraph one to run inside another (with parentGraphPath it adds the Subgraph node there too); a graph already at the path is refused unless overwrite is true, which hands back that graph unchanged (created false). connect_pins wires an output pin of one node to an input pin of another (labels default to Out and In; PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the labels). set_node_settings changes an existing node (found by nodeId or nodeName) and refuses an edit that changes nothing. set_partition_grid_size sets the world or one component's generation grid and saves the level unless save is false. Graph edits save the graph unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: edit=create: Procedural content (scattered rocks, trees, props along splines) needs a graph to build it.
edit=create_subgraph: Steps several PCG graphs share (scatter rules, cleanup) should live in one graph run from each.
edit=connect_pins: Points must flow from one PCG node into the next, such as a sampler into a spawner.
edit=set_node_settings: A PCG node must scatter, filter or spawn differently, such as a denser sampler or another mesh.
edit=set_partition_grid_size: Partitioned PCG makes too many small cells, or cells too large to stream well.
whenNotToUse: edit=connect_pins|set_partition_grid_size: A node is added (add_pcg_node).
edit=set_node_settings: A new node (add_pcg_node).

discovery.summary: Add a pin to a material function (assetPath), chosen by io: input adds a Function Input named inputName of inputType (default Vector3; an unknown type is refused) that callers wire into; output adds a Function Output named inputName that carries out whatever is wired into it, of that type. A name the function already has is NAME_TAKEN. The node lands at x, y (default 0, 0), the function recompiles and is left unsaved; the reply gives its nodeId for connect_nodes.
whenToUse: io=input: A material function needs an input pin (scalar, vector, Texture2D, TextureCube, Bool or MaterialAttributes) that callers wire into.
io=output: A material function needs a named result pin so a graph can wire its result out.
whenNotToUse: The asset is a base material; only material functions take input or output pins (a material result goes to Main with material.connect_nodes).
The function does not exist yet (use material.create_material with kind=function).

inputType.description: input only: Scalar, Vector2, Vector3 (default), Vector4, Texture2D, TextureCube, Bool or MaterialAttributes (Float1 to Float4 work too); another type is refused. An output takes the type of what is wired into it.
