discovery.summary: Add a node to a material graph: any expression class by name, or a typed node (parameters, texture sample/coordinate, math, noise, panner, rotator, fresnel, switches, custom HLSL, function call, landscape layer), or build a whole graph (nodes, wires, material properties) in one batch.
whenToUse: nodeKind=node: An expression is needed by class name with no dedicated adder, such as Constant, Constant3Vector (with defaultValue), ComponentMask or Saturate.
nodeKind=node: A texture object must feed a Custom node or a material function input (nodeType TextureObjectParameter with name and texturePath).
nodeKind=node: A material must read a value of a Material Parameter Collection (nodeType CollectionParameter with collectionPath and name).
nodeKind=custom_expression: A calculation the standard nodes cannot express is needed as HLSL, with named inputs and optional extra outputs.
nodeKind=fresnel: A rim light, edge glow or view-angle fade is needed.
nodeKind=if: A value must switch by comparing two numbers: A greater than, equal to or less than B.
nodeKind=math: Values must be combined or reshaped: Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp, Clamp, Power, Frac, OneMinus or Append.
nodeKind=noise: A surface needs procedural variation such as dirt, clouds or breakup, with a scale and a number of octaves (levels).
nodeKind=panner: UVs must scroll over time, as with flowing water or a conveyor belt.
nodeKind=pixel_depth: Distance from the camera per pixel is needed, for depth fades or distance-based blending.
nodeKind=reflection_vector: A reflection direction is needed, for example to sample a cubemap for fake reflections.
nodeKind=rotator: UVs must rotate over time, as with spinning dials or radial effects.
nodeKind=scalar_parameter: A float value must be tweakable per material instance, such as roughness, opacity or a speed.
nodeKind=static_switch_parameter: A compile-time on/off toggle must pick between two graph branches for each instance.
nodeKind=switch: A compile-time two-way branch is needed with no named parameter, chosen by a bool input or the node default.
nodeKind=texture_coordinate: A texture must repeat more or less often across a surface, or read a UV channel other than 0.
nodeKind=texture_sample: A texture must be sampled in the graph; pass parameterName to make it a texture parameter that instances can override.
nodeKind=vector_parameter: A color or vector value must be tweakable per instance, such as a tint or an emissive color.
nodeKind=vertex_normal: The world-space vertex normal is needed, for example for slope-based blending.
nodeKind=voronoi: A cell, crack or cobble-like pattern is needed from a Voronoi noise function; scale is its only setting.
nodeKind=world_position: The world position of each pixel is needed, for world-aligned textures or height-based blending.
nodeKind=material_function: A reusable material function must be called from a material or another function as a single node.
nodeKind=landscape_layer: A landscape weight layer needs its layer info asset, with hardness, physical material and weight-blend option, so it can be painted.
nodeKind=batch: Many nodes, wires and material properties must be built at once, with the material compiled and saved only at the end.
nodeKind=batch: New nodes must be wired to each other in the same call by id ($id) without waiting for node ids.
whenNotToUse: nodeKind=node: The node already exists and only needs wiring or moving (use material.connect_nodes or material.set_node_position).
nodeKind=custom_expression: The code or inputs of an existing Custom node must change (use material.update_custom_expression).
nodeKind=fresnel: The Fresnel node already exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=if: A per-instance toggle is wanted (add a static switch parameter, then use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=math: A math node already exists and only needs new wires (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=noise: A noise texture asset is wanted instead of a per-pixel node (use texture.create_texture with kind=noise).
nodeKind=panner: The panner exists and only its wiring or position changes (use material.connect_nodes or material.set_node_position).
nodeKind=pixel_depth: A pixel depth node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=reflection_vector: The reflection vector node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=rotator: The rotator exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=scalar_parameter: An existing scalar parameter value must change (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=scalar).
nodeKind=static_switch_parameter: The value of an existing switch must change on an instance (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=switch: The choice must change per instance (use a static switch parameter, set with material.set_material_parameter and parameterKind=static_switch).
nodeKind=texture_coordinate: The UV node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=texture_sample: An instance only needs a different texture (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=texture).
nodeKind=texture_sample: The texture asset itself must be made, adjusted or configured (use texture.create_texture, texture.adjust_texture or texture.configure_texture).
nodeKind=vector_parameter: An existing vector parameter value must change (use material.set_material_parameter with parameterKind=vector).
nodeKind=vertex_normal: A normal map should shade the surface: wire a texture sample into Normal (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=voronoi: The Voronoi node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=world_position: The world position node exists and only needs wiring (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=material_function: The function does not exist yet (use material.create_material with kind=function).
nodeKind=material_function: The function needs another input or output pin (use material.add_function_io).
nodeKind=landscape_layer: The material needs a layer blend node that lists the layers (use material.configure_layer_blend).
nodeKind=landscape_layer: The landscape must be painted with the layer (use build_environment.edit_landscape with edit=paint_landscape_layer).
nodeKind=batch: Only one wire is needed (use material.connect_nodes).
nodeKind=batch: Nodes must be deleted or unwired; batches do not run those (use material.delete_node or material.disconnect_nodes).

nodeType.description: Material expression to add: its class name without the MaterialExpression prefix (Constant, Lerp, TextureSample, ScalarParameter, Multiply...) or the full class name; Float, Color, TexCoord and StaticSwitch are accepted as short names. An unknown type adds nothing (UNKNOWN_TYPE).

name.description: Parameter name, when the node type is a parameter of any kind (scalar, vector, static switch, TextureObjectParameter, TextureSampleParameter2D), or the parameter of collectionPath a CollectionParameter node reads.

collectionPath.description: Material Parameter Collection a CollectionParameter node reads (name picks its parameter); a collection that does not load, or lacks the parameter, adds nothing and fails, listing its parameters.

texturePath.description: Texture for a texture node (TextureObjectParameter, TextureSample...): its default, with the sampler type set to match (a normal map samples as Normal). A path that does not load adds nothing and fails.

defaultValue.description: Initial value for a Constant (number) or Constant3Vector (rgb array or {r,g,b}) node.

x.description: Node X position (preferred spelling; posX is the fallback).

y.description: Node Y position (preferred spelling; posY is the fallback).

outputType.description: Output type: Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes.

description.description: Node title shown in the material editor (the Custom node Description).

inputs.description: Input definitions, each {name}; wire one with connect_nodes targetPin set to that name.

additionalOutputs.description: Extra output pins after the return value, each {name, type}: type Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes. Assign each by name in the HLSL (Emis = ...;) and wire it as "$node.Name".

constA.description: Value used while input A is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

constB.description: Value used while input B is unwired (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Lerp).

path.description: Folder for the layer info asset, e.g. /Game/Landscape/Layers (overrides the material folder).

physicalMaterialPath.description: Physical material the layer applies, e.g. /Game/Physics/PM_Grass.

noWeightBlend.description: Exclude the layer from weight blending (default false).

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...the params of that edit}: edit is a node adder (add_material_node, add_scalar_parameter, add_vector_parameter, add_texture_sample, add_texture_coordinate, add_math_node, add_noise, add_custom_expression, ...; or add_material_node with nodeKind, as in the single call: {"edit": "add_material_node", "nodeKind": "world_position"}), use_material_function, connect_nodes, set_node_position, update_custom_expression, set_blend_mode, set_shading_model, set_material_domain or set_two_sided. Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in sourceNodeId/targetNodeId/nodeId), from/to ("$id.Pin" shorthand for connect_nodes, where a source pin may be channel letters like "$uv.G"; "Main.EmissiveColor" is the material output). A created node without x/y is laid out automatically. Deleting and disconnecting are not batched. The batch stops at the first failing step; when every step ran, the material is compiled and saved once.

nodeKind.description: Which add material node variant to run; omit for 'node'.

details.description: Operation details.

nodeId.description: Created node ID.

posX.description: X coordinate the node was placed at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node was placed at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width; an estimate from the node name, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height, from connector count plus an allowance for a parameter node's inline default-value widget. Offset the next node by at least this much to avoid overlap.

overlappingNodes.description: Names of existing expressions whose estimated bounds intersect this one. Absent when placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

assetPath.description: The material the batch edited, compiled and saved.

results.description: Per-step outcome: index, edit, id, success, nodeId, placementWarning, error. A step that ran and has nothing more to say (a plain connect_nodes) is counted in succeeded, not listed; a failed batch lists every step.

nodeIds.description: Step id -> node id for every node the batch created.

failedIndex.description: Index of the step that stopped the batch (failures only).

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile after the batch; compileErrors says why.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors after the batch, empty when the material compiles.

saved.description: Whether the material was saved after the batch.

examples.title: Add a node to a material graph: any expression class by name, or a typed node (parameters, texture sample/coordinate, math, noise, panner, rotator, fresnel, switches, custom HLSL, function call, landscape layer), or build a whole graph (nodes, wires, material properties) in one batch.

discovery.summary: Recompile a material or material function from its graph (compileOp compile, the default; rebuild runs the same recompile) and wait for every shader. A material that does not compile answers compiled false with compileErrors, since it renders as the default material until fixed; saved says whether it was written (save, default true). A material function is updated without the shader check.
whenToUse: compileOp=compile: The compile errors of an edited graph must be read; a material that fails to compile renders as the default material.
compileOp=compile: Graph edits left the asset unsaved, so it must be compiled and saved.
compileOp=rebuild: The shader must be regenerated after graph edits; the compile, error check and save are identical to a plain compile.
whenNotToUse: A property or parameter was just set (material.set_material_property and material.set_material_parameter already recompile).
compileOp=compile: Domain, blend mode or node counts are wanted rather than compile errors (use material.get_material_info).

materialPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of assetPath).

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

compileOp.description: Which compile material variant to run; omit for 'compile'.

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile; compileErrors says why.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors from the material translator and, once it has finished, the shader compile (where a Custom node's HLSL fails); empty when it compiles.

saved.description: Whether the asset was saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Recompile a material or material function from its graph (compileOp compile, the default; rebuild runs the same recompile) and wait for every shader. A material that does not compile answers compiled false with compileErrors, since it renders as the default material until fixed; saved says whether it was written (save, default true). A material function is updated without the shader check.

discovery.summary: Add a Landscape Layer Blend node to a landscape material, listing the paint layers in order (layers; the first previews at full weight), each with its blend: weight, height or alpha. Every call adds a new node, at x, y (default 0, 0); wire its output with connect_nodes (blendNodeId). An unknown blend type is refused. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: A landscape material needs a Landscape Layer Blend node listing its paint layers, each with a weight, height or alpha blend.
All named layers must be added to one blend node in one call (layers takes [{name, blendType}] or plain names).
whenNotToUse: Layer info assets for the layers must be created (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=landscape_layer).
A finished material must be assigned to a landscape (use build_environment.sculpt with sculptOp=material).

layers.description: The paint layers, in order, each { name } or { name, blendType } to give that layer its own blend.

blendType.description: Blend for the layers that do not name one: LB_WeightBlend (default), LB_HeightBlend or LB_AlphaBlend (Weight, Height or Alpha work too).

x.description: Node X position of the layer blend node.

y.description: Node Y position of the layer blend node.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Weight-blend the landscape layers

discovery.summary: Wire an output of sourceNodeId (sourcePin: a name, an index or channel letters such as G or RG; default its first output) into targetPin of targetNodeId, replacing whatever fed that input. targetNodeId Main is the material output (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor...), or in a material function its output named targetPin (the first when left out). The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it). NODE_NOT_FOUND names Main when the target id is missing; INVALID_PIN or PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the inputs the node has.
whenToUse: The output of one material node must feed an input of another node in the same material or function.
A node result must drive a material output such as BaseColor or Roughness (targetNodeId Main).
whenNotToUse: A whole graph of nodes and wires is being built (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=batch).
A wire must be removed (use material.disconnect_nodes).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

sourcePin.description: Source output: its name, its index, or channel letters of the default output ("G", "RG"; X/Y/Z/W work too). Omit for the default output.

targetPin.description: Target pin name. On the material output (targetNodeId Main): BaseColor, Metallic, Specular, Roughness, Anisotropy, EmissiveColor, Opacity, OpacityMask, Normal, Tangent, WorldPositionOffset, SubsurfaceColor, ClearCoat, ClearCoatRoughness, AmbientOcclusion, Refraction, PixelDepthOffset (and SurfaceThickness, Displacement on newer engines); a Cloth material's Cloth and FuzzColor, and CustomData0/CustomData1, name the clear-coat and subsurface pins they share.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Wire an output of sourceNodeId (sourcePin: a name, an index or channel letters such as G or RG; default its first output) into targetPin of targetNodeId, replacing whatever fed that input. targetNodeId Main is the material output (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, EmissiveColor...), or in a material function its output named targetPin (the first when left out). The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it). NODE_NOT_FOUND names Main when the target id is missing; INVALID_PIN or PIN_NOT_FOUND lists the inputs the node has.

discovery.summary: Create a material asset: a standard material, a decal, landscape or post-process material, a material function, or a Material Parameter Collection (values every material reading it shares).
whenToUse: kind=material: A mesh, surface or effect needs a shader of its own and no material asset exists for it yet.
kind=material: A translucent, unlit or two-sided material is wanted from the start (materialDomain, blendMode, shadingModel, twoSided).
kind=decal: A material is needed to project onto surfaces as a deferred decal, such as scorch marks or stains.
kind=landscape: A material is being made for a landscape; it starts empty (Surface domain, Opaque) and its layers are added afterwards.
kind=post_process: A full-screen effect such as a vignette or color grade needs a post-process domain material.
kind=function: A chunk of graph logic must be reused by several materials as one node, listed in the function library unless exposeToLibrary is false.

kind=parameter_collection: One value must drive many materials at once, set once at runtime (a level-wide wetness, wind strength, time of day or flash): a material reads it with a CollectionParameter node (material.add_material_node nodeType CollectionParameter with collectionPath and name), and a Blueprint sets it with SetScalarParameterValue or SetVectorParameterValue of the Kismet Material Library, the collection on its Collection pin.
kind=parameter_collection: An existing collection needs another parameter or new defaults: send it again; parameters are never removed, since materials read them by id.
whenNotToUse: kind=material: A variation of an existing material with different parameter values is wanted (use material.create_material_instance).
kind=material: An existing material must be copied as it is (use asset.duplicate).
kind=decal: A decal material already exists and only its blend mode must change (use material.set_material_property).
kind=landscape: The material exists and only needs assigning to a landscape (use build_environment.sculpt with sculptOp=material).
kind=post_process: A built-in post-process setting such as bloom or exposure is enough (use build_environment.configure_post_process).
kind=function: The logic is used by one material only (build it in that material with material.add_material_node).
kind=parameter_collection: The value differs per object (use a material instance and material.set_material_parameter, or a dynamic material instance per actor).

name.description: Asset name.

path.description: Package path.

materialDomain.description: Material domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess or UI (a widget, brush or font material). The Details panel label (User Interface) and the MD_ name work too.

blendMode.description: Blend mode, such as Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate or AlphaComposite. The Details panel label and the BLEND_ name work too.

shadingModel.description: Shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or TwoSidedFoliage. The Details panel label and the MSM_ name work too.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep it in memory only.

exposeToLibrary.description: Expose in the material function library.

scalars.description: Scalar parameters, each {name, default}: a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default (0 when a new one gives none).

vectors.description: Vector parameters, each {name, default}: default as [r, g, b, a] or {r, g, b, a} (alpha 1 when omitted); a name the collection lacks is added, one it has takes the new default.

kind.description: Which create material variant to run; omit for 'material'.

details.description: Operation details.

created.description: True when the call made the collection, false when it updated one.

scalars.description: Every scalar parameter of the collection after the call: {name, default}.

vectors.description: Every vector parameter after the call: {name, default [r, g, b, a]}.

saved.description: Whether the collection reached disk.

examples.title: Create a material asset: a standard material, a decal, landscape or post-process material, a material function, or a Material Parameter Collection (values every material reading it shares).

discovery.summary: Create a material instance from a parent material, optionally with its parameter values already set, or several instances (a palette) under one consent.
whenToUse: A variation of a base material is needed with new parameter values and no second node graph.
An instance should start with scalar, vector or texture overrides already applied (pass parameters).
A palette of instances of one parent must be made at once (instances), under one consent instead of one per instance.
whenNotToUse: The material needs its own node graph (use material.create_material).
An existing instance needs new values (use material.set_material_parameter); the parent must be a base material, not another instance.

name.description: Instance name.

parameters.description: Several parameter values at once, each {parameterName, parameterType (scalar | vector | texture), value, or texturePath for a texture}; applied counts those that took, and an entry that did not is listed under parameters with why and fails the call.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep it in memory only.

instances.description: Several instances in one call, in place of name: each {name, and any of parentMaterial, savePath, parameters, save}; the call's own parentMaterial, savePath and save are every entry's defaults. Every entry is reported under instances; the call fails naming any that were not created.

details.description: Operation details.

instances.description: With instances: one entry per instance in order: name, success, error and errorCode when it failed, and what a single create reports (assetPath, parameters).

created.description: With instances: how many were created.

examples.title: Instance a base material
Make a palette of instances under one consent

discovery.summary: Delete nodes from a material or material function graph: nodeId, or nodeIds for several. Every wire to a deleted node is cut, the material outputs it fed included, so what it fed falls back to its default; the material is then recompiled and saved unless save is false. Ids that match nothing come back in notFound, and NOT_FOUND answers only when none matched (read the ids with get_material_info or find_node).
whenToUse: An unused or wrong node must leave a material or function graph, taking its wires with it.
Several stray nodes must go in one call (nodeIds).
whenNotToUse: Only the wire to a node must be cleared while the node stays (use material.disconnect_nodes).
Unused nodes must be found first (use material.get_material_info with info=subgraph and orphansOnly=true).

materialPath.description: The material or material function /Game path.

nodeId.description: Node ID to delete.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to delete in one batch, in place of nodeId.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

notFound.description: Ids that matched no node; the call still succeeds while one matched.

saved.description: Whether the material was saved.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Delete nodes from a material or material function graph: nodeId, or nodeIds for several. Every wire to a deleted node is cut, the material outputs it fed included, so what it fed falls back to its default; the material is then recompiled and saved unless save is false. Ids that match nothing come back in notFound, and NOT_FOUND answers only when none matched (read the ids with get_material_info or find_node).

discovery.summary: Unplug the wire into pinName of nodeId (or with nodeId Main a material output such as BaseColor), keeping both nodes; the input falls back to its default. A pin name that matches none fails listing the inputs; a material function output node with no pinName unplugs every output. The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it).
whenToUse: The wire into one input pin of a node must be cleared while both nodes stay.
A material output such as BaseColor must be unplugged (nodeId Main with pinName BaseColor).
whenNotToUse: A node is no longer needed (use material.delete_node, which also clears every wire that used it).
A pin must take a different source (use material.connect_nodes, which replaces the current wire).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

nodeId.description: Node ID.

pinName.description: Input to unplug: a pin of nodeId by name or label (a custom node input such as OB), or for nodeId Main a material output input (BaseColor, Normal...). A name that matches none fails listing the inputs; only a material function's output node takes none, unplugging every output.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Unplug the wire into pinName of nodeId (or with nodeId Main a material output such as BaseColor), keeping both nodes; the input falls back to its default. A pin name that matches none fails listing the inputs; a material function output node with no pinName unplugs every output. The material recompiles and is left unsaved (save_all keeps it).

discovery.summary: Inspect a material or material function: summary with its parameters and overrides, node lookup, node details/properties/connections, node chains and connected subgraphs.
whenToUse: info=material: An existing material must be understood before editing: node ids, parameter names, wiring, domain and blend mode, or the parent and overrides of an instance.
info=function: A material function must be understood before calling or editing it: its inputs, outputs, description and library exposure.
info=find_node: A node id is unknown and the node must be found by expression class, parameter name, function pin name or Custom node title.
info=node_details|node_properties: The settings of one node must be read back, such as a scalar or vector parameter default or a function input or output pin.
info=node_connections|node_chain: The wiring of a node must be traced across the graph, for example to see where its result ends up at the material output.
info=subgraph: Nodes not wired to any output (orphans) must be found, or the connected island around one node listed.
whenNotToUse: info=material: Shading model, sampler counts or the instances of a parent are wanted (use asset.query_asset lookup=material_stats or asset.list kind=material_instances).
info=function: The materials that call the function must be found (use asset.inspect_asset with lookup=dependencies and referencers=true).
info=find_node: The material asset itself must be located by name or class (use asset.query_asset).
info=node_details|node_properties: A parameter value or Custom node code must change, not be read (use material.set_material_parameter or material.update_custom_expression).

info=node_details|node_properties: Any other property of a node must change, such as the Texture or SamplerType of a texture parameter (use inspect.set_property with objectPath "<material path>.<material name>:<nodeId>").
info=node_connections|node_chain: A wire must be added, cut or rerouted, not traced (use material.connect_nodes or material.disconnect_nodes).
info=subgraph: Orphaned nodes are to be removed (use material.delete_node once their ids are known).

materialPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of assetPath).

filter.description: Which sections to return: parameters, expressions, connections, or all (default).

nodeId.description: A node, by the id the graph lists: material and function report only the connections touching it; node_details, node_properties and node_connections describe it; node_chain and subgraph start from it (node_chain also takes it as startNodeId; subgraph needs it unless orphansOnly is true).

nodeIds.description: Only report connections touching these nodes.

nodeName.description: Name to find: a node id, parameter name, function input or output name, or custom node title (substring match).

expressionIndex.description: Zero-based position in the expression list; picks the node when nodeId is omitted.

direction.description: Connection direction to report (inputs or outputs).

depth.description: Traversal depth; -1 walks the whole graph.

upstream.description: Walk every upstream producer, overriding direction and depth.

downstream.description: Report downstream connections instead of upstream.

startNodeId.description: Starting node ID accepted by the handler in place of nodeId.

endPin.description: Terminal pin name to stop the chain walk at.

orphansOnly.description: Report only the nodes whose result reaches no output of the material or function: nothing wired to them, or a branch that ends in a node nothing reads (left behind when the node it fed was rewired). Accepted in place of nodeId.

info.description: Which get material info variant to run; omit for 'material'.

assetType.description: Asset type: Material, MaterialFunction or MaterialInstance.

parent.description: MaterialInstance: the material or instance it overrides.

baseMaterial.description: MaterialInstance: the material at the root of its parent chain, which owns the node graph.

parameterOverrides.description: MaterialInstance: each overridden parameter (name, type scalar/vector/texture, value).

nodeCount.description: Number of expression nodes in the graph.

domain.description: Material domain, e.g. Surface, PostProcess, UI.

blendMode.description: Blend mode, e.g. Opaque, Masked, Translucent.

exposeToLibrary.description: Whether a material function is exposed to the library.

parameters.description: Material parameters of every kind (name, type, nodeId). A texture parameter also carries texture (its default texture path, empty while none is set) and samplerType (Color, Normal, Masks, ...); a runtime virtual texture parameter carries its virtual texture under texture.

details.description: Operation details.

nodeId.description: Resolved node ID.

vectorDefault.description: DefaultValue as rgba, for vector parameter expressions.

inputName.description: Pin name, for a function input.

inputType.description: Pin type, for a function input.

outputName.description: Pin name, for a function output.

sortPriority.description: Pin sort priority, for function input/output expressions.

usePreviewValueAsDefault.description: Whether a function input previews its default.

type.description: Expression class name of the start node.

connections.description: Edges found, each with sourceNodeId, sourceOutputIndex, targetNodeId, targetInput, hop and direction. A targetNodeId of "Main" is the material output node.

examples.title: Inspect a material or material function: summary with its parameters and overrides, node lookup, node details/properties/connections, node chains and connected subgraphs.

discovery.summary: Set material parameter values, chosen by parameterKind. On a material instance it overrides a parameter its parent publishes (a name it does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing the published ones); on a base material it sets the parameter node's default, refused while the material is open in its editor (ASSET_EDITOR_OPEN; the editor would write its own copy back on close). scalar takes a number value, vector value {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture texturePath, static_switch value true or false, and a missing value is refused; parameter takes parameterType (scalar, the default, vector or texture) with value, several at once with parameters, or several instances under one consent with assets. The asset is saved unless save is false (saved).
whenToUse: parameterKind=parameter: Several parameter values on a base material or an instance must change in one call (parameters list).
parameterKind=parameter: Several material instances must be retuned at once, a palette recoloured (assets), under one consent instead of one per instance.
parameterKind=parameter: The default of a parameter node on a base material must change; on an instance the value is stored as an override.
parameterKind=scalar: A float parameter such as roughness, opacity or a speed must change on an instance or as a base material default.
parameterKind=vector: A color or vector parameter such as a tint must change; value takes an rgba object or an array of at least three numbers.
parameterKind=texture: A texture parameter must point at a different texture asset (texturePath).
parameterKind=static_switch: A static switch parameter must be turned on or off; on an instance this rebuilds the shader permutation.
whenNotToUse: The parameter is not on the base material yet (add it there with asset.edit_material_instance edit=add_parameter or material.add_material_node).
parameterKind=parameter: Every override on an instance must be cleared back to its parent (use asset.edit_material_instance edit=reset_parameters).
parameterKind=texture: The texture asset itself needs other compression or LOD settings (use texture.configure_texture).

parameterType.description: Parameter kind: scalar (default), vector, or texture. Selects which parameter expression the value is written to.

value.description: Parameter value.

parameters.description: Several parameter values at once, each {parameterName, parameterType (scalar | vector | texture), value, or texturePath for a texture}; applied counts those that took, and an entry that did not is listed under parameters with why and fails the call.

assets.description: Several materials or material instances at once, in place of assetPath: each {assetPath, and parameters or parameterName with value}; the call's own save applies to every entry. Every entry is reported under assets, and the call fails naming any that did not apply.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

parameterKind.description: Which set material parameter variant to run; omit for 'parameter'.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Set material parameter values, chosen by parameterKind. On a material instance it overrides a parameter its parent publishes (a name it does not publish is PARAMETER_NOT_FOUND, listing the published ones); on a base material it sets the parameter node's default, refused while the material is open in its editor (ASSET_EDITOR_OPEN; the editor would write its own copy back on close). scalar takes a number value, vector value {r, g, b, a} or [r, g, b, a], texture texturePath, static_switch value true or false, and a missing value is refused; parameter takes parameterType (scalar, the default, vector or texture) with value, several at once with parameters, or several instances under one consent with assets. The asset is saved unless save is false (saved).

discovery.summary: Set a property of a material, or override it on a material instance, by materialProperty: blend_mode, domain, shading_model or two_sided. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved), and the reply gives the value written; on an instance the value becomes an override of its parent, as its Material Property Overrides do (instanceOverride), and the domain cannot be overridden (MATERIAL_INSTANCE). An unknown value is INVALID_ENUM, listing the valid ones, and leaves the asset as it was; a material function is UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT), so duplicate it into /Game first.
whenToUse: materialProperty=blend_mode: A material must become translucent, cut out (Masked) or additive instead of Opaque.
materialProperty=domain: A material must change domain, for example between Surface, DeferredDecal, PostProcess and UI.
materialProperty=shading_model: A surface needs a different shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or Hair.
materialProperty=two_sided: Both faces of a mesh must render, as with leaves, cloth or thin sheets.
whenNotToUse: materialProperty=blend_mode|shading_model|two_sided: Only a parameter of a material instance must change (use material.set_material_parameter).
materialProperty=blend_mode: A new material is being created with the blend mode already known (use material.create_material with blendMode).
materialProperty=domain: The target is a material instance: the domain belongs to its parent material (find it with material.get_material_info).
materialProperty=domain: A new material is being created with the domain already known (use material.create_material with materialDomain).
materialProperty=shading_model: A new material is being created with the shading model already known (use material.create_material with shadingModel).

assetPath.description: Material or material instance /Game asset path; an instance takes the value as an override of its parent (every property but the domain).

blendMode.description: Blend mode, such as Opaque, Masked, Translucent, Additive, Modulate or AlphaComposite. The Details panel label and the BLEND_ name work too.

save.description: Save the asset afterwards. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

materialDomain.description: Material domain: Surface, DeferredDecal, LightFunction, Volume, PostProcess or UI (a widget, brush or font material). The Details panel label (User Interface) and the MD_ name work too.

shadingModel.description: Shading model, such as DefaultLit, Unlit, Subsurface, ClearCoat or TwoSidedFoliage. The Details panel label and the MSM_ name work too.

value.description: Two-sided value: true renders both faces, false only the front.

materialProperty.description: Which set material property variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Set a property of a material, or override it on a material instance, by materialProperty: blend_mode, domain, shading_model or two_sided. The material recompiles and is saved unless save is false (saved), and the reply gives the value written; on an instance the value becomes an override of its parent, as its Material Property Overrides do (instanceOverride), and the domain cannot be overridden (MATERIAL_INSTANCE). An unknown value is INVALID_ENUM, listing the valid ones, and leaves the asset as it was; a material function is UNSUPPORTED_ASSET_TYPE; engine content is refused (ENGINE_CONTENT), so duplicate it into /Game first.

discovery.summary: Move a node of a material or material function graph (materialPath or assetPath; nodeId as add_material_node and get_material_info give it) to x and y, keeping every wire. The material recompiles and is left unsaved, and the move is no undo step; the reply gives where the node now sits and warns when it overlaps another.
whenToUse: Overlapping nodes reported by a node add (overlappingNodes) must be spread out without losing wires.
A cluttered graph must be tidied by moving an existing node to new x and y.
whenNotToUse: A new node needs a position (pass x and y when adding it with material.add_material_node).
Wires must change (use material.connect_nodes or material.disconnect_nodes).

assetPath.description: Material asset path (accepted in place of materialPath).

nodeId.description: Node ID to move.

x.description: New X coordinate (posX is the fallback spelling).

y.description: New Y coordinate (posY is the fallback spelling).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

nodeId.description: Moved node ID.

posX.description: X coordinate the node now sits at.

posY.description: Y coordinate the node now sits at.

estimatedWidth.description: Approximate node width; an estimate, not a measurement.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height from connector count plus the inline default-value widget allowance.

overlappingNodes.description: Names of expressions still overlapping after the move. Absent when the placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

examples.title: Space a stacked parameter node out

discovery.summary: Update a custom expression node: its HLSL code, inputs, output type, additional outputs or title. An input that keeps its name keeps its wire. The material is then compiled and saved, and compiled, compileErrors and saved in the reply say how that went (a step of build_material_graph leaves both to the batch).
whenToUse: The HLSL code of an existing Custom node must be rewritten without rebuilding its wiring.
Inputs, output type, extra outputs or the title of a Custom node must change; inputs that keep their name keep their wire.
whenNotToUse: A new Custom node is needed (use material.add_material_node with nodeKind=custom_expression).
The node is a parameter or any other non-Custom expression; only Custom nodes are accepted (parameter values use material.set_material_parameter).

nodeId.description: Node ID.

inputs.description: Replacement input list, each {name}; inputs whose names stay keep their connections.

outputType.description: Output type: Float1, Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes.

description.description: Node title shown in the material editor.

additionalOutputs.description: Extra output pins after the return value, each {name, type}: type Float1 (default), Float2, Float3, Float4 or MaterialAttributes. Assign each by name in the HLSL (Emis = ...;) and wire it as "$node.Name".

compiled.description: False when the material does not compile after the edit (the default material renders in its place); compileErrors says why. A material function has no translation of its own to read, so this is true for one.

compileErrors.description: Compile errors after the edit, from the material translator and, once it has finished, the shader compile (where a Custom node's HLSL fails); empty when it compiles.

saved.description: Whether the material or function was saved after the edit.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rewrite a custom node's HLSL

discovery.summary: Add a cinematic track: camera cut, camera shake, transform, property, skeletal animation, material parameter, particle, event, fade, level visibility, shot, or subsequence.
whenToUse: trackKind=camera_cut: A camera cut track must be added for shot transitions.
trackKind=camera_shake: Camera shake must be animated along the sequence.
trackKind=transform: Add a transform track to animate actor transforms during cinematic.
trackKind=property: Add a property track to animate a specific property on a bound actor.

trackKind=skeletal_animation: Add a skeletal animation track to play animations on a skeletal mesh. A clip whose skeleton the mesh cannot play is refused with SKELETON_MISMATCH instead of silently showing the rest pose. Overlap the clips before and after it and give easeInFrames/easeOutFrames to crossfade between them instead of cutting in one frame.
trackKind=material_parameter: Add a material parameter collection track to animate material parameters.
trackKind=particle: Add a particle track to trigger particle systems during cinematic: trigger fires a one-shot burst (a hit, a spark) once, activate keeps a system running for the section.
trackKind=event: Add an event track to trigger events at specific frames.
trackKind=fade: Add a fade track for cinematic fade-in/fade-out transitions.
trackKind=level_visibility: Add a level visibility track to control level streaming during cinematic.
trackKind=shot: A shot track must be added to organize camera cuts.
trackKind=subsequence: A sub-sequence must be nested inside the master sequence.
whenNotToUse: trackKind=camera_cut: The sequence already has a camera cut track.
trackKind=camera_shake: No camera shake is needed.

trackKind=camera_shake: The shake is gameplay feedback during play (a hit, a landing): create a Blueprint with parentClass /Script/EngineCameras.LegacyCameraShake (blueprint.create) and call PlayerCameraManager StartCameraShake from a graph (blueprint.edit_graph).
trackKind=transform|property|skeletal_animation|material_parameter|particle|event|fade|level_visibility: The track is not needed for this sequence.
trackKind=fade: The fade happens during play (level start, death, level change): call PlayerCameraManager StartCameraFade from a graph (blueprint.edit_graph).
trackKind=shot: The master sequence already has a shot track.
trackKind=subsequence: The sequence should remain flat.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Canonical /Game sequence asset path.

actorName.description: Actor name in the current level.

cameraName.description: Actor name in the current level.

endFrame.description: Section end in display-rate frames; used when durationFrames is absent.

rowIndex.description: Sequencer row index for the created section.

save.description: Whether to save the sequence asset after the mutation.

property.description: Property to animate, by name (Transform, Intensity...); required, or send it as propertyName (refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT when neither is sent).

propertyName.description: Property name to animate (alias of property).

soundPath.description: Audio track only: /Game path of the SoundWave, SoundCue or MetaSound the section plays. Without end the section is as long as the sound (one second for a looping one).

end.description: Section end in display-rate frames, after start (default 100; with soundPath, the length of the sound).

property.description: Property to key: Transform, Location, Rotation or Scale; Visibility, which shows (true) or hides (false) the bound actor in the editor and in renders; or a float or bool property by name.

value.description: Keyframe value. For property "Transform" pass a composed object with any subset of {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}}; each component supplied must carry all of its finite axes; a new Transform track starts from the current transform of the actor, so the parts a key leaves out keep their values. Add lookAt:{x,y,z} beside location to aim the key at that point (a camera at its subject): pitch and yaw are worked out, roll comes from rotation.roll or 0, and the yaw turns the short way from the key before, so an orbit of aimed keys never spins round. For "Location"/"Rotation"/"Scale" pass that component object alone. Visibility takes true or false; other properties take their own scalar value, so no type is declared here.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key: auto (default) a smooth curve through the keys, linear a steady rate to the next key (a bullet, a constant pan), constant a hold that jumps at the next key.

value.description: Key value, in the form value takes.

interpolation.description: How the curve leaves this key; default the interpolation of the call.

keys.description: Several keys on this property in one call, in place of frame and value: a whole curve, or a flash shown on one frame and hidden on the next. Each entry is {frame, value, interpolation}; they are written in order, so lookAt keys turn the short way from the entry before. Every frame is checked before any key is written.

sectionIndex.description: Which section of the track, in the order info=keys lists them (default 0).

startFrame.description: New start of the section in display-rate frames.

endFrame.description: New end of the section in display-rate frames, after its start.

easeInFrames.description: Frames the section fades in over; 0 removes its ease in.

easeOutFrames.description: Frames the section fades out over; 0 removes its ease out.

playRate.description: The speed of an animation section (2 is twice as fast). Without endFrame the section keeps playing the same frames, so it gets shorter or longer by the same factor, as in Sequencer.

edit.description: Which edit sequence tracks variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Record and play back gameplay replays in the running game, chosen by control; outside Play every control is NOT_IN_PIE. start_recording records replayName (else the configured default, else McpReplay_<time>) until stop_recording, which answers the name, and is refused while a replay plays or records (ALREADY_PLAYING, ALREADY_RECORDING). play plays replayName back (refused while recording); pause pauses or resumes it (paused; without it, toggles); seek jumps to timeSeconds, clamped to the replay's length, and answers once playback gets there (REPLAY_SEEK_TIMEOUT after 10 s); set_playback_speed sets speed (at most 16); start_killcam plays the last durationSeconds of the playing replay, or of replayName. pause, seek and set_playback_speed need a replay playing (NOT_PLAYING). Replies give the replay state (activeReplayName, recording, playing, currentTimeSeconds, totalTimeSeconds, paused, playbackSpeed).

control=start_killcam: No killcam is needed.

discovery.summary: Record a take with the Take Recorder (Takes plugin), chosen by setting: sources picks the actors and allowlisted source classes to record and the sequence or preset to record from; recorded_tracks turns recorded properties of actor sources on or off; panel opens the panel and reads its mode, sequence, frame rate and source count; start_recording begins a take once its countdown ends, for duration seconds or until stop_recording; stop_recording finalizes the take and says whether it recorded anything (RECORDING_OUTPUT_EMPTY when not). discovery.summary: Delete a Blueprint Struct asset (deleteScope struct, the default: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, naming referencers, while other assets use it, unless force deletes it anyway and recompiles the loaded Blueprints that used it; NOT_FOUND when there is none) or remove one member (member: by memberName or varGuid; the assets using the struct are refreshed, and it is saved unless save is false).
whenToUse: deleteScope=struct: An unused struct asset must be deleted; a struct still referenced is refused, with its referencers listed, unless force is set.

deleteScope=member: A field only needs a new name or type (use struct.edit_struct).

force.description: Delete even when other assets use the struct, breaking them: the loaded Blueprints among them recompile, and the engine removes their variables of it (the reply's warnings name them). Default false: refused with STRUCT_IN_USE, listing the referencers.

varGuid.description: Stable member GUID, as get_struct lists it; pass this or memberName.

save.description: Persist the struct to disk. Defaults to true; pass false to keep the change in memory only.

deleteScope.description: Which delete struct variant to run; omit for 'struct'.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Create a user-defined struct or edit it: members, defaults, metadata, types, order, rename, duplicate, import, recompile, refresh dependencies, instanced struct properties.
whenToUse: edit=create_struct: A new Blueprint struct is needed; give its members up front, otherwise it keeps one placeholder member.
edit=add_struct_member: One or several fields, each with a type, optional default and tooltip, must be added to an existing struct.
edit=rename_struct_member: A field must be renamed while keeping its type and default; it is found by memberName or varGuid.
edit=reorder_struct_members: One field, named by memberName or varGuid, must move to first, last, or before or after another field.
edit=set_struct_member_default: A field needs a new default value; a value that cannot convert to the field type is rejected.
edit=set_struct_member_metadata: A field needs a tooltip or metadata key and value pairs.
edit=set_struct_member_type: A field needs a different type, for example Int to Float or a container; self-referencing and cyclic types are refused.
edit=rename_struct: The struct asset needs a new name or folder; a redirector is left at the old path when it is referenced, and dependent Blueprints recompile.
edit=duplicate_struct: A struct must be forked into a new asset with the same members, for example to try a second revision.
edit=import_struct: A struct must be rebuilt from a member list or a JSON file; members are replaced and a failed apply is rolled back.
edit=recompile_struct: Dependent Blueprints must be recompiled after a struct change and their compile errors listed; the changed assets are saved unless save is false.
edit=refresh_struct_dependencies: A struct was edited outside these tools and its Blueprints and DataTables must be rebuilt against the new layout; the affected assets are listed.
edit=set_instanced_struct_property: An FInstancedStruct property on an asset must be set to a chosen struct type with given field values.
whenNotToUse: edit=create_struct: A DataTable is wanted as well as its row struct (use datatable.edit_data_table to create the table and bind the struct).
edit=add_struct_member: A variable is needed on a Blueprint, not a field on a struct (use blueprint.edit_variable).
edit=rename_struct_member: A field must be removed instead of renamed (use struct.delete_struct with deleteScope=member).
edit=reorder_struct_members: The current member order must be read before moving anything (use struct.get_struct).
edit=set_struct_member_default: Values stored in a DataTable row must change, not the struct default (use datatable.edit_data_table).
edit=set_struct_member_metadata: Metadata for an enum entry is wanted (use enum.edit_enum).
edit=set_struct_member_type: The assets that use the struct must be found before a type change (use struct.get_struct with info=usage).
edit=rename_struct: A non-struct asset must be renamed or moved (use asset.rename or asset.move).
edit=duplicate_struct: An asset that is not a struct must be copied (use asset.duplicate).
edit=import_struct: The definition must be exported as JSON, not imported (use struct.get_struct with info=export).
edit=recompile_struct: One Blueprint must be compiled rather than a struct (use blueprint.compile).
edit=refresh_struct_dependencies: Only the struct status and validity must be read (use struct.get_struct).
edit=set_instanced_struct_property: A plain property on an actor or asset must be written (use inspect.set_property).

discovery.summary: Read structs, chosen by info. struct (read, members and export give the same reply) reads a Blueprint or native struct: name, status, validity and every member { guid, name, type, default, tooltip, containerType, metaData }, the members array import_struct takes back; list lists the Blueprint struct assets under path (default /Game/Structs, recursive); usage lists the assets that reference a Blueprint struct (assetPath, className, referencerType Blueprint, Struct, DataAsset or Other), narrowed by a searchScope path prefix; compare diffs two Blueprint structs member by member, paired by member guid so a rename reads as renamedFrom and renamedTo, each diff added, removed or changed with its type and default in each, plus tooltip and metadata mismatches (metadata from UE 5.5); instanced_property reads an FInstancedStruct property of an asset. info=usage: Every asset that references a struct, such as Blueprints, other structs and DataTables, must be found before changing or deleting it.
info=compare: Two structs must be diffed for added, removed, renamed or retyped members and changed defaults, tooltips or order.
info=export: A struct definition must be returned as JSON members that import_struct accepts, to reuse or restore it.

info=compare: A struct must be brought in line with another; the comparison only reports differences (use struct.edit_struct).
info=export: A struct must be copied as a new asset (use struct.edit_struct with edit=duplicate_struct).
info=instanced_property: A plain property on an actor or asset must be read (use inspect.get_property).

discovery.summary: Configure performance settings: scalability, frame rate limit, resolution scale, vsync, LOD, Nanite, occlusion culling, texture streaming, World Partition streaming, GPU timing, draw-call and shader optimization, baseline profile.
whenToUse: setting=scalability: A scalability group level must be changed atomically.
setting=frame_rate_limit: A maximum FPS cap must be applied.
setting=resolution_scale: The primary render resolution scale must be changed.
setting=vsync: VSync must be toggled at runtime.
setting=lod: A forced LOD level or LOD bias must be applied.
setting=nanite: Nanite must be enabled or its runtime parameters tuned.
setting=occlusion_culling: Occlusion culling must be enabled or its parameters tuned.
setting=texture_streaming: Texture streaming pool size or player-location boost must be tuned.
setting=world_partition: World Partition runtime settings must be tuned.
setting=gpu_timing: Per-frame GPU timing instrumentation must be enabled or disabled.
setting=draw_calls: Draw-call count must be reduced through instancing or batching.
setting=shaders: Shader compilation must be optimized or force-recompiled.
setting=baseline: A predefined performance baseline profile must be applied.
whenNotToUse: setting=scalability: A single CVar outside scalability groups is needed (use set_cvar).
setting=frame_rate_limit: VSync should be used instead for display-synced limiting.
setting=resolution_scale: The window resolution must change (use set_resolution).
setting=lod: Per-actor LOD is the goal (use control_actor).
setting=nanite: The target mesh is not Nanite-compatible.
setting=occlusion_culling: The scene is too small to benefit from occlusion culling.
setting=texture_streaming: A one-off texture import is the goal (use manage_asset).
setting=world_partition: Level streaming is managed per-sublevel (use manage_level).
setting=gpu_timing: A full profiling capture is needed (use start_profiling).
setting=draw_calls: Actors should be merged into a single mesh (use merge_actors).
setting=shaders: A full material recompile is needed (use manage_asset compile_material).

setting.description: Which configure performance variant to run.

Any other project setting (use set_project_setting).

discovery.summary: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output, at most 4096 characters). A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.
whenToUse: A console command must be run with explicit empty-input rejection.
The sounds playing right now must be listed (is the music still on, did a loop stop): au.DumpActiveSounds puts each one with its asset, owner and volume in output.

C++ must be recompiled while the editor runs: LiveCoding.Compile (read_log shows the result; a Live Coding patch is lost when the editor restarts, so a lasting change needs a full build with the editor closed).
An arbitrary console command must be run and its result returned.
whenNotToUse: The command is empty or whitespace-only.
A dedicated system_control action exists for the operation.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

command.description: The non-empty console command to execute.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

output.description: Bounded console output captured from the command.

examples.title: Run one console command against the editor world, or through the first player while Play In Editor runs, and return what it printed (output, at most 4096 characters). A command the engine does not recognise fails (EXEC_FAILED); one holding ;, |, &&, a backtick or several lines, or a blocked name (quit, exit, py, crash and the like), is refused (COMMAND_BLOCKED). Success means the engine ran it, not that it had the effect wanted.

classLocation.description: public (default): header in Public, .cpp in Private; private: both in Private. A module without those folders takes both files in its own folder.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

note.description: What the class needs before it can be used: a build, a restart, or nothing.

examples.title: Create a new C++ class in a project module, as the editor's New C++ Class does: a header and a .cpp from a parent class (Actor, Character, ActorComponent, Object ..., or None for a plain class), then the editor's own compile.

discovery.summary: Make a Widget Blueprint and fill it, or raise an editor notification, chosen by widgetOp. create makes a Widget Blueprint asset (name and savePath, default /Game/UI/Widgets, or widgetPath) from UserWidget or a subclass (widgetType). add_child adds a widget of childClass (TextBlock, Button, Image and so on) under parentName (default the root panel; PARENT_NOT_FOUND for a name that is no panel), named name, with text for one that shows text. show only raises an editor toast with message for duration seconds (default 4): it puts nothing on screen in the game. duration.description: Seconds the notification stays up (default 4, 0.5 to 60).

widgetOp.description: Which create widget variant to run; omit for 'create'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

discovery.summary: Change a SaveGame slot on disk: set saved properties and write it again (a missing slot is created from saveGameClass), or delete the slot.
whenToUse: Test runs left values in a save (a best score, unlocks) that must be put back.
A save must be seeded or removed to test a load, continue or first-run flow.
whenNotToUse: The slot only needs reading (use list_save_games).

saved.description: True when the slot was written.

discovery.summary: Enable or disable a plugin, or limit it to some build targets: targets ["Editor"] keeps an editor-only plugin out of the packaged game.

Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.

executableName.description: With executableName: the game target that is built and names the package.

targetFile.description: With executableName: the target file of that name.

targetCreated.description: With executableName: true when this call wrote that target file (it stays in the project).

uatResult.description: UAT's own result word once the task finished.

discovery.summary: Measure performance, chosen by control. benchmark samples every frame for duration seconds (default 10) and answers averageFps, frame times and game, render and GPU thread times; start and stop record a .uestats file under Saved/Profiling for Unreal Insights (no MCP action reads it); memory_report runs memreport (detailed: memreport -full) and answers the .memreport file it wrote (reportPath, reportIsNew); show_stats turns an on-screen stat overlay on or off. A minimized or unfocused editor is throttled and measures slow. To find what makes a frame slow, inspect get_stats with stats frame names the busiest thread and what in view weighs on it.
whenToUse: control=start: A named profiling capture must begin for CPU, GPU, memory, or thread analysis.
control=stop: A profiling capture started by start_profiling must be stopped.
control=benchmark: A timed benchmark must be executed and its metrics collected.
control=memory_report: A snapshot of engine memory usage must be generated.
control=show_stats: A specific stat category overlay must be shown or hidden.
whenNotToUse: control=stop: No profiling capture is running.
control=show_stats: Only the FPS counter is needed (use show_fps).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

duration.description: Seconds after which the capture stops by itself (default: runs until stop_profiling).

type.description: What to report: cpu (frame and thread times), gpu (GPU frame time) or all (default); another value is refused.

category.description: Stat category to display (e.g. Unit, GPU).

enabled.description: Show (true, default) or hide (false) the overlay.

control.description: Which profile performance variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

A minimized or unfocused editor is throttled and measures slow. To find what makes a frame slow, inspect get_stats with stats frame names the busiest thread and what in view weighs on it.

discovery.summary: Read the newest editor log lines (kept since editor start), filtered by text, category or minimum severity, or read the build (UnrealBuildTool), Live Coding or previous-run log instead; returns the lines and a match count.
whenToUse: A one-shot historical log read is needed: Live Coding or compile results, PIE warnings such as Accessed None, or the output of a console command that only logs (au.DumpActiveSounds).
whenNotToUse: New lines must be streamed as they arrive (use subscribe).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

lines.description: How many of the newest matching lines to return, oldest first (default 100, max 1000).

filter.description: Case-insensitive plain text (not a regex) a line must contain; separate alternatives with | to match any of them (LoadMap|Bringing World).

category.description: Only lines of this log category, e.g. LogBlueprintUserMessages. Editor source only; refused with the other sources.

minVerbosity.description: Least severe level to include (default log): error returns errors only, warning adds warnings, verbose returns everything. Editor source only; refused with the other sources.

source.description: editor (default): the editor log. build: the UnrealBuildTool log of the last compile, where the compiler errors behind "Live coding failed" go. livecoding: the Live Coding console log (patching and linking). previous: the log of the editor's previous run, e.g. why an editor that went away exited. Only filter and lines apply to build, livecoding and previous.

runsBack.description: With source previous: how many editor runs back to read (default 1, max 20). After a crash and one more restart, the crashed run is 2.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

lines.description: Matching lines as "[seconds since start] Category: Verbosity: message", oldest first.

matched.description: How many buffered lines matched; more than returned means the lines cap cut the oldest.

logFile.description: For build, livecoding and previous: the file read. A previous run's name carries its start time.

discovery.summary: Run automation tests and answer with each one's result (passed or not, its errors and warnings), or run UnrealBuildTool for a target.
whenToUse: kind=tests: The project automation tests must be executed and their results read.
kind=ubt: The project must be built via UnrealBuildTool.
whenNotToUse: kind=tests: A single ad-hoc console command is needed.
kind=tests: Play In Editor is running: the automation framework starts no test while a game runs (stop it first).
kind=ubt: Only a console command or CVar is needed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

filter.description: Run the tests whose full path contains this, ignoring case (System.Core.Math, Project.MyGame). Omitted, every test is a match, capped by maxTests. Functional tests (Project.Functional Tests.<map>.<test>) open their map in the editor.

maxTests.description: Run at most this many of the matching tests, in the order the editor lists them (default 50, at most 200); matched says how many there were.

timeoutSeconds.description: Stop a test still running after this many seconds and count it failed (default 60, at most 600).

kind.description: Which run build variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

tests.description: One row per test run: name (its full path), passed, durationSeconds, errorCount and errors, warningCount and warnings (the first 10 of each), and a note when it timed out or was not run.

matched.description: Tests matching the filter, run or not.

failed.description: Tests that failed or timed out.

notRun.description: Tests the framework did not start (another run or Play In Editor began meanwhile).

allPassed.description: True when at least one test ran and every test passed.

discovery.summary: Capture a screenshot as a PNG, returned inline (downscaled to fit 1600x900 unless resolution sets the box) and saved under Saved/Screenshots unless keepFile is false. mode editor_viewport, the default, shoots the level viewport; game_viewport the running game frame without its UMG widgets (path picks the folder; NO_VIEWPORT when no game runs); full_editor_window the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included (window picks another open window by index or title). returnBase64 false returns only the saved path, at full size.
whenToUse: A viewport or window screenshot must be captured, optionally as base64.
whenNotToUse: The camera must move first, or shaders finish compiling, in the same call (use control_editor.screenshot, which takes the same shots plus location, rotation and waitForShaders).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

filename.description: File name of the PNG (.png is added; a folder part is dropped). Default Screenshot_<unix time>.

mode.description: What to capture: editor_viewport (default, the level viewport), game_viewport (the running game frame without its UMG widgets) or full_editor_window (the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included).

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index (2, or "2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame; responses list the open windows under windows[].

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the PNG (e.g. "1280x720"), aspect ratio kept, never upscaled. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

path.description: game_viewport mode only: project-relative folder to write the PNG into (default Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor).

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

includeMetadata.description: true: echo metadata back in the reply (default false).

metadata.description: An object of your own, such as a label or a step number, returned under metadata when includeMetadata is true; the capture itself never reads it.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Capture a screenshot as a PNG, returned inline (downscaled to fit 1600x900 unless resolution sets the box) and saved under Saved/Screenshots unless keepFile is false. mode editor_viewport, the default, shoots the level viewport; game_viewport the running game frame without its UMG widgets (path picks the folder; NO_VIEWPORT when no game runs); full_editor_window the editor window as displayed, game UI and asset editors included (window picks another open window by index or title). returnBase64 false returns only the saved path, at full size.

The level the game or the editor opens first must change: section GameMapsSettings, key GameDefaultMap (the game and a packaged build) or EditorStartupMap (the editor), value the level as /Game/Maps/L_Main.L_Main.
whenNotToUse: The full settings document must be read (use get_project_settings).

section.description: Settings section: a settings class path such as /Script/EngineSettings.GameMapsSettings, its class name (GameMapsSettings), or a raw ini section in brackets ([SystemSettings]); a name that is none of these is refused.

value.description: Setting value.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

control=pause: Trace capture must be temporarily suspended.

whenToUse: control=subscribe: New editor log lines must be streamed as they arrive.
control=unsubscribe: A log subscription made with subscribe must end.
control=spawn_category: A Gameplay Debugger category (AI, BehaviorTree, EQS, Perception, ...) must show or hide in the in-game debugger.
whenNotToUse: control=subscribe: A one-shot historical log read is needed.
control=unsubscribe: No subscription is active.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

categoryName.description: Category name (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen only).
